cardSummary: Water-level tunnel into a lagoon on Bo Hòn. Included on many cruises; kayak extra on some boats. 30–50 minutes. Low tide can close the arch. Pair with Sửng Sốt or Ti Tốp if the route lists them.
whyGo: The bay’s most famous kayak hole, not a walking cave.

name: Hồ Động Tiên (Fairy Lake Cave)
keywords: Visit Hồ Động Tiên when your route includes it: a grotto-and-lake pocket used on some overnight itineraries, quieter than the Sửng Sốt queue.
about: Visit Hồ Động Tiên when your route includes it: a grotto-and-lake pocket used on some overnight itineraries, quieter than the Sửng Sốt queue.
hook: A cave mouth that opens onto a still “fairy” lake.
cardSummary: Fairy Lake Cave — confirm it is on your cruise sheet. 30–45 minutes. Pair with Mê Cung or Luồn. Not a city-shore walk.
whyGo: A lake-in-the-rock rather than a stadium cavern.

name: Soi Sim Island
keywords: Land on Soi Sim for a short sand strip and a ridge path with bay views.
about: Land on Soi Sim for a short sand strip and a ridge path with bay views. Some day boats use it when Ti Tốp is crowded or closed to extra landings.
hook: A small beach-and-ridge stop, often instead of or after Ti Tốp.
cardSummary: Small island beach and ridge. Cruise landing. 45–75 minutes. Pair with a cave stop. Do not book Soi Sim and Ti Tốp as two half-days — most boats pick one.
whyGo: A lighter island landing than the Ti Tốp stair queue.

name: Tuần Châu Island & Marina
keywords: Tuần Châu is a schist island on the southwest side of Quảng Ninh in Vietnam. Overview Covered by palm forests, Tuần Châu island has an area of 2.
typical hours Daylight; marina by cruise
about: Use Tuần Châu for marina check-in, the beach strip, and evening entertainment — a man-made resort island linked to Ha Long by a short causeway, not a wild karst.
hook: The causeway island where many overnight boats actually board.
cardSummary: Marina island west of Bãi Cháy. Free to enter; shows and beach clubs extra. 2–4 hours or embarkation only. Pair with Bãi Cháy. Confirm your boat’s pier — some still use Hon Gai or other ports.
wikiAnchor: Tuần Châu is a schist island on the southwest side of Quảng Ninh in Vietnam. Overview Covered by palm forests, Tuần Châu island has an area of 2. To the east and south are two man-made beaches with white sand. Tuần Châu Island is among the most touristic destinations in Hạ Long. Etymology In the feudal time, the royal army set up a guard station here to patrol and defend the borderland. The name of Tuần Châu is the combination of ‘linh tuan’ (the patrolman) and ‘tri chau’ (district chief). Location Tuần Châu is located in an important position at the entrance of the waterway system of Thăng Long, Bặch Đằng and Vân Ðồn. History The island has many archaeological sites pertaining to the ancient Hạ Long culture from 3,000 to 5,000 years ago.
whyGo: Where the cruise day often starts and ends, plus a usable town beach.

name: Cô Tô Island
keywords: Ferry to Cô Tô for a proper island stay: beaches, a small town, and open East Sea weather.
about: Ferry to Cô Tô for a proper island stay: beaches, a small town, and open East Sea weather. It is a Vân Đồn / Cô Tô trip, not a Ha Long junk landing.
hook: The far-east island district — beaches and a town, not a day cruise stop.
cardSummary: District island east of Bai Tu Long. Ferry from Cái Rồng / Vân Đồn. Overnight minimum. Do not stack with a Ha Long day cruise. Pair with Quan Lạn only if you have a week.
whyGo: When you want sand and a night ashore, not another karst cave.

name: Quan Lạn Island
keywords: Stay on Quan Lạn for Minh Châu / Quan Lạn beaches and a working island town.
about: Stay on Quan Lạn for Minh Châu / Quan Lạn beaches and a working island town. Access is by ferry from the Vân Đồn mainland, not from a Ha Long day boat.
hook: A long Bai Tu Long island with a fishing town and an empty east beach.
cardSummary: Bai Tu Long island stay. Ferry extra. One or two nights. Pair with Ngọc Vừng if boats connect. Not a cruise cave day.
whyGo: The inhabited island that still feels like a village, not a marina.

name: Ngọc Vừng Island
keywords: Reach Ngọc Vừng for a wide sand crescent and a small settlement.
about: Reach Ngọc Vừng for a wide sand crescent and a small settlement. Treat it as a Bai Tu Long overnight, not a Ha Long sightseeing hour.
hook: A crescent beach island in Bai Tu Long, quieter than Cát Bà town.
cardSummary: Bai Tu Long beach island. Ferry or tour boat. Overnight preferred. Pair with Quan Lạn. Cát Bà is a different archipelago — do not book both as one day.
whyGo: Beach first, karst second.

name: Mắt Rồng Island (Dragon Eye)
keywords: Pass Mắt Rồng by boat — a pierced limestone stack photographed as a “dragon eye.”
about: Pass Mắt Rồng by boat — a pierced limestone stack photographed as a “dragon eye.” There is usually no landing; the visit is the alignment.
hook: The islet whose hole reads as a dragon’s eye from the right angle.
cardSummary: Photo islet from the water. No ticket of its own. Ask the deck if it is on the route. Pair with Hòn Trống Mái. Do not hike it.
whyGo: A five-minute photo, if the skipper knows the angle.

name: Hòn Trống Mái (Fighting Cocks Islet)
keywords: Watch Hòn Trống Mái (Gà Chọi) from the deck: two limestone knobs that look like fighting cocks.
about: Watch Hòn Trống Mái (Gà Chọi) from the deck: two limestone knobs that look like fighting cocks. It is a no-landing icon on almost every inner-bay route.
hook: Two leaning rocks — the bay’s most printed silhouette.
cardSummary: Deck photo only. Free with any inner-bay cruise. 5–10 minutes. Pair with Hòn Đỉnh Hương and Hòn Con Cóc as you sail, not as separate tickets.
whyGo: The shape that sells the postcard.

name: Hòn Đỉnh Hương (Incense Burner Islet)
keywords: Pass Đỉnh Hương from the water — a solitary stack used in poems and postcards, often near the inner-bay approach rather than a landing.
about: Pass Đỉnh Hương from the water — a solitary stack used in poems and postcards, often near the inner-bay approach rather than a landing.
hook: A single pillar that reads as a giant incense burner in the channel.
cardSummary: Deck viewing. No separate ticket. Pair with Hòn Trống Mái. Not a hike.
whyGo: The incense-burner silhouette after the fighting cocks.

name: Hòn Con Cóc (Toad Islet)
keywords: Spot Hòn Con Cóc from the boat among the named “animal” islets.
about: Spot Hòn Con Cóc from the boat among the named “animal” islets. No landing; the pleasure is the resemblance and the surrounding channel.
hook: A squat karst that looks like a toad on the water.
cardSummary: Deck photo. Free on the cruise. Pair with Trống Mái and Đỉnh Hương. Do not expect a beach.
whyGo: Another of the bay’s story-shaped rocks.

name: Hòn Chó Đá (Stone Dog Islet)
keywords: Look for Hòn Chó Đá among the named islets — a stone-dog silhouette from one angle, easy to miss if you are below deck.
about: Look for Hòn Chó Đá among the named islets — a stone-dog silhouette from one angle, easy to miss if you are below deck.
hook: A low rock profile read as a dog watching the channel.
cardSummary: Deck viewing only. Pair with the other named islets. Not a stop you can book alone.
whyGo: The last of the famous animal rocks on a classic inner-bay run.

name: Cửa Vạn Floating Fishing Village
keywords: Visit Cửa Vạn by tender or rowboat: floating houses, a small cultural centre, and aquaculture.
about: Visit Cửa Vạn by tender or rowboat: floating houses, a small cultural centre, and aquaculture. Many families have been resettled on land; treat remaining homes as a working place, not a set.
hook: The best-known floating community — now a cultural stop more than a live town.
cardSummary: Floating village in a sheltered cove. Usually a Ha Long cruise tender. 45–75 minutes. Pair with Vung Viêng only if routes differ — do not pay for two “village” add-ons the same day. The Cat Ba cua-van-via-cat-ba card is this same cove; Cái Bèo is the Cát Bà harbour float. Ask before photographing people.
whyGo: The bay’s headline floating village, if your cruise still calls there.

name: Vung Viêng Floating Village
keywords: Pass or paddle Vung Viêng: fish pens, floating houses, and a less staged feel than the busiest Cửa Vạn calls — still a tourism stop, still someone’s workplace.
about: Pass or paddle Vung Viêng: fish pens, floating houses, and a less staged feel than the busiest Cửa Vạn calls — still a tourism stop, still someone’s workplace.
hook: A quieter floating hamlet used on some overnight and kayak routes.
cardSummary: Floating village on selected routes. Cruise or kayak. 40–70 minutes. Pair with Luồn. Do not book Cửa Vạn and Vung Viêng as two must-dos.
whyGo: When you want a village hour without the largest tender queues.

name: Ba Hàng Fishing Village
keywords: Call at Ba Hàng when the itinerary lists it: a compact floating community, less famous than Cửa Vạn, still part of the bay’s working aquaculture.
about: Call at Ba Hàng when the itinerary lists it: a compact floating community, less famous than Cửa Vạn, still part of the bay’s working aquaculture.
hook: A smaller fishing cluster — three “rows” of boats and pens.
cardSummary: Small floating village. Cruise dependent. 30–50 minutes. One village per day is enough. Ask before photos.
whyGo: A short village pass without the headline name.

name: Bãi Cháy Beach
keywords: Walk or swim Bãi Cháy: a man-made / nourished city beach facing the bay, handy after a cruise, not a remote island strand.
about: Walk or swim Bãi Cháy: a man-made / nourished city beach facing the bay, handy after a cruise, not a remote island strand.
hook: The city’s long urban beach under Sun World and the hotel strip.
cardSummary: City beach on the west shore. Free. Morning or late afternoon. Pair with the night market or Sun World. Water quality varies; this is not Ti Tốp.
whyGo: The only easy swim you can do from a Ha Long hotel without a boat.

name: Bãi Cháy Bridge
keywords: The Bãi Cháy Bridge (Vietnamese: Cầu Bãi Cháy) is a cable-stayed bridge on Highway 18, connecting Hồng Gai with Bãi Cháy over the Cửa Lục straits, separating Cửa Lục Bay with Hạ Long Bay, on the territory of Hạ Long city, Quảng Ninh province, Vietnam. It is the first, and at the
about: Cross or photograph Bãi Cháy Bridge (opened 2006): the city’s landmark crossing between the resort shore and the older Hòn Gai centre.
hook: The cable-stayed span linking Bãi Cháy to Hòn Gai across Cửa Lục.
cardSummary: City bridge. Free to cross by taxi or bus. 20–40 minutes as a viewpoint stop. Pair with Bài Thơ or the coastal road. Evening lights are the photo.
wikiAnchor: The Bãi Cháy Bridge (Vietnamese: Cầu Bãi Cháy) is a cable-stayed bridge on Highway 18, connecting Hồng Gai with Bãi Cháy over the Cửa Lục straits, separating Cửa Lục Bay with Hạ Long Bay, on the territory of Hạ Long city, Quảng Ninh province, Vietnam. It is the first, and at the time of its inauguration, the longest central-line cable-stayed bridge in Vietnam.
whyGo: The view that explains how the two halves of Ha Long City meet.

name: Bài Thơ Mountain (Poem Mountain)
keywords: Climb or ride up Núi Bài Thơ — the “poem mountain” facing the bay, named for verses associated with Lê Thánh Tông and later visitors.
about: Climb or ride up Núi Bài Thơ — the “poem mountain” facing the bay, named for verses associated with Lê Thánh Tông and later visitors. Lôi Âm Pagoda sits on the same massif.
hook: The limestone hill over Hòn Gai with a carved poem and a city view.
cardSummary: City karst hill on the Hòn Gai side. Entry may be ticketed for the viewpoint. 1–2 hours. Pair with Long Tiên and Lôi Âm. Steep; not a substitute for Ti Tốp.
whyGo: The land viewpoint that is not a cruise deck.

name: Quảng Ninh Museum & Library
keywords: Tour the Quảng Ninh Museum (with its library wing): a contemporary building presenting the province’s mining, seascape, and cultural history.
about: Tour the Quảng Ninh Museum (with its library wing): a contemporary building presenting the province’s mining, seascape, and cultural history. A land day when the bay is fogged in.
hook: A striking modern museum on the Bãi Cháy shore — coal, bay, and province.
cardSummary: Provincial museum on the west shore. Ticketed. 1.5–2.5 hours. Closed on some Mondays — check the door. Pair with the flower park or beach. Not a cave.
whyGo: The one museum that explains why this province is more than cruises.

name: Sun World Halong Complex
keywords: Buy the Sun World Ha Long campus ticket for Bãi Cháy hill — Queen Cable Car, Sun Wheel, Dragon Park, and Typhoon Water Park share one hillside.
about: Buy the Sun World Ha Long campus ticket for Bãi Cháy hill — Queen Cable Car, Sun Wheel, Dragon Park, and Typhoon Water Park share one hillside. Inner cards are the rides, not extra destinations.
hook: The Bãi Cháy hillside ticket: cable, wheel, Dragon Park, and water park.
cardSummary: Hillside amusement campus above Bãi Cháy. Combo tickets. Half to full day. Last cable down is earlier than the lights. The Queen Cable, Sun Wheel, Dragon Park, and Typhoon cards are stops on this same ticket — do not book four extra half-days.
whyGo: A full land afternoon when you are done with boats.

name: Queen Cable Car
keywords: Ride Cáp treo Nữ Hoàng as the main lift into Sun World — bay views on the way up, parks at the top.
about: Ride Cáp treo Nữ Hoàng as the main lift into Sun World — bay views on the way up, parks at the top. It is the access, not a separate mountain.
hook: The gondola from Bãi Cháy Beach up the Sun World hill.
cardSummary: Sun World gondola. Included in most campus tickets. 15–25 minutes each way. Last car down matters. Pair with the Sun Wheel on the same hill.
whyGo: The view ride that is the campus front door.

name: Sun Wheel Ha Long
keywords: Ride the Sun Wheel on the Sun World summit for a slow 360° of the city, bridge, and outer karsts.
about: Ride the Sun Wheel on the Sun World summit for a slow 360° of the city, bridge, and outer karsts. Best after dusk when the wheel is lit.
hook: The hilltop Ferris wheel over Bãi Cháy and the bay mouth.
cardSummary: Ferris wheel on the Sun World hill. Usually on the combo ticket. 15–20 minutes. Pair with Queen Cable. Do not treat as a separate day from Sun World.
whyGo: The land panorama that does not need a junk.

name: Dragon Park Ha Long
keywords: Dragon Park is the largest theme park in Southeast Asia located in Ha Long, Quang Ninh, Vietnam. It opened on January 25, 2017.
about: Spend the afternoon in Dragon Park on the same hill as the cable and wheel. Typhoon next door is the water park; this card is the dry rides.
hook: The dry-rides side of Sun World — coasters and family machines.
cardSummary: Amusement rides on the Sun World campus. Combo ticket. 2–4 hours. Pair with Typhoon only if you have a full day and a change of clothes. Same hill as the cable.
wikiAnchor: Dragon Park is the largest theme park in Southeast Asia located in Ha Long, Quang Ninh, Vietnam. It opened on January 25, 2017. The amusement park is part of a large resort complex known as Sun World Halong Complex that includes an aerial tramway called the Queen Cable Car, Sun Wheel — a large observation wheel, as well as gardens, restaurants, a shopping district and a family entertainment center with arcade games. The Typhoon water park opened in April 2017. The park was designed in 2015 by International Theme Park Services, Inc. (Cincinnati, Ohio) in collaboration with Wyatt Design Group and Hetzel Design, both based in California.
whyGo: If the group wants machines more than caves.

name: Typhoon Water Park
keywords: Swim Typhoon Water Park on the same campus ticket as Dragon Park.
about: Swim Typhoon Water Park on the same campus ticket as Dragon Park. Seasonal hours; bring a suit and expect local-holiday crowds.
hook: Slides and pools on the Sun World hillside — summer land day.
cardSummary: Water park on Sun World hill. Combo or add-on. 2–4 hours. Closed or short hours in cool months. Same ticket family as Dragon Park — one campus day.
whyGo: Heat relief when you are not boarding a junk.

name: Ha Long Market (Chợ Hạ Long 1)
keywords: Shop Chợ Hạ Long 1 on the older Hòn Gai side: a working city market, not the Bãi Cháy night-souvenir strip.
about: Shop Chợ Hạ Long 1 on the older Hòn Gai side: a working city market, not the Bãi Cháy night-souvenir strip.
hook: The Hòn Gai covered market — produce, seafood, and household aisles.
cardSummary: Day market in Hòn Gai. Free to enter. 45–75 minutes. Morning. Pair with Long Tiên or Bài Thơ. The Bãi Cháy night market is a different card.
whyGo: Breakfast and fruit the way the town actually shops.

name: Bãi Cháy Night Market
keywords: Wander the Bãi Cháy night market after the beach or Sun World — clothes, snacks, and bay souvenirs.
about: Wander the Bãi Cháy night market after the beach or Sun World — clothes, snacks, and bay souvenirs. Bargain lightly; this is not Chợ Hạ Long 1.
hook: Souvenir lanes and grilled snacks behind the Bãi Cháy hotel strip.
cardSummary: Night souvenir market on the west shore. Free. 1–2 hours after dusk. Pair with Bãi Cháy Beach. Day produce is the Hòn Gai market card.
whyGo: An easy evening when the boat has docked.

name: Hạ Long Flower Park
keywords: Walk Công viên hoa Hạ Long for seasonal beds, paths, and a calm hour between the museum and the beach.
about: Walk Công viên hoa Hạ Long for seasonal beds, paths, and a calm hour between the museum and the beach. It is a city park, not a botanical expedition.
hook: A landscaped flower park on the Bãi Cháy waterfront.
cardSummary: Waterfront flower park. Usually free. 45–75 minutes. Pair with Quảng Ninh Museum. Best when beds are in season; winter can look sparse.
whyGo: A free, flat pause on a land day.

name: 3D Funny Art Museum Ha Long
keywords: Pose in the 3D Funny Art Museum — painted rooms and photo illusions, usually on or near the Bãi Cháy / Sun World entertainment strip.
about: Pose in the 3D Funny Art Museum — painted rooms and photo illusions, usually on or near the Bãi Cháy / Sun World entertainment strip.
hook: Trick-eye rooms for a rainy or kid-heavy land hour.
cardSummary: Indoor 3D photo museum. Ticketed. 45–75 minutes. Pair with Sun World if you are already on the hill. Skip if you came only for karsts.
whyGo: A weather backup, not a cultural must.

name: Lôi Âm Pagoda
keywords: Climb to Chùa Lôi Âm on Núi Bài Thơ — a working pagoda with a city-and-bay lookout.
about: Climb to Chùa Lôi Âm on Núi Bài Thơ — a working pagoda with a city-and-bay lookout. Combine it with the poem-mountain walk rather than a second hike.
hook: The pagoda on Bài Thơ mountain above Hòn Gai.
cardSummary: Pagoda on Bài Thơ. Modest donation. 45–90 minutes with the hill. Pair with Bài Thơ Mountain and Long Tiên. Dress shoulders and knees.
whyGo: Temple and viewpoint on the same hill.

name: Long Tiên Pagoda
keywords: Visit Chùa Long Tiên in the old town — a late-Nguyễn / early-20th-century city pagoda, easier than the hill climb to Lôi Âm.
about: Visit Chùa Long Tiên in the old town — a late-Nguyễn / early-20th-century city pagoda, easier than the hill climb to Lôi Âm.
hook: Hòn Gai’s central pagoda at the foot of Bài Thơ.
cardSummary: City pagoda in Hòn Gai. Free; donation usual. 30–45 minutes. Pair with Chợ Hạ Long 1. Lôi Âm is the hill pagoda — not the same courtyard.
whyGo: The town temple you can do between market and bridge.

name: Cửa Ông Temple
keywords: Cửa Ông Temple (Vietnamese: Đền Cửa Ông) is located in Cửa Ông Ward, Cẩm Phả, Quảng Ninh province, Vietnam. This is a place of worship for Hưng Nhượng Đại Vương Trần Quốc Tảng, a famous figure during the Trần dynasty, and it is also the venue for the annual Cửa Ông Temple Festiva
about: Travel to Đền Cửa Ông to honor Trần Quốc Nghiễn (Hưng Nhượng Đại Vương) and the Trần-era coastal cult. It is a Cẩm Phả pilgrimage, not a Bãi Cháy stroll.
hook: A major coastal temple in Cẩm Phả, east of Ha Long City.
cardSummary: Temple in Cẩm Phả. Free; festival crowds in first lunar month. 1.5–2 hours plus the drive. Pair with the coastal road, not with a cruise morning. The city Trần Quốc Nghiễn temple is a different, smaller shrine.
wikiAnchor: Cửa Ông Temple (Vietnamese: Đền Cửa Ông) is located in Cửa Ông Ward, Cẩm Phả, Quảng Ninh province, Vietnam. This is a place of worship for Hưng Nhượng Đại Vương Trần Quốc Tảng, a famous figure during the Trần dynasty, and it is also the venue for the annual Cửa Ông Temple Festival. At the end of 2017, Cửa Ông Temple was classified by the government as a Special National Site.
whyGo: The province’s important sea temple, if you have a land half-day east.

name: Trần Quốc Nghiễn Temple
keywords: Stop at Đền Trần Quốc Nghiễn in Ha Long City — a local temple to the same figure honored at Cửa Ông, sitting along the waterfront road named for him.
about: Stop at Đền Trần Quốc Nghiễn in Ha Long City — a local temple to the same figure honored at Cửa Ông, sitting along the waterfront road named for him.
hook: The city shrine to the Trần prince who gives the coastal road its name.
cardSummary: City temple on the coastal road. Free. 20–40 minutes. Pair with Đường Bao Biển. Cửa Ông is the larger pilgrimage — do not book both unless you like Trần temples.
whyGo: A short sacred stop without the Cẩm Phả drive.

name: Hạ Long Coastal Road (Đường Bao Biển Trần Quốc Nghiễn)
keywords: Follow Đường Bao Biển Trần Quốc Nghiễn along the Hòn Gai / city waterfront: parks, sculptures, and open water toward the karsts.
about: Follow Đường Bao Biển Trần Quốc Nghiễn along the Hòn Gai / city waterfront: parks, sculptures, and open water toward the karsts. This is the land promenade, not a cruise.
hook: The bay-front boulevard — walk, cycle, or drive the city’s best land view.
cardSummary: Coastal boulevard. Free. 45–90 minutes on foot or by xe. Pair with Bãi Cháy Bridge and the Trần Quốc Nghiễn temple. Best at late light; midday is just traffic.
whyGo: Sunset without buying another boat ticket.

name: Trang An Boat Circuit
keywords: Choose a Trang An circuit for longer cave tunnels and quieter temple stops than Tam Coc.
about: Choose a Trang An circuit for longer cave tunnels and quieter temple stops than Tam Coc.
hook: UNESCO boat routes through caves and temple landings.
cardSummary: Row the UNESCO Trang An boat circuits through river caves, karst walls, and small temple landings. Slightly more structured than Tam Coc and excellent for half-day photography without motorcycle logistics.
whyGo: The more managed, cave-rich sibling to Tam Coc — often preferred for scenery variety.

name: Tam Coc Boat Ride
keywords: Take a traditional boat through Tam Coc’s paddies and low river caves.
about: Take a traditional boat through Tam Coc’s paddies and low river caves.
hook: Rice-field karsts and three caves on a classic rowboat route.
cardSummary: Glide through Tam Coc’s rice paddies and three low river caves on a traditional wooden boat. More village-edge and intimate than Trang An — go early to beat heat and overlapping boats.
whyGo: The original “inland Ha Long” experience — intimate and photogenic.

name: Van Long Nature Reserve
keywords: Row Van Long’s wetland reserve looking for birds and cliff reflections.
about: Row Van Long’s wetland reserve looking for birds and cliff reflections.
hook: Quiet wetland boats under limestone cliffs — fewer crowds than Tam Coc.
cardSummary: Drift through Van Long’s wetland reserve beneath sheer limestone cliffs — quieter and wilder than Tam Coc. Ideal when you want Ninh Binh scenery without peak-hour boat traffic.
whyGo: Hidden-gem Ninh Binh water scenery without the main tourist crush.

name: Bai Dinh Pagoda Complex
keywords: Explore massive halls, Arhat corridors, and panoramic temple grounds.
about: Explore massive halls, Arhat corridors, and panoramic temple grounds.
hook: Vietnam’s largest modern Buddhist complex near Trang An.
cardSummary: Visit Bai Dinh, one of Vietnam’s largest pagoda complexes — vast courtyards, long Arhat corridors, and hilltop views near Trang An. A cultural counterweight to Ninh Binh’s boat-focused days.
whyGo: Scale and spirituality after a morning of boats — optional electric carts help.

name: Thung Nham Bird Park
keywords: Ride the included wetland boat through Thung Nham’s bird garden, then walk caves and forest trails inside the Tràng An landscape.
about: Ride the included wetland boat through Thung Nham’s bird garden, then walk caves and forest trails inside the Tràng An landscape.
hook: Sunset boats through a valley of storks, five kilometres from Tam Cốc.
cardSummary: Ecotourism park in Hải Nham with a bird garden (dozens of species, late-afternoon roost), caves, and garden walks. Adult ticket about 150,000đ includes the boat and Bút Cave. Summer 07:00–18:00; winter 07:30–17:30. Cash at the gate.
whyGo: The same UNESCO karst as Tam Cốc, with birds instead of boat traffic.

name: Tuyệt Tình Cốc (Am Tiên Cave)
keywords: Walk from Hoa Lư’s Đinh temple into Am Tiên — the cliff-ringed valley nicknamed Tuyệt Tình Cốc — with a cave shrine (including the old Cổ Am worship space) and green water.
about: Walk from Hoa Lư’s Đinh temple into Am Tiên — the cliff-ringed valley nicknamed Tuyệt Tình Cốc — with a cave shrine (including the old Cổ Am worship space) and green water.
hook: A hidden lake-valley a few hundred metres behind the Đinh temple.
cardSummary: Secluded limestone valley and cave temple just behind Đền Đinh Tiên Hoàng. Usually included on the Hoa Lư ticket (~20,000đ). Hours follow the capital site, about 07:00–17:00. The Cổ Am shrine is inside this valley — not a second outing.
whyGo: The quietest landscape on the Hoa Lư ticket, if you walk past the temples.

name: Cúc Phương National Park
keywords: Cúc Phương National Park (Vietnamese: Vườn quốc gia Cúc Phương) is located in Ninh Bình Province, in Vietnam's Red River Delta. Cuc Phuong was Vietnam's first national park and is the country's largest nature reserve.
about: Spend a day in Cúc Phương for primary forest trails, caves, and the primate, turtle, and carnivore rescue centres in Nho Quan.
hook: Vietnam’s first national park — ancient forest and rescue centres.
cardSummary: Oldest national park in Vietnam (~120 km from Hanoi). Gate about 60,000đ; each rescue centre is extra (~50,000đ). Park roughly 06:00–18:00. Bring cash. Combine with the FOUR PAWS bear sanctuary on the Bái Đính road, not the same site.
wikiAnchor: Cúc Phương National Park (Vietnamese: Vườn quốc gia Cúc Phương) is located in Ninh Bình Province, in Vietnam's Red River Delta. Cuc Phuong was Vietnam's first national park and is the country's largest nature reserve. The park is one of the most important sites for biodiversity in Vietnam.
whyGo: A true wilderness day when the karst boats start to repeat.

name: Động Thiên Hà (Galaxy Cave)
keywords: Walk the dry hall of Thiên Hà, then board a boat through the water cave — stalactites and a quieter circuit than Tràng An’s main piers.
about: Walk the dry hall of Thiên Hà, then board a boat through the water cave — stalactites and a quieter circuit than Tràng An’s main piers.
hook: Dry chamber then a boat into a 700-metre cave under Tượng mountain.
cardSummary: Galaxy Cave: about 200 m dry, 500 m on water, southwest of Hoa Lư. Typical visit 07:00–17:00 with a combined walk-and-boat ticket. Bring a light layer — the water section is cool and drippy.
whyGo: Cave-first scenery without the Tam Cốc boat crush.

name: Động Tiên Cánh (Hang Tiên)
keywords: Visit Hang Tiên / Động Tiên Cánh, a limestone cave stop near Bích Động used on countryside walks rather than the main Ngo Đồng boat.
about: Visit Hang Tiên / Động Tiên Cánh, a limestone cave stop near Bích Động used on countryside walks rather than the main Ngo Đồng boat.
hook: The fairy cave on the Tam Cốc–Bích Động walking loop.
cardSummary: Compact cave in the Tam Cốc–Bích Động scenic area, often paired with Bích Động Pagoda on foot or by bicycle. Daylight hours; a small local fee may apply on top of the area ticket. Not a substitute for Tràng An’s long water caves.
whyGo: A short cave when you want karst without another two-hour row.

name: Bích Động Pagoda
keywords: Climb Hạ, Trung, and Thượng pagodas at Bích Động, with a dark cave between the middle and upper halls and rice-field views toward Tam Cốc.
about: Climb Hạ, Trung, and Thượng pagodas at Bích Động, with a dark cave between the middle and upper halls and rice-field views toward Tam Cốc.
hook: Three pagodas stacked in a mountain — “second cave of the southern sky.”
cardSummary: Mountain pagoda complex in Đam Khê: lower, middle, and upper halls plus Xuyên Thủy water cave nearby. Named Bích Động in the 18th century. Pair with Tam Cốc by bicycle; cover shoulders and knees. Typical hours 07:00–17:00.
whyGo: The sacred stop that actually sits in the karst, not a roadside megaplex.

name: Thái Vi Temple
keywords: Visit Thái Vi, a historic temple dedicated to Trần kings, set among paddies on the cycling loop from the Tam Cốc pier.
about: Visit Thái Vi, a historic temple dedicated to Trần kings, set among paddies on the cycling loop from the Tam Cốc pier.
hook: Trần-dynasty temple in the rice at the edge of Tam Cốc.
cardSummary: 13th-century temple to Trần rulers in the Tam Cốc–Bích Động area. Easy by bicycle from the boat pier; often combined with Cố Viên Lầu. Quiet, modest, and usually open ~07:00–17:30. Dress for an active shrine.
whyGo: History without leaving the village-and-karst landscape.

name: Hang Thiên Hương Temple
keywords: Enter Động Thiên Hương in the Tam Cốc–Bích Động complex: a high cave chamber holding the Linh Từ shrine to Trần Thị Dung.
about: Enter Động Thiên Hương in the Tam Cốc–Bích Động complex: a high cave chamber holding the Linh Từ shrine to Trần Thị Dung.
hook: A cave-bell shrine to Quốc mẫu Trần Thị Dung.
cardSummary: Cave temple about 60 m high in the Tam Cốc–Bích Động area, with a carved shrine to Trần Thị Dung. Daylight visit; often on walking or cycling loops after the boat. Distinct from Tràng An’s many cave landings.
whyGo: Cave and temple in one stop, without a two-hour boat.

name: Đền Trần (Đền Nội Lâm)
keywords: Visit Đền Trần in the Tràng An hills — rebuilt under Trần Thái Tông with famous carved stone columns — also called Đền Nội Lâm or Đền Nhất Lâm.
about: Visit Đền Trần in the Tràng An hills — rebuilt under Trần Thái Tông with famous carved stone columns — also called Đền Nội Lâm or Đền Nhất Lâm.
hook: Stone-column shrine to Quý Minh, south guardian of Hoa Lư.
cardSummary: Temple to water-guardian Quý Minh on the south gate of old Hoa Lư, inside today’s Tràng An scenic area. Often reached on a boat circuit. Đền Nhất Lâm / Nội Lâm is the same shrine — do not book it twice. Hours follow Tràng An boats, roughly 07:30–16:00.
whyGo: The temple landing people remember from a Tràng An boat, worth naming.

name: Chùa Bái Đính Cổ
keywords: Climb to old Bái Đính (1136, associated with Nguyễn Minh Không): Hang Sáng, Hang Tối, Cao Sơn shrine, and Ngọc well in the mountain.
about: Climb to old Bái Đính (1136, associated with Nguyễn Minh Không): Hang Sáng, Hang Tối, Cao Sơn shrine, and Ngọc well in the mountain.
hook: The original cave pagoda, 800 metres from the new megacomplex.
cardSummary: Historic cave pagoda on Bái Đính mountain, about 800 m from the 2003 “new” complex already on this list. Stone steps, dark and light caves, modest halls. Combine after the big courtyards if you still have legs; this is the quieter, older site.
whyGo: The thousand-year pagoda — the new halls next door are a different visit.

name: Phố Cổ Hoa Lư
keywords: Stroll Phố Cổ Hoa Lư, the landscaped pedestrian street and café strip near Kỳ Lân in today’s Hoa Lư city, separate from the Trường Yên temple precinct.
about: Stroll Phố Cổ Hoa Lư, the landscaped pedestrian street and café strip near Kỳ Lân in today’s Hoa Lư city, separate from the Trường Yên temple precinct.
hook: The new old-street quarter — not the tenth-century temples.
cardSummary: Contemporary “ancient street” in Hoa Lư city (Kỳ Lân area), with shophouses, lights, and snacks. Free to walk. This is not Cố đô Hoa Lư at Trường Yên. Go at dusk; the heritage temples close mid-afternoon.
whyGo: Evening food and photos after a temple morning — do not confuse the two Hoa Lưs.

name: Tombs of Đinh Tiên Hoàng & Lê Đại Hành
keywords: Climb toward Núi Mã Yên for the burial sites of Đinh Tiên Hoàng and Lê Đại Hành — the tombs, not the two courtyard temples already listed as Hoa Lư Ancient Capital.
about: Climb toward Núi Mã Yên for the burial sites of Đinh Tiên Hoàng and Lê Đại Hành — the tombs, not the two courtyard temples already listed as Hoa Lư Ancient Capital.
hook: The hill tombs behind the temples, often skipped on a rushed Hoa Lư stop.
cardSummary: Imperial tombs on/near Mã Yên hill in the Hoa Lư precinct. Same heritage zone and typical 07:00–17:30 ticket as the capital temples, but a separate walk. Do not add Đền Đinh or Đền Lê as extra cards — those temples are the existing Hoa Lư Ancient Capital visit.
whyGo: The actual graves, if the temple halls left you wanting the rest of the story.

name: Phát Diệm Stone Cathedral
keywords: Tour the Phát Diệm complex built 1875–1899 by Father Trần Lục: stone-and-ironwood nave, Phương Đình bell tower, side chapels, and carved Vietnamese motifs.
about: Tour the Phát Diệm complex built 1875–1899 by Father Trần Lục: stone-and-ironwood nave, Phương Đình bell tower, side chapels, and carved Vietnamese motifs.
hook: Pagoda roofs on a neo-Gothic stone cathedral in Kim Sơn.
cardSummary: Catholic cathedral in Phát Diệm town, Kim Sơn: Vietnamese temple roofs on European stone walls, 48 ironwood columns. Free to view with modest dress; avoid mass unless invited. About 30–40 km from Tam Cốc. Pair with Kim Sơn sedge village.
whyGo: The most unexpected building in the province — a half-day south of the karsts.

name: Kim Sơn Sedge Craft Village
keywords: Watch Kim Sơn artisans harvest and weave sedge (chiếu cói) in villages around the cathedral district.
about: Watch Kim Sơn artisans harvest and weave sedge (chiếu cói) in villages around the cathedral district.
hook: Sedge mats from the coastal fields south of Phát Diệm.
cardSummary: Traditional sedge-weaving villages in Kim Sơn district. Informal workshops, not a single ticket booth — ask before photographing. Combine with Phát Diệm Cathedral on a southern half-day. Daylight hours.
whyGo: A living craft stop on the same road as the stone church.

name: Ninh Vân Stone Carving Village
keywords: Walk Ninh Vân’s carving lanes in Hoa Lư — raw limestone to finished sculpture — a working village, not a museum.
about: Walk Ninh Vân’s carving lanes in Hoa Lư — raw limestone to finished sculpture — a working village, not a museum.
hook: The yards that cut the stone for temples and Bái Đính statues.
cardSummary: Stone-carving village in Hoa Lư city. Workshops are open in daylight; dust, noise, and forklifts are part of the visit. Ask before entering a yard. Easy to pair with Hoa Lư temples or Bái Đính.
whyGo: You see the craft behind every dragon and Buddha in the province.

name: Văn Lâm Lace Embroidery Village
keywords: Visit Văn Lâm in Ninh Hải, where families still embroider and teach short needlework sittings for visitors.
about: Visit Văn Lâm in Ninh Hải, where families still embroider and teach short needlework sittings for visitors.
hook: Needlework studios on the Tam Cốc–Bích Động road.
cardSummary: Embroidery village in Hoa Lư’s Ninh Hải commune. Some houses offer try-the-needle sessions — agree a price first. Daylight; shops stay open later. On the bicycle loop with Thái Vi and Cố Viên Lầu.
whyGo: A craft hour between the boat pier and Bích Động.

name: BEAR SANCTUARY Ninh Binh
keywords: Join a guided visit at the FOUR PAWS bear sanctuary on the Cúc Phương–Bái Đính road in Kỳ Phú, Nho Quan, where rescued bile-farm bears live in large enclosures.
about: Join a guided visit at the FOUR PAWS bear sanctuary on the Cúc Phương–Bái Đính road in Kỳ Phú, Nho Quan, where rescued bile-farm bears live in large enclosures.
hook: FOUR PAWS rescue centre — not a zoo show.
cardSummary: FOUR PAWS sanctuary with 40+ rescued bears on 5.5 ha. Open 09:00–17:00 daily except Tuesday. Guided tours; vegetarian café on site. On the Cúc Phương–Bái Đính road — pair with the national park or Bái Đính, not with a second “bear park.”
whyGo: The ethical wildlife stop in the province.

name: Cố Viên Lầu
keywords: Walk Cố Viên Lầu (Làng Việt Cổ): a cluster of 18th–20th-century houses moved from the Red River Delta, now a restaurant, lodge, and outdoor museum next to Tam Cốc.
about: Walk Cố Viên Lầu (Làng Việt Cổ): a cluster of 18th–20th-century houses moved from the Red River Delta, now a restaurant, lodge, and outdoor museum next to Tam Cốc.
hook: Relocated northern timber houses beside the Tam Cốc pier.
cardSummary: Open-air collection of traditional northern houses (~20,000 m²) by Tam Cốc wharf, added to the scenic area in 2008. Come for a meal and a house walk, not a ruined citadel. Pair with Thái Vi Temple on the same lane.
whyGo: Lunch with architecture, on the way to Thái Vi.

name: Cát Cát Village
keywords: Descend into Cat Cat for ethnic village paths, a waterfall, and handicraft shops.
about: Descend into Cat Cat for ethnic village paths, a waterfall, and handicraft shops.
hook: Waterfalls, Hmong craft stalls, and valley views below Sapa town.
cardSummary: Walk down into Cat Cat village for waterfall views, Hmong handicraft stalls, and terraced valley scenery just below Sapa town. A manageable cultural outing when you want mountains without an all-day trek.
whyGo: Easiest cultural half-day from Sapa without a full trek.

name: Sa Pa Town Market
keywords: Browse Sapa’s central market for local foods, fabrics, and people-watching.
about: Browse Sapa’s central market for local foods, fabrics, and people-watching.
hook: Highland produce, textiles, and morning mountain-town energy.
cardSummary: Browse Sapa’s town market for highland produce, textiles, and snacks between treks. A short local-life stop that fills a rainy morning or the hours before a Fansipan cable-car day.
whyGo: Local life between treks — compact and atmospheric in cool weather.

name: Hàm Rồng Mountain
keywords: Climb Hàm Rồng, the landscaped hill just above Sa Pa town — cloud yard, orchid gardens, and a rocky crest that looks back over Muong Hoa.
about: Climb Hàm Rồng, the landscaped hill just above Sa Pa town — cloud yard, orchid gardens, and a rocky crest that looks back over Muong Hoa.
hook: Orchid gardens and a stone “dragon jaw” above the church square.
cardSummary: Ham Rong Mountain Park above the stone church. Ticket about 100,000đ; typical 07:00–18:00. One to two hours of stairs and gardens. Pair with the square and lake, not with Fansipan the same morning. Cloud often sits on the crest after 10:00.
whyGo: The in-town mountain when you do not want a valley trek or a cable car.

name: Hoàng Liên National Park
keywords: Hoang Lien National Park (Vietnamese: Vườn quốc gia Hoàng Liên, also known as Hoàng Liên Sơn, Dãy Hoàng Liên) is a national park within Hoang Lien Son Range, in the districts of Sa Pa and Than Uyên of Lào Cai Province, and part of Phong Thổ District in Lai Châu Province in Northe
about: Enter Hoàng Liên National Park — the forest reserve around Sa Pa that covers Fansipan, Trạm Tôn, and the high trails. Wikipedia lists it as a national park on the Hoang Lien massif, not a single gate attraction.
hook: The protected Hoang Lien Son range that holds Fansipan and the cloud forest.
cardSummary: National park wrapping Sa Pa (Wikipedia: Hoàng Liên National Park). Park ticket at trailheads such as Trạm Tôn / Ô Quy Hồ, typically ~40,000–80,000đ; daylight. Full-day hiking, not a viewpoint stop. Fansipan’s cable sits inside this landscape but is a separate Sun World ticket.
wikiAnchor: Hoang Lien National Park (Vietnamese: Vườn quốc gia Hoàng Liên, also known as Hoàng Liên Sơn, Dãy Hoàng Liên) is a national park within Hoang Lien Son Range, in the districts of Sa Pa and Than Uyên of Lào Cai Province, and part of Phong Thổ District in Lai Châu Province in Northern Vietnam. Its area is 68,569 hectares (264. 75 sq mi) with terrain mostly between 1,000 and 3,000 meters above sea level. The national park was established according to the Decision number 90/2002/QĐ-TTg dated 12 July 2006 by the government of Vietnam. This decision turned the Nature Reserve into a National Park. Hoang Lien National Park is recognized as a part of ASEAN Heritage Parks and a Centre of Plant Diversity in the International Union for Conservation of Nature's (IUCN) Plant Conservation Program.
whyGo: The wilderness frame for every Sapa day, if you want forest rather than town stairs.

name: Ô Quy Hồ Pass
keywords: Ride Ô Quy Hồ (Trạm Tôn) Pass, the high saddle west of town where the road cuts the Hoang Lien crest, with cloud, hairpins, and the Rồng Mây glass walk at the top.
about: Ride Ô Quy Hồ (Trạm Tôn) Pass, the high saddle west of town where the road cuts the Hoang Lien crest, with cloud, hairpins, and the Rồng Mây glass walk at the top.
hook: Heaven’s Gate — the QL4D ridge between Sa Pa and Lai Châu.
cardSummary: Mountain pass on QL4D, about 15–18 km west of Sa Pa. Free to ride; viewpoints and the glass bridge are extra. 45 minutes each way. Combine with Silver Waterfall, Love Waterfall, or Rồng Mây. Weather closes views — go early.
whyGo: Sapa’s classic pass day, not another village ticket.

name: Mường Hoa Valley
keywords: Look over Mường Hoa, the valley that holds Sapa’s famous rice terraces, Giáy and Hmong villages, and the ancient rock field.
about: Look over Mường Hoa, the valley that holds Sapa’s famous rice terraces, Giáy and Hmong villages, and the ancient rock field. The existing Sapa trek walks this valley; this card is the landscape itself.
hook: The terrace amphitheatre below town — Lao Chải, Tả Van, and the stone carvings.
cardSummary: Terrace valley south-east of Sa Pa. Road viewpoints are free; village paths and the stone field have local tickets. Best at harvest (Sep–Oct) and planting (May–Jun). The full-day trek is the separate sapa-trek card — do not book both for the same morning.
whyGo: The view every postcard uses, without booking a guide if you only want the road viewpoints.

name: Sapa Ancient Stone Field
keywords: Walk Bãi đá cổ Sapa in the Muong Hoa floor — large stones incised with what researchers read as fields, tools, and figures, still unexplained in full.
about: Walk Bãi đá cổ Sapa in the Muong Hoa floor — large stones incised with what researchers read as fields, tools, and figures, still unexplained in full.
hook: Boulders in Mường Hoa carved with terraces, houses, and unknown signs.
cardSummary: Carved-stone field in Mường Hoa, usually reached via Hầu Thào / Tả Van roads. Small site ticket common (~30,000–50,000đ); daylight. 45 minutes on the stones. Pair with Tả Van, not with Fansipan. Paths are muddy in the rains.
whyGo: The valley’s archaeology, not another viewpoint café.

name: Séng Mỹ Tý Reservoir (Hồ Séo Mý Tỷ)
keywords: Ride past Tả Van to Hồ Séo Mý Tỷ (Séng / Séo Mỹ Tý), the 1,600 m hydro lake formed by the Séo Chong Hô dam, inside Hoàng Liên National Park.
about: Ride past Tả Van to Hồ Séo Mý Tỷ (Séng / Séo Mỹ Tý), the 1,600 m hydro lake formed by the Séo Chong Hô dam, inside Hoàng Liên National Park. Vietnamese sources call it the highest artificial lake in the country.
hook: Vietnam’s highest reservoir — a lake in the clouds above Tả Van.
cardSummary: High reservoir ~20 km from Sa Pa via Tả Van (completed road 2021). Free to view; boats and homestays extra. Half day with a motorbike or car. Inside the national park core. Combine with Tả Van, not with Ô Quy Hồ the same morning unless you start very early.
whyGo: A half-day that is not terraces and not the cable car.

name: Cốc San Cave & Waterfalls
keywords: Visit the Cốc San cave and waterfall cluster — a local outing west/south of town, wet rock, and short jungle paths rather than a Muong Hoa terrace walk.
about: Visit the Cốc San cave and waterfall cluster — a local outing west/south of town, wet rock, and short jungle paths rather than a Muong Hoa terrace walk.
hook: A cave-and-fall pocket on the Cốc San side of the range.
cardSummary: Cave and falls in the Cốc San area. Small local ticket common; daylight; 1.5–2.5 hours on site. Grip shoes. Needs a motorbike or xe ôm. Not the same as Fairy Cave on the Love Waterfall road.
whyGo: Water and stone when the famous falls on Ô Quy Hồ are socked in.

name: Fairy Cave
keywords: Step into Fairy Cave (Hang Tiên), the small cave usually paired with Love Waterfall or the Tả Phìn side — formations and a cool corridor, not a Phong Nha-scale cavern.
about: Step into Fairy Cave (Hang Tiên), the small cave usually paired with Love Waterfall or the Tả Phìn side — formations and a cool corridor, not a Phong Nha-scale cavern.
hook: Hang Tiên — a short limestone cave on the waterfall road.
cardSummary: Small cave on the Silver / Love Waterfall approach (sometimes ticketed with the falls). Typical park hours 07:00–17:00. Do not plan a separate half-day. Watch your head; paths are slick.
whyGo: Fifteen minutes of cave if you are already on the Ô Quy Hồ waterfall circuit.

name: Silver Waterfall (Thác Bạc)
keywords: Stop at Thác Bạc, the Silver Waterfall west of town — a tall roadside cascade with a short stair to the spray.
about: Stop at Thác Bạc, the Silver Waterfall west of town — a tall roadside cascade with a short stair to the spray. Often the first halt on the pass.
hook: A 100-metre white fall on the Ô Quy Hồ road.
cardSummary: Roadside waterfall on QL4D toward Ô Quy Hồ. Ticket about 20,000–40,000đ; ~07:00–17:30. Thirty to forty-five minutes. Combine with Love Waterfall and the pass. Stairs are wet; the view from the road is free-ish if you only photograph the drop.
whyGo: The easiest famous fall from Sa Pa, fifteen minutes from the square.

name: Love Waterfall (Thác Tình Yêu)
keywords: Walk in to Thác Tình Yêu — Love Waterfall — a broader cascade reached by a park path and sometimes a short tram, usually paired with Fairy Cave on the same ticket.
about: Walk in to Thác Tình Yêu — Love Waterfall — a broader cascade reached by a park path and sometimes a short tram, usually paired with Fairy Cave on the same ticket.
hook: A longer forest walk to a wider fall than Thác Bạc.
cardSummary: Forest waterfall west of Sa Pa, often bundled with Fairy Cave. Ticket about 70,000–100,000đ; 07:00–17:00. 60–90 minutes. Combine with Thác Bạc on the same road. Not a swim park — stay off wet rock.
whyGo: More of a walk than Silver Waterfall, if you want spray without the pass traffic.

name: Cat Cat Waterfall
keywords: Descend to Cat Cat Waterfall inside the village ticket — hydro flume, spray, and the photo bridge at the lowest point of the walk.
about: Descend to Cat Cat Waterfall inside the village ticket — hydro flume, spray, and the photo bridge at the lowest point of the walk. The village card covers the hamlet; this is the water.
hook: The fall at the bottom of the Cat Cat village stair.
cardSummary: Waterfall inside Cát Cát (same village ticket as cat-cat-village, typically ~75,000đ, 07:00–17:00). Steep return climb. Do not buy a second entrance. Pair with the village walk, not as a separate taxi trip.
whyGo: The reason people go all the way down instead of turning around at the first stall.

name: Cầu Mây
keywords: Walk Cầu Mây, Sapa’s timber cloud bridge — a short span used for terrace photographs when the fog sits in the valley.
about: Walk Cầu Mây, Sapa’s timber cloud bridge — a short span used for terrace photographs when the fog sits in the valley. Different from the Rồng Mây glass skywalk on Ô Quy Hồ.
hook: The wooden “cloud bridge” viewpoint — mist under the boards, valley below.
cardSummary: Wooden mist bridge on the Sa Pa / valley edge. Small ticket or garden fee common; daylight. Do not confuse with Rồng Mây Glass Skywalk. Pair with Hàm Rồng or a Muong Hoa viewpoint. Slippery when wet.
whyGo: A five-minute photograph if the cloud is in; skip if the glass bridge is already the plan.

name: Rồng Mây Glass Skywalk Bridge
keywords: Walk Cầu kính Rồng Mây, the glass skywalk and cliff complex at the top of Ô Quy Hồ Pass on the Lào Cai–Lai Châu line.
about: Walk Cầu kính Rồng Mây, the glass skywalk and cliff complex at the top of Ô Quy Hồ Pass on the Lào Cai–Lai Châu line. Opened 2019; the glass arm is about 60 m over the drop.
hook: A glass cliff walk at 2,200 m on Ô Quy Hồ — “dragon in the clouds.”
cardSummary: Glass skywalk ~16–18 km west of Sa Pa on QL4D. Ticket often 200,000–400,000đ depending on combo (bridge, coaster, zipline); typical 08:00–18:00. 1–2 hours. Combine with the pass and Silver Waterfall. Closed or socked in when the cloud is total — check the morning you go.
whyGo: The thrill stop on the pass, not a village morning.

name: Tả Van Village
keywords: Walk Tả Van, the Giáy (and Hmong) village at the far end of the classic Lao Chải–Tả Van terrace trek, with river, homestays, and a slower street than Cat Cat.
about: Walk Tả Van, the Giáy (and Hmong) village at the far end of the classic Lao Chải–Tả Van terrace trek, with river, homestays, and a slower street than Cat Cat.
hook: Giáy homestays on the floor of Mường Hoa.
cardSummary: Valley village ~8–10 km from Sa Pa. Paths are free once you are on the trek ticket or community fee; homestays extra. Half day or overnight. Pair with Lao Chải on the same walk. This is a living commune — ask before photographing people.
whyGo: The overnight village if you want the valley after dark.

name: Lao Chải Village
keywords: Descend into Lao Chải, the Hmong village on the near side of the Muong Hoa trek, with the widest terrace photographs from the road above.
about: Descend into Lao Chải, the Hmong village on the near side of the Muong Hoa trek, with the widest terrace photographs from the road above.
hook: Black Hmong houses on the first big terrace step of Mường Hoa.
cardSummary: Hmong village on the Mường Hoa trail. Community / trek fees apply on guided walks. 1–2 hours through the lanes. Combine with Tả Van the same day. Steep, muddy in rain. The sapa-trek card is the guided version of this path.
whyGo: The first village on the classic walk — skip Cat Cat if you only have one descent.

name: Tả Phìn Village
keywords: Visit Tả Phìn, the Red Dao village known for herbal baths, brocade, and the old French convent ruin — a different circuit from Mường Hoa.
about: Visit Tả Phìn, the Red Dao village known for herbal baths, brocade, and the old French convent ruin — a different circuit from Mường Hoa.
hook: Red Dao herbal baths and a ruined convent north of town.
cardSummary: Red Dao village ~10–12 km north of Sa Pa. Baths are priced per tub; village walk is a small fee or free. Half day. Do not stack Lao Chải the same afternoon. Ask before photographing costume.
whyGo: Dao culture and a soak, not another terrace selfie.

name: Ý Linh Hồ Village
keywords: Walk Ý Linh Hồ, a small Hmong village used as the gentle start of many day treks before Lao Chải.
about: Walk Ý Linh Hồ, a small Hmong village used as the gentle start of many day treks before Lao Chải.
hook: The first hamlet off the Cat Cat / Muong Hoa ridge — quieter terraces.
cardSummary: Small terrace village on the classic trek start. Free to pass on a guided walk; 45–75 minutes. Combine with Lao Chải–Tả Van. Not a separate taxi destination unless you only want a short look.
whyGo: A shorter descent than Cat Cat, with fewer stalls.

name: Sín Chải Village
keywords: Visit Sín Chải, a quieter Hmong settlement used as an alternative to the Cat Cat stair — forest edge, homestays, and fewer tour buses.
about: Visit Sín Chải, a quieter Hmong settlement used as an alternative to the Cat Cat stair — forest edge, homestays, and fewer tour buses.
hook: A Hmong village on the Fansipan / Cat Cat western shoulder.
cardSummary: Hmong village west of town toward the Fansipan slope. Daylight; small community fee possible. 1–2 hours. Pair with Hoàng Liên trails, not with Cat Cat the same morning.
whyGo: Village time without the Cat Cat gauntlet.

name: Bản Hồ Village
keywords: Reach Bản Hồ, the Tay (and Xa Pho) village down-valley from Tả Van, used for two-day treks and riverside homestays below the main terrace belt.
about: Reach Bản Hồ, the Tay (and Xa Pho) village down-valley from Tả Van, used for two-day treks and riverside homestays below the main terrace belt.
hook: A lower Tay village — river, bamboo, and a longer trek out of Mường Hoa.
cardSummary: Lower valley village ~15–18 km from Sa Pa. Best as a trek overnight, not a motorbike pop-in. Free to walk; homestay extra. Combine with Tả Van or Nậm Sài. Hotter and lower than town.
whyGo: The overnight that is not Tả Van, if you want river instead of the tourist floor.

name: Nậm Sài Village
keywords: Continue to Nậm Sài when a two-day trek drops below Bản Hồ — fewer guesthouses, more river agriculture, and a night that is not on the Tả Van circuit.
about: Continue to Nậm Sài when a two-day trek drops below Bản Hồ — fewer guesthouses, more river agriculture, and a night that is not on the Tả Van circuit.
hook: A farther Tay / Xa Pho hamlet past Bản Hồ.
cardSummary: Remote valley village beyond Bản Hồ. Trek or local motorbike; not a town taxi hop. Overnight is the point. Combine with Bản Hồ. Leave it off a two-night Sapa if you only have Cat Cat energy.
whyGo: Only if you already walked Bản Hồ and still want quieter water.

name: Sả Pả Village
keywords: Walk Sả Pả, the village-commune that still farms the slopes beside urban Sa Pa, with lanes that feel like a suburb of the hill station rather than a named trek.
about: Walk Sả Pả, the village-commune that still farms the slopes beside urban Sa Pa, with lanes that feel like a suburb of the hill station rather than a named trek.
hook: The old commune on the edge of town — terraces without a famous ticket booth.
cardSummary: Commune village beside Sa Pa town. Free; daylight; 45–90 minutes. Pair with the town market or Hầu Thảo. Easy to confuse with “Sa Pa” the town — this card is the farming hamlet.
whyGo: A short local loop when you do not want a 75,000đ village gate.

name: Hầu Thảo Village
keywords: Visit Hầu Thảo, a Hmong village on the Muong Hoa rim used as a quieter approach to the stone field and terrace viewpoints.
about: Visit Hầu Thảo, a Hmong village on the Muong Hoa rim used as a quieter approach to the stone field and terrace viewpoints.
hook: Hmong lanes toward the ancient stones and the valley rim.
cardSummary: Hmong village on the stone-field / valley-rim road. Free or small fee; 1–2 hours. Combine with the ancient stone field. Ask before entering yards.
whyGo: A village that is not on the Lao Chải conveyor belt.

name: Sa Pa Stone Church
keywords: Stand at Nhà thờ đá Sa Pa, the granite church the French hill station built in the 1930s — still the town’s orientation point and Saturday love-market backdrop.
about: Stand at Nhà thờ đá Sa Pa, the granite church the French hill station built in the 1930s — still the town’s orientation point and Saturday love-market backdrop.
hook: The 1930s stone parish church that still faces the square.
cardSummary: Stone church on the central square. Free from the yard; mass times for the interior. Always visible. Pair with the square and lake. Cover shoulders if you go in. Evening lights are the photograph.
whyGo: Five minutes that tells you Sa Pa was a colonial hill town before it was a trek brand.

name: Sa Pa Center Square
keywords: Use Quảng trường Sa Pa as the town hinge — vendors, the church façade, and the steps down toward the lake.
about: Use Quảng trường Sa Pa as the town hinge — vendors, the church façade, and the steps down toward the lake. Weekend evenings still carry the love-market crowd.
hook: The pedestrian square between church, lake stairs, and weekend love market.
cardSummary: Central square, free, liveliest after 17:00 and on Saturday night. Pair with the church, lake, and Sun Plaza. Watch bags in the crowd. This is not a trek start — it is the hill-station living room.
whyGo: Orientation, not a ticket. Every other town sight is a two-minute walk.

name: Sa Pa Lake
keywords: Walk Hồ Sa Pa, the town lake below the church — a short circuit, cafés, and the first cool-air stroll after the night bus.
about: Walk Hồ Sa Pa, the town lake below the church — a short circuit, cafés, and the first cool-air stroll after the night bus.
hook: The small hill-station lake under the square — fog, pedal boats, and a loop path.
cardSummary: Town lake, free to walk; boats extra. 20–40 minutes. Pair with the square and church. Not a highland wilderness lake — that is Séo Mý Tỷ. Pretty in mist, ordinary in hard sun.
whyGo: Recovery legs before a valley day.

name: Kim Sơn Bảo Thắng Temple
keywords: Visit Kim Sơn Bảo Thắng, the monumental temple on the Sun World Fansipan complex — the same cable ticket as the peak, not a town pagoda.
about: Visit Kim Sơn Bảo Thắng, the monumental temple on the Sun World Fansipan complex — the same cable ticket as the peak, not a town pagoda.
hook: The great temple hall on the Fansipan Legend summit terrace.
cardSummary: Summit-complex temple on the Fansipan Legend ticket (same as fansipan, typically 07:30–16:30). Altitude stairs. Cover shoulders. Do not add a second Sun World ticket. Pair with Bích Vân Thiền Tự and the Grand Buddha on the same visit.
whyGo: The spiritual set-piece of the cable day, before or after the Buddha.

name: Bích Vân Thiền Tự Temple
keywords: Walk Bích Vân Thiền Tự, the zen temple cluster on the Fansipan Legend summit — incense, courtyards, and cloud, included on the cable ticket.
about: Walk Bích Vân Thiền Tự, the zen temple cluster on the Fansipan Legend summit — incense, courtyards, and cloud, included on the cable ticket.
hook: The zen monastery halls on the Fansipan terrace.
cardSummary: Zen temple on the same Sun World Fansipan ticket as the mountain. Typical cable hours 07:30–16:30. 20–30 minutes. Modest dress. Last cable down is earlier than the posted close — watch the clock.
whyGo: Quieter than the Buddha platform if the queue is long.

name: Grand Buddha Statue of Fansipan
keywords: Stand at the Grand Buddha on the Fansipan summit complex — a monumental Amitabha above the temple terraces, reached by cable, funicular, and stairs.
about: Stand at the Grand Buddha on the Fansipan summit complex — a monumental Amitabha above the temple terraces, reached by cable, funicular, and stairs.
hook: The giant Amitabha on the roof of Indochina.
cardSummary: Summit Buddha on the Fansipan Legend ticket (same as fansipan). Thin air and stairs. 15–25 minutes at the statue. Morning cloud can hide it entirely — that is normal. Not a separate entrance.
whyGo: The photograph people mean when they say they “did Fansipan” without the last scramble.

name: Sapa Museum
keywords: Visit the Sa Pa Museum for textiles, tools, and a short history of the hill station and the Hmong, Dao, Giáy, and Tay communities around it.
about: Visit the Sa Pa Museum for textiles, tools, and a short history of the hill station and the Hmong, Dao, Giáy, and Tay communities around it.
hook: A compact highland-culture museum in town.
cardSummary: Small town museum near the centre. Modest ticket (~20,000–30,000đ); typical 07:30–17:00. Rainy-morning stop. Pair with the town market. English labels vary.
whyGo: Forty minutes of context before you walk into someone’s village.

name: Sun Plaza Sapa
keywords: Walk Sun Plaza Sa Pa — the stone arcade, shops, and valley-station end of the Fansipan Legend system in the town centre.
typical hours Shops ~08:00 – 21:00; cable desk earlier
about: Walk Sun Plaza Sa Pa — the stone arcade, shops, and valley-station end of the Fansipan Legend system in the town centre.
hook: The French-style arcade and cable-station plaza in town.
cardSummary: Town plaza and Fansipan Legend valley station. Free to walk; cable tickets sold here. Pair with the square. This is not a second Fansipan card — the mountain ride stays on fansipan.
whyGo: Where you buy the cable ticket and get out of the rain.

name: Bắc Hà Market
keywords: Time a Sunday for Chợ Bắc Hà, the large ethnic market in Bắc Hà town, about 80 km east of Sa Pa — textiles, livestock, and the week’s social hour for the plateau.
about: Time a Sunday for Chợ Bắc Hà, the large ethnic market in Bắc Hà town, about 80 km east of Sa Pa — textiles, livestock, and the week’s social hour for the plateau.
hook: Sunday highland market — Flower Hmong, ponies, and a long drive.
cardSummary: Sunday market in Bắc Hà (other days are ordinary town). 2.5–3.5 hours each way from Sa Pa. Arrive 07:30–08:30. Full day. Not the Sa Pa town market card. Combine with Cán Cấu on Saturday only if you have two nights and a driver.
hours: Sunday morning is the point; pack down by early afternoon
whyGo: The market people mean when they say “Sapa market” and then leave town.

name: Cốc Ly Market
keywords: Go on Tuesday to Chợ Cốc Ly on the Chảy River in Bắc Hà district — a working upland market that still loads goods by boat.
about: Go on Tuesday to Chợ Cốc Ly on the Chảy River in Bắc Hà district — a working upland market that still loads goods by boat.
hook: Tuesday riverside market — boats, buffalo, and fewer tour buses than Bắc Hà.
cardSummary: Tuesday market, ~70–90 km from Sa Pa. Full day with a car. Morning only. Combine with a Chảy River boat if offered. Different day from Bắc Hà and Cán Cấu — pick one market per trip unless you have a week.
whyGo: The midweek market if Sunday Bắc Hà is too staged for you.

name: Cán Cấu Market
keywords: Visit Chợ Cán Cấu on Saturday — a high, colourful market in Bắc Hà district that many travellers use as a quieter alternative to Sunday Bắc Hà.
about: Visit Chợ Cán Cấu on Saturday — a high, colourful market in Bắc Hà district that many travellers use as a quieter alternative to Sunday Bắc Hà.
hook: Saturday Flower Hmong market closer to the Chinese border.
cardSummary: Saturday market, long drive from Sa Pa (often 3 hours). Morning. Full day. Do not book Bắc Hà the next morning unless you enjoy two 6-hour road days. Ask before close portraits.
whyGo: Saturday colour if you cannot stay for Sunday.

name: Mường Hum Market
keywords: Drive to Chợ Mường Hum in Bát Xát on Sunday for a highland market on the other road from Bắc Hà — different valley, different dress, same “come early” rule.
about: Drive to Chợ Mường Hum in Bát Xát on Sunday for a highland market on the other road from Bắc Hà — different valley, different dress, same “come early” rule.
hook: Sunday market in Bát Xát — west of Sa Pa, not the Bắc Hà plateau.
cardSummary: Sunday market west of Sa Pa in Bát Xát. Full day. Do not try to do Bắc Hà the same Sunday. Morning only. Local food stalls, not a craft mall.
whyGo: If you already did Bắc Hà, or if you are heading toward Lai Châu.

name: Cao Sơn Market
keywords: Reach Chợ Cao Sơn on Wednesday in Mường Khương district, often via Bảo Nhai and the Chảy River — a remote Flower Hmong market that rewards a dedicated car day.
about: Reach Chợ Cao Sơn on Wednesday in Mường Khương district, often via Bảo Nhai and the Chảy River — a remote Flower Hmong market that rewards a dedicated car day.
hook: Wednesday upland market in Mường Khương — the farthest of the set.
cardSummary: Wednesday market, 100–120 km-class outing from Sa Pa. Morning. Full day with a driver. Confirm the week’s date locally — highland markets shift around holidays. Not a substitute for Bắc Hà if you only have one market day.
whyGo: Only if you collect markets; skip it on a two-night Sapa.

name: Sao Beach (Bãi Sao)
keywords: Spend a lazy stretch at Bai Sao — clear shallows, beach restaurants, and soft sand.
about: Spend a lazy stretch at Bai Sao — clear shallows, beach restaurants, and soft sand.
hook: Powder sand and turquoise water on Phu Quoc’s southeast coast.
cardSummary: Settle into Bai Sao’s pale sand and clear turquoise shallows on Phu Quoc’s southeast coast. Bring shade and go earlier on weekends — it is the island’s most loved classic beach day.
whyGo: Often called the island’s prettiest classic beach day.

name: Dương Đông Night Market
keywords: Wander Duong Dong’s night market for grilled seafood and casual shopping.
about: Wander Duong Dong’s night market for grilled seafood and casual shopping.
hook: Seafood grills, souvenirs, and island evening buzz.
cardSummary: Wander Duong Dong night market for grilled seafood, fruit shakes, and souvenir stalls after a beach day. Lively, informal, and the island’s default evening social scene.
whyGo: Phu Quoc’s easiest evening plan after a beach day.

name: Dinh Cậu Shrine (Dinh Cậu Rock)
keywords: Visit the coastal shrine and watch the sun drop over the Gulf of Thailand.
about: Visit the coastal shrine and watch the sun drop over the Gulf of Thailand.
hook: Sea temple and rocky outcrop for Duong Dong sunsets.
cardSummary: Visit Dinh Cau’s seaside temple and rocky lookout for Duong Dong sunsets over the Gulf of Thailand. Free, central, and easy to combine with the night market afterward.
whyGo: Compact spiritual stop plus a reliable sunset viewpoint in town.

name: Starfish Beach (Rạch Vẹm)
keywords: Wade Rạch Vẹm’s clear shallows — the “starfish beach” on the north-west — and leave the animals in the water.
about: Wade Rạch Vẹm’s clear shallows — the “starfish beach” on the north-west — and leave the animals in the water. Boats and a dirt approach keep it rougher than Bãi Sao.
hook: Shallow north-coast flats where starfish sit in the sand.
cardSummary: North-coast sand flats near Rạch Vẹm. Free beach; boat extra. Daylight. Do not lift starfish. Combine with Gành Dầu, not with Bãi Sao the same morning. Access can be rough after rain.
whyGo: The island’s most photographed north-coast stop, if you treat the starfish as wildlife.

name: Long Beach (Bãi Trường)
keywords: Use Bãi Trường for the convenient west-facing hotel beach south of Dương Đông.
about: Use Bãi Trường for the convenient west-facing hotel beach south of Dương Đông. The existing sunset card is the evening ritual on this coast; this card is the beach itself.
hook: The 20 km west-coast hotel strip — sunset chairs, not powder like Bãi Sao.
cardSummary: West-coast resort beach from Dương Đông toward the south. Free public stretches; lounge chairs extra. Anytime. Pair with Dinh Cậu and the night market. The phu-quoc-sunset card is golden hour on this same shore — do not book both as separate half-days.
whyGo: Where most visitors actually swim between dinners.

name: Khem Beach (Bãi Khem)
keywords: Swim Bãi Khem, the neighbouring south-east beach to Sao — similar water, more hotel frontage, slightly fewer day-trip crowds on the public bits.
about: Swim Bãi Khem, the neighbouring south-east beach to Sao — similar water, more hotel frontage, slightly fewer day-trip crowds on the public bits.
hook: A pale south-east crescent next to Bãi Sao, more resort, still turquoise.
cardSummary: South-east beach beside Bãi Sao. Free public sand; resorts extra. Daylight. Combine with Sao or Hòn Thơm, not with the north-coast starfish run. Shade yourself — little natural tree cover on some stretches.
whyGo: Sao’s quieter sibling if the parking lot at Bãi Sao is full.

name: Ông Lang Beach
keywords: Spend time at Ông Lang — a broken west-coast beach of rocks, small bays, and quieter hotels than Bãi Trường.
about: Spend time at Ông Lang — a broken west-coast beach of rocks, small bays, and quieter hotels than Bãi Trường.
hook: Boulder coves and smaller resorts north of Dương Đông.
cardSummary: West-coast cove beach north of town. Free; cafés extra. Afternoon into sunset. Pair with Cửa Cạn or Vũng Bầu if you are already heading north. Not a long swimming strip — pick a cove.
whyGo: Sunset without the Long Beach chair rows.

name: Gành Dầu Beach
keywords: Stop at Gành Dầu’s working beach: boats, casuarinas, and a view toward the Cambodian coast.
about: Stop at Gành Dầu’s working beach: boats, casuarinas, and a view toward the Cambodian coast. The cape lookout is a separate card a few minutes up.
hook: The north-west fishing beach under the cape — Cambodia on a clear day.
cardSummary: North-west village beach. Free; seafood extra. Daylight. Combine with Gành Dầu Cape and Rạch Vẹm. Do not expect Bãi Sao water. Wind can be sharp in the wet months.
whyGo: Local north-west sand, not a resort brochure.

name: Vũng Bầu Beach
keywords: Walk Vũng Bầu — a wide, quieter west-facing beach that still has space between resorts.
about: Walk Vũng Bầu — a wide, quieter west-facing beach that still has space between resorts.
hook: A long, less-built north-west bay between Ông Lang and Gành Dầu.
cardSummary: North-west bay beach. Free; few services on some stretches. Daylight. Pair with Ông Lang or Gành Dầu. Bring water. Good shoulder-season alternative to Bãi Sao’s weekend crush.
whyGo: Room to swim when Long Beach feels like a road.

name: Cửa Cạn Beach
keywords: Use Cửa Cạn Beach for a west-coast swim next to the estuary and village — less polished than Ông Lang, more working boats.
about: Use Cửa Cạn Beach for a west-coast swim next to the estuary and village — less polished than Ông Lang, more working boats.
hook: River-mouth sand by the fishing village of the same name.
cardSummary: West-coast beach at the Cửa Cạn river mouth. Free. Pair with Cửa Cạn Fishing Village (the lanes, not a second beach). Sunset is possible; the village card is the food and boats.
whyGo: Beach plus village in one stop if you are already north of town.

name: Thom Beach (Bãi Thơm)
keywords: Ride out to Bãi Thơm on the north-east — long, quieter sand with park forest behind it, not the south-east turquoise of Sao.
about: Ride out to Bãi Thơm on the north-east — long, quieter sand with park forest behind it, not the south-east turquoise of Sao.
hook: A remote north-east strand under the national park.
cardSummary: North-east beach at the park edge. Free; few services. Half day with a motorbike. Combine with Phú Quốc National Park. Not Hòn Thơm island — different place, different coast.
whyGo: The far-north beach day when you want empty sand more than resorts.

name: Hòn Thơm Island (Pineapple Island)
keywords: Ride to Hòn Thơm (Pineapple Island) on the record over-sea cable or a boat.
about: Ride to Hòn Thơm (Pineapple Island) on the record over-sea cable or a boat. The island holds beaches and the VinWonders campus; the cable station and Kiss Bridge sit at Sunset Town on the Phú Quốc side.
hook: The cable-car island — beaches, VinWonders, and the south-end playground.
cardSummary: Southern island reached by cable (Sunset Town) or boat. Cable/park tickets are the cost; beach bits vary. Half to full day. Wikipedia-class islet in the An Thới group. Pair with the cable-station card only if you need the station as a meeting pin — the ride is this visit.
whyGo: The south-end island day, not another west-coast chair.

name: Hòn Mây Rút Island
keywords: Land on Hòn Mây Rút (often split North/South) on an An Thới boat day — the default reef-and-beach stop for snorkel tours.
about: Land on Hòn Mây Rút (often split North/South) on an An Thới boat day — the default reef-and-beach stop for snorkel tours.
hook: A classic An Thới snorkel stop — two islets, coral, and a lunch beach.
cardSummary: An Thới islet pair, reached by boat. Usually bundled on the phu-quoc-snorkel activity (~$40–60). Do not book a second private boat for the same reefs. Dry season (Nov–Mar) is clearer water.
whyGo: The island people mean when they book “Phu Quoc snorkel.”

name: Hòn Móng Tay Island (Fingernail Island)
keywords: Stop at Hòn Móng Tay, a small sand-and-coral islet in the An Thới chain, usually on the same boat as Mây Rút.
about: Stop at Hòn Móng Tay, a small sand-and-coral islet in the An Thới chain, usually on the same boat as Mây Rút.
hook: A tiny An Thới fingernail of sand — often a second snorkel hop.
cardSummary: Tiny An Thới islet. Boat-tour stop, not a stay. Same outing as Hòn Mây Rút and the snorkel activity. Fifteen to forty minutes in the water if the skipper stops.
whyGo: A named pin for the second reef, not a separate day.

name: Hòn Gầm Ghì Island
keywords: Snorkel Hòn Gầm Ghì when the boat skips the busiest sandbars — more rock, sometimes better fish, less beach time.
visit length 30–50 min on a boat day
about: Snorkel Hòn Gầm Ghì when the boat skips the busiest sandbars — more rock, sometimes better fish, less beach time.
hook: A rockier An Thới stop — deeper water, fewer picnic tables.
cardSummary: An Thới rock island on many snorkel loops. Same ticket as the boat day. Not a resort island. Confirm the itinerary; some cheap tours never land here.
whyGo: The third An Thới name if you care which reef you actually enter.

name: An Thới Archipelago
keywords: Treat the An Thới islands as one seascape: the boat-day reefs plus Hòn Thơm’s cable island.
about: Treat the An Thới islands as one seascape: the boat-day reefs plus Hòn Thơm’s cable island. The hidden snorkel activity is the typical way to see several in one morning.
hook: The southern island cluster — Hòn Thơm, Mây Rút, Móng Tay, Gầm Ghì.
cardSummary: Island group off An Thới. Wikipedia lists the southern islets as a cluster. Boat day or cable to Hòn Thơm. This card is the archipelago overview; individual islands are listed separately. Dry season water is the point.
whyGo: The map for the south, so you do not book four island days.

name: Phú Quốc National Park
keywords: Phú Quốc National Park (Vietnamese: Vườn quốc gia Phú Quốc) is a national park on Phú Quốc Island, in the Kiên Giang Province of Vietnam's Mekong Delta Region. The park covers approximately 70% of the island.
about: Enter Phú Quốc National Park for forest roads, capes, and quiet north beaches. Wikipedia: a national park covering much of the island’s north, not a single gated zoo.
hook: The forested north — half the island is still park.
cardSummary: Northern forest reserve. Some roads free; trailheads may collect a small fee. Half to full day by motorbike. Combine with Bãi Thơm or Gành Dầu. This is not Vinpearl Safari — different fence, different ticket.
wikiAnchor: Phú Quốc National Park (Vietnamese: Vườn quốc gia Phú Quốc) is a national park on Phú Quốc Island, in the Kiên Giang Province of Vietnam's Mekong Delta Region. The park covers approximately 70% of the island. This park includes land and sea area, protecting oceanic species such as dugong. This park was established by the Decision 91/2001/QĐ-TTg dated 8 June 2001 signed by the Prime Minister of Vietnam on upgrading Northern Phú Quốc Islands Preservation Zone to Phu Quoc National Park.
whyGo: The wild half after the south-end parks.

name: Suối Tranh Waterfall
keywords: Walk Suối Tranh, Phú Quốc’s most visited waterfall: ticketed path, pools, and a trickle in the dry months.
about: Walk Suối Tranh, Phú Quốc’s most visited waterfall: ticketed path, pools, and a trickle in the dry months.
hook: The easy inland fall — a short forest walk and a swimming hole after rain.
cardSummary: Inland waterfall, small ticket (~10,000–30,000đ); ~07:00–17:00. 45–90 minutes. Best after rain; disappointing in peak dry season. Pair with Suối Đá Bàn or a pepper farm, not with a snorkel boat.
whyGo: A non-beach morning in the island’s middle.

name: Suối Đá Bàn Waterfall
keywords: Follow Suối Đá Bàn’s boulder stream for swimming holes and a longer walk than Tranh.
about: Follow Suối Đá Bàn’s boulder stream for swimming holes and a longer walk than Tranh.
hook: A rockier stream walk — more scramble, fewer tour buses than Suối Tranh.
cardSummary: Rocky stream/fall inland. Small ticket; daylight; 1–2 hours. Grip shoes. Pair with Suối Tranh only if you want two water mornings. Dry-season flow is low.
whyGo: The inland alternative if Tranh is a queue.

name: Gành Dầu Cape
keywords: Stand at Mũi Gành Dầu, the cape lookout above the fishing beach — the geographic full-stop of the north-west road.
about: Stand at Mũi Gành Dầu, the cape lookout above the fishing beach — the geographic full-stop of the north-west road.
hook: The island’s north-west tip — wind, rocks, Cambodia on the horizon.
cardSummary: North-west cape viewpoint. Free; daylight. 20–40 minutes. Combine with Gành Dầu Beach and Rạch Vẹm. Wind and sun — no shade. Different from Dinh Cậu’s town rock.
whyGo: The view, not the swim. The beach card is down below.

name: Hộ Quốc Pagoda (Trúc Lâm Hộ Quốc)
keywords: Walk Thiền viện Trúc Lâm Hộ Quốc, the large coastal pagoda south of Dương Đông — courtyards, ocean, and a monument-scale Buddha.
about: Walk Thiền viện Trúc Lâm Hộ Quốc, the large coastal pagoda south of Dương Đông — courtyards, ocean, and a monument-scale Buddha.
hook: A seaside zen campus — white halls and a giant Buddha on the south-west shore.
cardSummary: Coastal zen monastery, free; typical 07:00–18:00. 45–75 minutes. Modest dress. Pair with Long Beach or the prison museum to the south. Not a theme-park ticket.
whyGo: The island’s strongest temple stop, and a sunset alternative to Dinh Cậu.

name: Sùng Hưng Pagoda
keywords: Visit Chùa Sùng Hưng, a historic Phú Quốc pagoda inland from Dương Đông, with a working monastic feel and fewer tour groups.
about: Visit Chùa Sùng Hưng, a historic Phú Quốc pagoda inland from Dương Đông, with a working monastic feel and fewer tour groups.
hook: An older island pagoda in the hills — quieter than Hộ Quốc.
cardSummary: Hill pagoda, free; typical 07:00–17:00. 30–45 minutes. Modest dress. Pair with Suối Tranh or a pepper farm. Not the coastal Hộ Quốc complex.
whyGo: A local shrine morning if the seaside campus is too grand.

name: Sư Muôn Pagoda (Chùa Sư Muôn)
keywords: Stop at Chùa Sư Muôn, a modest working pagoda that locals use — not a viewpoint campus.
about: Stop at Chùa Sư Muôn, a modest working pagoda that locals use — not a viewpoint campus.
hook: A small island pagoda named for the monk Sư Muôn.
cardSummary: Small pagoda, free; daylight. 20–30 minutes. Modest dress. Pair with Sùng Hưng or Hộ Quốc, not as a standalone taxi from Sunset Town.
whyGo: Five quiet minutes if you are already inland.

name: Cao Đài Temple Phú Quốc
keywords: Visit the Cao Đài temple in the Dương Đông area — a compact example of Vietnam’s syncretic faith, far smaller than Tây Ninh’s Holy See.
typical hours Daylight; ceremony times posted
about: Visit the Cao Đài temple in the Dương Đông area — a compact example of Vietnam’s syncretic faith, far smaller than Tây Ninh’s Holy See.
hook: The island’s Cao Đài hall — the eye, the colours, a short look.
cardSummary: Town Cao Đài temple, free from the yard; ceremonies at set hours. Modest dress. Pair with Dinh Cậu or the night market. Do not expect the Tây Ninh scale.
whyGo: Twenty minutes of a faith you will not see at Hộ Quốc.

name: Phú Quốc Prison Museum (Coconut Tree Prison)
keywords: Walk Nhà tù Phú Quốc (Coconut Tree Prison), the museum on the former POW camp.
about: Walk Nhà tù Phú Quốc (Coconut Tree Prison), the museum on the former POW camp. Wikipedia records it as a major wartime prison; displays are graphic.
hook: The coconut-tree prison — a harsh 20th-century site in An Thới.
cardSummary: Prison museum in the south (An Thới). Ticket about 15,000–30,000đ; typical 07:00–17:00. 60–90 minutes. Not for young children. Pair with Hộ Quốc or the cable if you are already south — emotionally it does not mix with VinWonders the same hour.
whyGo: The island’s necessary history hour, not a beach.

name: Cội Nguồn Museum
keywords: Tour Bảo tàng Cội Nguồn, the privately assembled Phú Quốc museum of local life, fishing, and wartime objects in a garden compound.
about: Tour Bảo tàng Cội Nguồn, the privately assembled Phú Quốc museum of local life, fishing, and wartime objects in a garden compound.
hook: A private island-history house — boats, ceramics, and a garden of objects.
