cardSummary: Private museum inland from Dương Đông. Ticket about 30,000–50,000đ; typical 08:00–17:00. 45–75 minutes. Pair with a pepper farm. English varies. Different story from the prison museum — do both only if you like objects.
whyGo: Context for pepper, fish sauce, and the prison, in one compound.

name: Hàm Ninh Fishing Village
keywords: Eat at Hàm Ninh, the east-coast fishing village used for seafood lunches and a pearl-farm hop, calmer water than the west in the dry season.
about: Eat at Hàm Ninh, the east-coast fishing village used for seafood lunches and a pearl-farm hop, calmer water than the west in the dry season.
hook: East-coast pier village — crab, clams, and boats on the lee shore.
cardSummary: East-coast village. Free to walk; lunch is the cost. 1.5–2.5 hours. Pair with Ngọc Hiền Pearl or Bãi Sao (south-east). Agree seafood prices. Different village from Cửa Cạn on the west.
whyGo: The island’s working lunch, not a resort grill.

name: Cửa Cạn Fishing Village
keywords: Walk Cửa Cạn village for a working west-coast harbour next to the beach of the same name — fish, boats, and a slower street than Dương Đông.
about: Walk Cửa Cạn village for a working west-coast harbour next to the beach of the same name — fish, boats, and a slower street than Dương Đông.
hook: West-coast estuary village — boats at the river mouth.
cardSummary: West-coast fishing village. Free; eat if a stall looks busy. 45–75 minutes. Pair with Cửa Cạn Beach. This is the lanes and harbour; the beach is the sand next door.
whyGo: Village life on the way to Ông Lang, not a second Hàm Ninh.

name: Grand World Phú Quốc (The Sleepless City)
keywords: Walk Grand World, Vinpearl’s “Sleepless City” — lit canals, shopping, and evening shows.
typical hours Evening is the point; shops into late
about: Walk Grand World, Vinpearl’s “Sleepless City” — lit canals, shopping, and evening shows. Aquatopia is the water park on the same campus, ticketed separately.
hook: The built night city — canals, shows, and Aquatopia next door.
cardSummary: South-island entertainment district. Grounds often free in the evening; shows and Aquatopia extra. 2–4 hours. Pair with Sunset Town / Kiss Bridge the same south-end day, not with a village lunch. This is not the Dương Đông night market.
hours: Evening is the point; shops into late
whyGo: The designed night when you are done with Dương Đông’s grills.

name: Sunset Town (Town of Sunset)
keywords: Wander Sunset Town at An Thới’s tip — the staged harbour town that holds the Hòn Thơm cable station and Cầu Hôn.
about: Wander Sunset Town at An Thới’s tip — the staged harbour town that holds the Hòn Thơm cable station and Cầu Hôn. Different campus from Grand World, same south-end trip.
hook: The Mediterranean-style south town — cable station, Kiss Bridge, pastel streets.
cardSummary: Purpose-built south town. Free to walk; cable and some decks extra. Afternoon into evening. Kiss Bridge and the cable station are pins inside this town — walk them, do not taxi twice. Pair with Hòn Thơm or VinWonders.
whyGo: The postcard streets and the cable, in one grid.

name: Kiss Bridge (Cầu Hôn)
keywords: Walk Cầu Hôn, the Kiss Bridge — a short showpiece span and sculpture at Sunset Town, built for photographs at dusk.
about: Walk Cầu Hôn, the Kiss Bridge — a short showpiece span and sculpture at Sunset Town, built for photographs at dusk.
hook: The golden lips sculpture and pedestrian span in Sunset Town.
cardSummary: Bridge and sculpture inside Sunset Town (same visit, no second ticket). Free. 20–40 minutes. Best at dusk. Do not make a separate trip from Grand World if you can walk or shuttle the south cluster.
whyGo: The one structure people mean when they say “Sunset Town photo.”

name: Hòn Thơm Cable Car Station
keywords: Board the Hòn Thơm cable at Sunset Town for the 7.
about: Board the Hòn Thơm cable at Sunset Town for the 7.9 km sea crossing to Pineapple Island. This card is the station and the ride; the island is the landing.
hook: The world’s longest over-sea cable — the station in Sunset Town.
cardSummary: Cable station in Sunset Town. Ticket is the ride (often combined with island parks). Typical 08:00–16:30; last car back is earlier than you think. Pair with Hòn Thơm Island. Not a town plaza stroll — buy the ticket or just photograph the station.
whyGo: The engineering reason people go south, even if they skip VinWonders.

name: VinWonders Phú Quốc Theme Park
keywords: Spend a ticketed day at VinWonders on Hòn Thơm: rides, aquarium/shows, and park food.
about: Spend a ticketed day at VinWonders on Hòn Thơm: rides, aquarium/shows, and park food. Cable is usually bundled or sold next door. Not the Safari, not Aquatopia.
hook: The island theme park on Hòn Thơm — rides, shows, a full ticket day.
cardSummary: Theme park on Hòn Thơm. Full-day ticket (often $40–70 with cable). 08:00–17:00 class hours. Different fence from Vinpearl Safari (on the main island) and Aquatopia (at Grand World). One park day is enough.
whyGo: If someone in the group wants a park, not another beach.

name: Vinpearl Safari Phú Quốc
keywords: Tour Vinpearl Safari, the fenced wildlife park in northern/central Phú Quốc — bus or self-drive loops, not a national-park hike.
about: Tour Vinpearl Safari, the fenced wildlife park in northern/central Phú Quốc — bus or self-drive loops, not a national-park hike.
hook: A drive-through safari on the main island — not the Hòn Thơm theme park.
cardSummary: Safari park on Phú Quốc island (not Hòn Thơm). Ticket about $20–40; typical 09:00–16:00. 3–4 hours. Different ticket from VinWonders and from Phú Quốc National Park. Midday heat is hard on animals and visitors — go early.
whyGo: A zoo-scale half-day if that is the trip, not a substitute for the real park.

name: Aquatopia Water Park
keywords: Spend a hot afternoon at Aquatopia, the water park attached to Grand World.
about: Spend a hot afternoon at Aquatopia, the water park attached to Grand World. Separate ticket from VinWonders on Hòn Thơm.
hook: The water-park campus beside Grand World — slides, not the Hòn Thơm rides.
cardSummary: Water park at Grand World. Ticket about $20–35; typical 10:00–18:00. 3–5 hours. Not VinWonders. Pair with a Grand World evening. Bring a rash guard — midday sun is fierce.
whyGo: Slides when the sea is rough, in the south-end built zone.

name: Khu Cượng Pepper Farm
keywords: Walk Khu Cượng’s pepper farm for the island’s famous vines and a short tasting.
about: Walk Khu Cượng’s pepper farm for the island’s famous vines and a short tasting. Phú Quốc pepper is a real GI product; the shop is optional.
hook: A working Phú Quốc pepper garden — vines, tasting, no obligation to buy sacks.
cardSummary: Pepper farm inland. Usually free entry; tasting and sales extra. 30–50 minutes. Pair with Đức Phát only if you like comparison — one farm is enough. Combine with Cội Nguồn or Suối Tranh.
whyGo: Twenty minutes of the crop the island is actually known for.

name: Đức Phát Pepper Farm
keywords: Visit Đức Phát if you want another Phú Quốc pepper walk.
about: Visit Đức Phát if you want another Phú Quốc pepper walk. The vines look the same; the welcome and shop differ.
hook: A second pepper garden — skip it if you already did Khu Cượng.
cardSummary: Pepper farm. Free or donation; shop extra. 30–45 minutes. Pick one pepper stop. Pair with a waterfall or museum, not a second farm.
whyGo: Only as an alternative farm, not a pair with Khu Cượng.

name: Khải Hoàn Fish Sauce Factory
keywords: Tour Khải Hoàn’s fish-sauce house: wooden vats, a sharp smell, and a tasting that explains why Phú Quốc nước mắm is a GI product.
about: Tour Khải Hoàn’s fish-sauce house: wooden vats, a sharp smell, and a tasting that explains why Phú Quốc nước mắm is a GI product.
hook: Barrel halls of Phú Quốc nước mắm — the island’s other famous export.
cardSummary: Fish-sauce factory, usually free tour; bottles for sale. 20–40 minutes. The smell is the experience. Pair with Phụng Hưng only if you collect factories — one is enough. Near Dương Đông for many visitors.
whyGo: Ten minutes that makes every seafood dinner make more sense.

name: Phụng Hưng Fish Sauce Factory
keywords: See Phụng Hưng’s nước mắm barrels if Khải Hoàn is closed or crowded.
about: See Phụng Hưng’s nước mắm barrels if Khải Hoàn is closed or crowded. Same craft, different shop.
hook: Another vat house — go here or Khải Hoàn, not both.
cardSummary: Fish-sauce factory, free tour typical. 20–35 minutes. Pick one sauce house. Combine with the night market for dinner, not with a second vat hall.
whyGo: A backup factory, not a second smelling.

name: Sim Wine Factory (Vườn Sim)
keywords: Taste rượu sim at a Vườn Sim garden: purple myrtle fruit, a short walk, and a sweet fortified wine the island sells to visitors.
about: Taste rượu sim at a Vườn Sim garden: purple myrtle fruit, a short walk, and a sweet fortified wine the island sells to visitors.
hook: Rose-myrtle wine — a sweet island tasting, not Bordeaux.
cardSummary: Sim (rose myrtle) garden and tasting. Often free entry; bottles extra. 30–45 minutes. Pair with a pepper farm. This is a tourist garden, not a fine-wine estate.
whyGo: A novelty pour after pepper, if you like sweet drinks.

name: Ngọc Hiền Pearl Farm
keywords: Visit Ngọc Hiền (or a similar east-coast pearl farm) for a short raft talk and a showroom.
about: Visit Ngọc Hiền (or a similar east-coast pearl farm) for a short raft talk and a showroom. Buy only if you want to; the visit is the process.
hook: A raft-and-showroom pearl farm, usually near the east-coast villages.
cardSummary: Pearl farm, often free tour; jewellery extra. 30–50 minutes. Pair with Hàm Ninh. Pressure to buy varies — walk out if you came for the raft. Not a beach.
whyGo: A 40-minute craft stop with Hàm Ninh seafood.

name: Paradise Cave (Động Thiên Đường)
keywords: Walk the illuminated wooden path deep into Paradise Cave’s vast chambers.
about: Walk the illuminated wooden path deep into Paradise Cave’s vast chambers.
hook: Boardwalk through one of Asia’s most spectacular dry caves.
cardSummary: Follow Paradise Cave’s wooden boardwalk into vast illuminated chambers of stalactites and soaring ceilings. The easiest jaw-drop cave near Phong Nha — allow time for the forest walk to the entrance.
whyGo: Phong Nha’s most accessible show-stopping cave — no swimming required.

name: Phong Nha Cave
keywords: Take a shared boat into Phong Nha Cave, then walk deeper sections on foot.
about: Take a shared boat into Phong Nha Cave, then walk deeper sections on foot.
hook: Riverboat into the illuminated river cave that named the park.
cardSummary: Board a riverboat into Phong Nha Cave’s illuminated waterway, then walk deeper chambers on marked paths. The park’s namesake experience — scenic, accessible, and easy to pair with Paradise Cave on another day.
whyGo: The namesake cave experience — classic and family-friendly.

name: Sơn Đoòng Cave
keywords: Join the multi-day Sơn Đoòng expedition through jungle, a collapsed doline, and a river passage tall enough for a jungle and clouds.
about: Join the multi-day Sơn Đoòng expedition through jungle, a collapsed doline, and a river passage tall enough for a jungle and clouds. Independent visits are not allowed.
hook: The world’s largest known cave passage — Oxalis permit only.
cardSummary: Oxalis-only 4–5 day trek. Permit waitlist, not a day ticket. Dry-season camps. Do not book Hang Én as a “Sơn Đoòng lite” without reading the difference. This is not Paradise Cave.
whyGo: The cave that redefined Phong Nha, if you can get a place.

name: Hang Én
keywords: Trek to Hang Én (Swallow Cave) on a 1–2 night Oxalis itinerary: river crossings, a vast portal, and a sand camp inside the cave.
about: Trek to Hang Én (Swallow Cave) on a 1–2 night Oxalis itinerary: river crossings, a vast portal, and a sand camp inside the cave. Many Sơn Đoòng teams pass through here.
hook: A huge swallow cave and camp beach on the Sơn Đoòng approach.
cardSummary: Oxalis overnight, not a boardwalk. Fitness required. Hang Én is a destination of its own — do not treat it as a failed Sơn Đoòng booking. Closed in heavy flood months.
whyGo: The biggest cave most travellers can actually book.

name: Hang Va
keywords: Visit Hang Va on selected Oxalis treks: unusual calcite towers in shallow water, not a lit tourist path.
typical hours With Hang Én trek
about: Visit Hang Va on selected Oxalis treks: unusual calcite towers in shallow water, not a lit tourist path. Often bundled with Hang Én rather than sold as a town half-day.
hook: Tower karst and a rimstone-pool cave, usually with Hang Én.
cardSummary: Expedition add-on. Confirm the sheet. Wet cave, helmets. Pair with Hang Én. Not a substitute for Paradise.
whyGo: The sculpted pool cave next to the Én route.

name: Nước Nứt Cave
keywords: Enter Nước Nứt on a Tu Lan / Oxalis wet-cave day: river passages and swim sections in the Minh Hóa karst, west of Phong Nha town.
about: Enter Nước Nứt on a Tu Lan / Oxalis wet-cave day: river passages and swim sections in the Minh Hóa karst, west of Phong Nha town.
hook: A wet Tu Lan cave — swim and wade, not a boardwalk.
cardSummary: Guided wet cave. Swim fitness. Minh Hóa, not the Paradise stairs. Pair with Tú Làn or Hang Tiên on the same operator sheet.
whyGo: The splash cave of the Tu Lan system.

name: Tú Làn Cave System
keywords: Trek the Tú Làn system with a licensed operator: a cluster of wet and dry caves, village edges, and overnight camps west of the main park road.
about: Trek the Tú Làn system with a licensed operator: a cluster of wet and dry caves, village edges, and overnight camps west of the main park road. Individual cave cards (Nước Nứt, Tiên, Trà Ang, Over, Pygmy) are stops on these routes.
hook: A multi-cave jungle system in Minh Hóa — rivers, camps, and dry halls.
cardSummary: Oxalis / licensed 1–3 day trek. Minh Hóa transfer. Inner cave cards are the same system — do not book Tú Làn plus Nước Nứt as two trips. Flood season closes wet caves.
whyGo: The expedition neighborhood that is not Sơn Đoòng.

name: Hang Tiên
keywords: Walk Hang Tiên on a Tu Lan itinerary: a large dry passage used on 2-day routes.
typical hours With Tu Lan tour
visit length On Tu Lan day
about: Walk Hang Tiên on a Tu Lan itinerary: a large dry passage used on 2-day routes. It is not Tiên Cave at Tràng An.
hook: A vast dry hall in the Tu Lan cluster — “fairy” cave, not a town stroll.
cardSummary: On the Tú Làn sheet. Helmets. Pair with Nước Nứt or Trà Ang. Not a Phong Nha boat cave.
whyGo: The big dry chamber of Tu Lan.

name: Trà Ang Cave
keywords: Wade Trà Ang when the Tu Lan route lists it — another wet sister to Nước Nứt, not a separate town ticket.
typical hours With Tu Lan tour
about: Wade Trà Ang when the Tu Lan route lists it — another wet sister to Nước Nứt, not a separate town ticket.
hook: A wet Tu Lan river cave with swim-through passages.
cardSummary: Tu Lan wet cave. Confirm the name. Do not book as a third full day after Tú Làn + Nước Nứt.
whyGo: A second swim cave on the same Minh Hóa day.

name: Hang Vòm
keywords: Hang Vòm is a major underground river in Phong Nha–Kẻ Bàng, explored as a technical or long jungle trip rather than a lit visitor cave.
about: Hang Vòm is a major underground river in Phong Nha–Kẻ Bàng, explored as a technical or long jungle trip rather than a lit visitor cave. Confirm the operator; many town desks will not sell it.
hook: A long river cave in the western park — specialist access.
cardSummary: Specialist / expedition. Not a boardwalk. Pair with park HQ advice, not with Paradise the same morning.
whyGo: A serious river cave, not the Phong Nha boat.

name: Hang Đại Ả
keywords: Hang Đại Ả sits among the western / Tu Lan–adjacent karsts.
about: Hang Đại Ả sits among the western / Tu Lan–adjacent karsts. It is not on the Paradise ticket. Treat it as a guided expedition stop.
hook: A lesser-sold jungle cave — book only with a named operator.
cardSummary: Specialist cave. Confirm location. Do not confuse with Phong Nha Cave.
whyGo: If your sheet lists it; otherwise skip.

name: Hang Over
keywords: Scramble Hang Over on selected Tu Lan dry-cave days — a high, dusty hall.
typical hours With Tu Lan tour
about: Scramble Hang Over on selected Tu Lan dry-cave days — a high, dusty hall. Same Minh Hóa system as Pygmy and Tiên.
hook: A dry Tu Lan cave named for the climb, not the drink.
cardSummary: On Tu Lan dry routes. Helmets. Pair with Hang Pygmy. Not a nightlife card.
whyGo: The dry-cave contrast after a wet Tu Lan day.

name: Hang Pygmy
keywords: Visit Hang Pygmy as a shorter dry stop on Tu Lan itineraries — tight in places, not a cathedral like Paradise.
typical hours With Tu Lan tour
visit length On Tu Lan day
about: Visit Hang Pygmy as a shorter dry stop on Tu Lan itineraries — tight in places, not a cathedral like Paradise.
hook: A compact dry cave on the Tu Lan circuit.
cardSummary: Tu Lan stop. Same ticket family as Hang Over. Do not book alone from town.
whyGo: A small hall between the bigger Tu Lan names.

name: Sơn Nữ Cave
keywords: Sơn Nữ is a lesser-visited cave in the Phong Nha–Kẻ Bàng karst.
about: Sơn Nữ is a lesser-visited cave in the Phong Nha–Kẻ Bàng karst. Some local tours use the name; it is not Sơn Đoòng and not a standard ticket window.
hook: A quieter named cave — confirm which operator actually goes.
cardSummary: Ask for the map pin before paying. Not the riverboat cave. Pair with park HQ if you want an official list.
whyGo: Only if a trusted desk lists a real route.

name: Rục Mòn Cave
keywords: Rục Mòn sits off the main Paradise road — a cave-and-forest pocket that appears on some trekking menus rather than the boat ticket.
about: Rục Mòn sits off the main Paradise road — a cave-and-forest pocket that appears on some trekking menus rather than the boat ticket.
hook: A remote western cave / valley used on longer jungle days.
cardSummary: Guided, not DIY. Full day. Do not stack with Sơn Đoòng. Confirm 4×4 or trek time.
whyGo: A far-west name if you already did the show caves.

name: E Cave
keywords: E Cave (Hang E) is a minor Phong Nha-area cave some motorbike or farmstay loops include.
about: E Cave (Hang E) is a minor Phong Nha-area cave some motorbike or farmstay loops include. It is not a UNESCO headline and not Dark Cave.
hook: A small letter-named cave used on some local loops.
cardSummary: Local add-on. 30–60 minutes. Pair with a valley loop, not with Paradise. Confirm which “E Cave” the driver means.
whyGo: A short extra hole if you are already on that road.

name: Moọc Spring (Suối Nước Moọc)
keywords: Swim or walk Suối Nước Moọc — a clear rise from the limestone, usually sold with the Chày River / Dark Cave complex rather than as a city pool.
about: Swim or walk Suối Nước Moọc — a clear rise from the limestone, usually sold with the Chày River / Dark Cave complex rather than as a city pool.
hook: Turquoise karst spring on the Chày River eco-trail.
cardSummary: Spring on the Chày eco-trail. Ticketed with the complex or a combo. 1–2 hours. Pair with Dark Cave or Sông Chày. Not a waterfall hike.
whyGo: The prettiest water you can reach without an expedition permit.

name: Chày River (Sông Chày)
keywords: Use Sông Chày as the water corridor northwest of town: kayaks, a long zipline on some tickets, and the trail to Hang Tối.
about: Use Sông Chày as the water corridor northwest of town: kayaks, a long zipline on some tickets, and the trail to Hang Tối. Dark Cave is the cave; this card is the river.
hook: The kayak-and-zipline river that hosts Dark Cave and Moọc.
cardSummary: River complex. Combo tickets common. 2–4 hours. Pair with Dark Cave and Moọc — one campus afternoon, not three days. Life jacket on the water.
whyGo: The surface river the adventure park is built on.

name: Hava Valley (Thung lũng Ngọc Bích)
keywords: Cycle or ride to Hava (Ngọc Bích) Valley for fields, a small river, and farmstays — countryside Phong Nha, not a cave ticket.
about: Cycle or ride to Hava (Ngọc Bích) Valley for fields, a small river, and farmstays — countryside Phong Nha, not a cave ticket.
hook: A farmstay valley of rice, karst, and a swimming hole.
cardSummary: Rural valley. Free to look; swim/farmstay extra. 2–3 hours. Pair with Bồng Lai or East Hill. Different road from Paradise.
whyGo: A green afternoon when you are cave-tired.

name: Ozo Treetop Park
keywords: Climb Ozo’s treetop courses — platforms, zip lines, and a jungle play park aimed at families and groups, not cavers.
about: Climb Ozo’s treetop courses — platforms, zip lines, and a jungle play park aimed at families and groups, not cavers.
hook: A forest high-ropes and zipline park near the cave roads.
cardSummary: Adventure park. Ticketed. 2–3 hours. Pair with Moọc or a rest day. Closed or wet-slippery after heavy rain. Not Oxalis.
whyGo: When the group wants height without a mud cave.

name: Phong Nha Botanical Garden
keywords: Walk the Phong Nha botanical / forest garden for labeled plants and a flat hour.
about: Walk the Phong Nha botanical / forest garden for labeled plants and a flat hour. It is not the national-park jungle trek.
hook: A park garden of native plants and easy forest paths.
cardSummary: Garden paths. Modest ticket. 1–1.5 hours. Pair with town or Ozo. Not Kẻ Bàng wilderness.
whyGo: Shade and names of trees after a cave morning.

name: Bồng Lai Valley
keywords: Ride Bồng Lai (often called the “countryside tour”): lanes, river views, and farm stops.
about: Ride Bồng Lai (often called the “countryside tour”): lanes, river views, and farm stops. The Duck Stop and Pub with Cold Beer sit on this same loop.
hook: The bicycle countryside — rice, buffalo, and farm pubs.
cardSummary: Valley loop by bike or xe. Free roads; drinks extra. 3–5 hours. Duck Stop and Pub with Cold Beer are stops here — do not book three half-days. Heat at midday; start early.
whyGo: The classic non-cave Phong Nha day.

name: The Duck Stop
keywords: Pause at The Duck Stop on the Bồng Lai loop for a farm lunch and the duck pond.
about: Pause at The Duck Stop on the Bồng Lai loop for a farm lunch and the duck pond. It is a café-farm, not a wildlife park.
hook: A Bồng Lai farm stop — ducks, noodles, and a river lawn.
cardSummary: Farm café on the Bồng Lai loop. Food extra. 45–90 minutes. Same valley as Pub with Cold Beer — pick one long lunch, not two.
whyGo: The lunch pin on the countryside ride.

name: Pub with Cold Beer
keywords: Drink at Pub with Cold Beer in Bồng Lai — a rustic riverside pub, hammocks, and the postcard “countryside beer” stop.
about: Drink at Pub with Cold Beer in Bồng Lai — a rustic riverside pub, hammocks, and the postcard “countryside beer” stop. It is a pub, not a cave.
hook: The farm pub that named a thousand motorbike tours.
cardSummary: Farm pub. Drinks extra. 1–2 hours. Same Bồng Lai card family. Heat + beer + bike needs water. Not a nightclub in town.
whyGo: The famous farm beer on the same loop as The Duck Stop.

name: East Hill Phong Nha
keywords: Climb or ride to East Hill for a terrace view of Phong Nha town and the limestone rim.
typical hours Café hours, often to dusk
about: Climb or ride to East Hill for a terrace view of Phong Nha town and the limestone rim. Sunset is the point; the cave is not here.
hook: A café-hill viewpoint over the town karst.
cardSummary: Hill café. Drink extra; view is the visit. 45–75 minutes. Pair with town market. Not Bài Thơ and not a trek.
whyGo: The land viewpoint after a river-cave morning.

name: Thác Gió (Wind Waterfall)
keywords: Walk to Thác Gió when water is up — a local waterfall west of town, more breeze and spray than a cave cathedral.
about: Walk to Thác Gió when water is up — a local waterfall west of town, more breeze and spray than a cave cathedral.
hook: A forest waterfall that can roar or thin with the season.
cardSummary: Seasonal waterfall. Modest access. 1–2 hours. Best after rain; late dry season can disappoint. Pair with a forest road, not with Sơn Đoòng.
whyGo: A surface fall after too many underground hours.

name: Vàng Macaque Enclosure
keywords: Visit the Vàng macaque enclosure used by a countryside farmstay: a fenced troop, not a wild-forest encounter.
about: Visit the Vàng macaque enclosure used by a countryside farmstay: a fenced troop, not a wild-forest encounter. Keep food away and follow the host.
hook: A farmstay macaque enclosure — look, do not feed.
cardSummary: Farm enclosure. Ask the host; not a national-park safari. 30–45 minutes. Do not feed. Skip if you want only wild wildlife.
whyGo: A short animal stop on a farm loop, if you accept a captive setting.

name: Eight Ladies Cave (Hang Tám Cô)
keywords: Pay respects at Hang Tám Cô: a wartime shelter where eight women died in a 1972 bombing.
about: Pay respects at Hang Tám Cô: a wartime shelter where eight women died in a 1972 bombing. It is a memorial, not an adventure cave.
hook: The cave-shrine to eight young volunteers killed on Highway 20.
cardSummary: Memorial cave on the Ho Chi Minh / Highway 20 side. Quiet visit. 45–75 minutes. Pair with the martyrs memorial. No zipline, no swimming.
whyGo: The park’s most important war cave.

name: Highway 20 Martyrs Memorial
keywords: Stop at the Highway 20 Decision / martyrs memorial — the land route through Kẻ Bàng that carried wartime traffic.
about: Stop at the Highway 20 Decision / martyrs memorial — the land route through Kẻ Bàng that carried wartime traffic. Pair with Hang Tám Cô on the same road.
hook: The monument on the Truong Son road that supplied the south.
cardSummary: Roadside memorial. Free. 20–40 minutes. Same outing as Hang Tám Cô. Not a cave.
whyGo: Context for the eight-ladies cave.

name: Bến Tiến Ferry
keywords: Ride Bến Tiến when the river still uses a small ferry: motorbikes, a few cars, and the opposite bank.
about: Ride Bến Tiến when the river still uses a small ferry: motorbikes, a few cars, and the opposite bank. Schedules follow water and local need.
hook: A Son River cable ferry — working crossing, not a cruise.
cardSummary: Local ferry. Small fare. 15–30 minutes including wait. Pair with a west-bank loop. Floods can stop it. Not the Phong Nha Cave boat.
whyGo: A living river crossing, five minutes that feel like 1970s logistics.

name: Trạm Trăn
keywords: Pass Trạm Trăn — a historic way-station / junction on the western park roads, more a place-name on the Ho Chi Minh trail story than a museum building.
about: Pass Trạm Trăn — a historic way-station / junction on the western park roads, more a place-name on the Ho Chi Minh trail story than a museum building.
hook: A former Truong Son station name still used as a road pin.
cardSummary: Road pin. Short stop. Pair with Highway 20 and Hang Tám Cô. Do not expect a ticketed site.
whyGo: A map point on the wartime supply road.

name: Phong Nha–Kẻ Bàng National Park Headquarters
keywords: Stop at the national-park headquarters for current cave status, permits, and the official map.
about: Stop at the national-park headquarters for current cave status, permits, and the official map. The phong-nha card is the landscape; this card is the desk.
hook: The official park office — tickets, maps, and which caves are open.
cardSummary: Park office. Free to ask; tickets for sites vary. 20–40 minutes. Pair with Phong Nha Cave or Paradise. Flood and fire rules change — ask here.
whyGo: Before you pay a tout for a cave that is closed.

name: Khe Gát Secret Airfield
keywords: Visit Khe Gát, a concealed airfield used during the war in the Phong Nha–Kẻ Bàng hills.
about: Visit Khe Gát, a concealed airfield used during the war in the Phong Nha–Kẻ Bàng hills. There is little infrastructure; the visit is the landscape and the history.
hook: A wartime airstrip in the karst — now a quiet field with a story.
cardSummary: Historic airfield. Free or local guide. 1–2 hours. Pair with Highway 20. Do not expect a museum café. Ask about access — it is not a daily tour.
whyGo: A war-engineering site, not a cave.

name: Phong Nha Town Market
keywords: Shop Phong Nha’s covered / street market on the Son River town grid.
about: Shop Phong Nha’s covered / street market on the Son River town grid. Morning is when it is a market; afternoon is half-shut.
hook: The small town market — fruit, meat, and breakfast noodles.
cardSummary: Town market. Free. 30–50 minutes. Morning. Pair with East Hill or the cave boat. Not a night market.
whyGo: Breakfast before the boat cave.

name: Po Nagar Cham Towers
keywords: Climb the hilltop sanctuary of the goddess Po Ină Nagar: red-brick towers built without mortar, a black-stone statue in the 23 m north-east tower, and a view over the river mouth t
about: Climb the hilltop sanctuary of the goddess Po Ină Nagar: red-brick towers built without mortar, a black-stone statue in the 23 m north-east tower, and a view over the river mouth toward the bay.
hook: Cham brick towers on a hill above the Cái River.
cardSummary: UNESCO-listed Cham sanctuary of the goddess Po Nagar. Ticket about 30,000 VND, typically 06:00–18:00 (often 17:30 Oct–Dec). Remove shoes in the towers; cover shoulders and knees. Pair with Tháp Bà mud baths next door, not a second temple circuit.
whyGo: The one Cham monument that belongs on a first Nha Trang day.

name: Long Sơn Pagoda (Great White Buddha)
keywords: Visit the working monastery at the foot of Trại Thủy Hill, then climb the dragon stairs to Kim Thân Phật Tổ — the seated white Buddha cast in 1964 and visible from the highway and
about: Visit the working monastery at the foot of Trại Thủy Hill, then climb the dragon stairs to Kim Thân Phật Tổ — the seated white Buddha cast in 1964 and visible from the highway and railway.
hook: A 24-metre white Buddha above the city rooftops.
cardSummary: Free active pagoda on 23 Tháng 10, a short hop from the station. Street-level halls plus ~150–193 steps to the 24 m white Buddha. Cover shoulders and knees. Pair with Hải Đức on the same hill, not a second giant-Buddha outing.
whyGo: Nha Trang’s landmark pagoda: hall, reclining Buddha, and a city-and-bay viewpoint.

name: Christ the King Cathedral (Mountain / Stone Church)
keywords: Walk up Hoàng Lan (Hòn Một) Hill to the mother church of the Diocese of Nha Trang: consecrated in 1933 under Louis Vallet, grey “stone” walls that are mostly concrete, and stained
about: Walk up Hoàng Lan (Hòn Một) Hill to the mother church of the Diocese of Nha Trang: consecrated in 1933 under Louis Vallet, grey “stone” walls that are mostly concrete, and stained glass of Joan of Arc and John Vianney.
hook: Gothic Revival cathedral on a 12-metre hill by the station.
cardSummary: Free Gothic Revival cathedral at 1 Thái Nguyên, near the six-way junction and the train station. Exterior anytime; dress modestly if Mass is on. The “Stone Church” nickname is visual — most of the fabric is painted concrete. Combine with Long Sơn, 10 minutes west.
whyGo: The city’s Catholic landmark — architecture and stained glass, not a beach stop.

name: Hải Đức Pagoda
keywords: Walk the ridge from Long Sơn to Hải Đức — founded as Duyên Sanh in 1883, renamed in 1891, and moved onto Trại Thủy Hill in the 1940s.
about: Walk the ridge from Long Sơn to Hải Đức — founded as Duyên Sanh in 1883, renamed in 1891, and moved onto Trại Thủy Hill in the 1940s. It later hosted the Central Vietnam Buddhist Institute.
hook: The quieter Trại Thủy monastery above Long Sơn.
cardSummary: Free working pagoda on Trại Thủy with East-Asian halls and a hill view. Wikipedia still lists it with Long Sơn as a main city site. Cover shoulders. Do not treat it as a second White Buddha — the statue is at Long Sơn.
whyGo: Same hill as the white Buddha, without the tour-bus landing.

name: Tòng Lâm Lô Sơn Pagoda (Đá Lố)
keywords: Ride 11 km north to Vĩnh Phương for the forest monastery founded in 1957 and later expanded around a 44 m Amitābha that Vietnam Records listed among the country’s tallest Buddha st
about: Ride 11 km north to Vĩnh Phương for the forest monastery founded in 1957 and later expanded around a 44 m Amitābha that Vietnam Records listed among the country’s tallest Buddha statues.
hook: A 44-metre Amitābha on Đá Lố mountain north of town.
cardSummary: Free (donation) Tịnh Độ monastery at Núi Đá Lố, ~11 km north. The 44 m Amitābha is the reason to come. Not in the city grid — budget a Grab or motorbike. Do not stack with Long Sơn the same hot afternoon.
whyGo: The giant-Buddha outing when Long Sơn’s hill already feels small.

name: Chùa Từ Tôn (Hòn Đỏ)
keywords: Cross ~300 m of water to the uninhabited red-granite islet where Thích Viên Mãn founded Từ Tôn in 1960, named for Maitreya.
about: Cross ~300 m of water to the uninhabited red-granite islet where Thích Viên Mãn founded Từ Tôn in 1960, named for Maitreya. Local boats run from the Hòn Chồng shore; fishermen still stop before going out.
hook: A 1960 pagoda on the red-rock islet off Hòn Chồng.
cardSummary: Small island pagoda off the north shore. Boat from Hòn Chồng, often casual/free or a small cash fare. Combine with Hòn Chồng rocks the same hour. The nature card “Hòn Đỏ” is the same islet from the geology side — do not book two trips.
whyGo: The sea pagoda — not another city hall with incense.

name: Kim Sơn Temple (Sắc Tứ Kim Sơn)
keywords: Visit the old monastery at Ngọc Hội (Vĩnh Ngọc / Tây Nha Trang), associated in local histories with Trần Nhân Tông’s 1301 stop and later “sắc tứ” royal recognition.
about: Visit the old monastery at Ngọc Hội (Vĩnh Ngọc / Tây Nha Trang), associated in local histories with Trần Nhân Tông’s 1301 stop and later “sắc tứ” royal recognition. The present halls are later rebuilds on an older Buddhist site.
hook: A Trần-dynasty hill temple later granted a royal plaque.
cardSummary: Free historic pagoda on a low hill in Vĩnh Ngọc, inland from the beach strip. Tradition ties the name Kim Sơn to Trần Nhân Tông in 1301. Quiet, local, and easy to confuse with other Kim Sơn nunneries — confirm Sắc Tứ Kim Sơn, Ngọc Hội.
whyGo: The deep-time pagoda if Po Nagar already covered Cham history.

name: Nguyễn Trung Trực Temple
keywords: Pay respects at Nha Trang’s neighborhood temple for Nguyễn Trung Trực, the southern commander who burned the French warship Espérance in 1868.
about: Pay respects at Nha Trang’s neighborhood temple for Nguyễn Trung Trực, the southern commander who burned the French warship Espérance in 1868. This is a working urban shrine, not the national relic complex in Rạch Giá.
hook: A local shrine to the 19th-century resistance hero.
cardSummary: Small free temple dedicated to Nguyễn Trung Trực. Do not plan a pilgrimage-scale visit — the famous đình is in Rạch Giá, Kiên Giang. Confirm the Nha Trang address before a Grab. Incense optional; 15–25 minutes is enough.
whyGo: A short civic stop if you want hero cults beyond Cham and Buddhist hills.

name: National Oceanographic Museum of Vietnam
keywords: Walk the French-founded Institute of Oceanography campus at 1 Cầu Đá: specimen halls, live tanks, an underwater tunnel, and outdoor pools on a ~20-hectare site that still does rese
about: Walk the French-founded Institute of Oceanography campus at 1 Cầu Đá: specimen halls, live tanks, an underwater tunnel, and outdoor pools on a ~20-hectare site that still does research, not only tourism.
hook: Southeast Asia’s oldest marine institute, still on Cầu Đá.
cardSummary: Open daily about 06:00–18:00. Adults ~40,000 VND; students less. 2–3 hours. South end of Trần Phú near the tourist port. Arrive at opening to beat groups in the tunnel. Pair with a Cầu Đá boat or skip Hon Mun if you only want fish behind glass.
whyGo: The serious indoor half-day when the bay is too rough for a boat.

name: Alexandre Yersin Museum (Pasteur Institute)
keywords: Alexandre Émile John Yersin (22 September 1863 – 1 March 1943) was a Swiss-French physician and bacteriologist. He is remembered for his work as a pioneer in microbiology and immunology.
about: Climb to the small 1997 museum in Yersin’s former Pasteur Institute home at 8–10 Trần Phú: letters, telescopes, the Hong Kong microscope, and the story of the Swiss-French doctor who founded the Nha Trang institute in 1895 and later pointed planners to Đà Lạt.
hook: The microscope that isolated Yersinia pestis, still on Trần Phú.
cardSummary: Compact upstairs museum inside the working Pasteur Institute. Wikipedia lists weekday hours around 08:00–11:00 and 14:00–16:30, closed weekends — confirm at the gate. Ticket often ~25–50,000 VND. Captions in French, English, and Vietnamese.
wikiAnchor: Alexandre Émile John Yersin (22 September 1863 – 1 March 1943) was a Swiss-French physician and bacteriologist. He is remembered for his work as a pioneer in microbiology and immunology. Yersin is the co-discoverer of both the Diphtheria and Tetanus toxins (1890 with Émile Roux) and of the bacillus responsible for the bubonic plague (1894, with Kitasato Shibasaburō). The bacteria was later named in his honour: Yersinia pestis. Yersin also demonstrated for the first time that the same bacillus was present in the rodent as well as in the human disease, thus underlining the possible means of transmission. Early life and education Yersin was born in 1863 in Aubonne, in the canton of Vaud, Switzerland, the youngest of three sons. His father, also named Alexandre (1825-1863), was the gunpowder superintendent for French-speaking Switzerland, based in La Vaux, in the Aubonne valley, and also a professor of natural sciences at the colleges of Aubonne and Morges and was passionate about studying insects. He died of a cerebral hemorrhage shortly before Alexandre's birth.
whyGo: The most interesting 45 minutes on the promenade that is not a beach.

name: Khanh Hoa Museum
keywords: Step into the provincial museum at 16 Trần Phú: Cham bricks and a Po Nagar model, bronze drums, wartime rooms, and roughly 10,000 objects that explain Khánh Hòa beyond the beach br
about: Step into the provincial museum at 16 Trần Phú: Cham bricks and a Po Nagar model, bronze drums, wartime rooms, and roughly 10,000 objects that explain Khánh Hòa beyond the beach brochure.
hook: Cham sculpture and provincial memory in a colonial townhouse.
cardSummary: Central Trần Phú museum in an early-20th-century building. Typically a morning weekday visit; hours and tickets change — check the door. One hour is enough. Combine with Yersin two blocks north, not a third indoor museum the same day.
whyGo: Context for Po Nagar without another hill climb.

name: Trầm Hương Tower (Incense / Lotus Tower)
keywords: Photograph and, when open, climb the six-storey orange-pink tower that became Nha Trang’s civic symbol after the 2004 “Hoa Biển” project opened in 2008 — agarwood (trầm hương) them
about: Photograph and, when open, climb the six-storey orange-pink tower that became Nha Trang’s civic symbol after the 2004 “Hoa Biển” project opened in 2008 — agarwood (trầm hương) themed galleries above the main beach junction.
hook: The pink lotus landmark on 2 Tháng 4 Square.
cardSummary: Iconic lotus/incense tower at Quảng trường 2/4 on Trần Phú. Exterior is free anytime; interior exhibits and hours vary by operator. Ten minutes for photos, longer if floors are open. Pair with the beach and night market, not a second architecture tower.
whyGo: The city’s logo in built form, right on the promenade.

name: Đố Theatre (Nhà hát Đố)
keywords: See the woven “đó” fish-trap silhouette at Vega City / Libera on Phạm Văn Đồng: a contemporary performance house facing Cô Tiên mountain and the bay, with paid evening shows (Rối M
about: See the woven “đó” fish-trap silhouette at Vega City / Libera on Phạm Văn Đồng: a contemporary performance house facing Cô Tiên mountain and the bay, with paid evening shows (Rối Mơ and similar) and a free daytime exterior.
hook: A fish-trap theatre on Bãi Tiên for puppet and water shows.
cardSummary: Architecture and show venue at Bãi Tiên, ~8–10 km north. Daytime photos are free; evening puppet/life-show tickets often 350,000–600,000 VND. Book the performance, not a “theatre museum.” Pair with Hòn Chồng on the same coastal road.
whyGo: The one purpose-built stage north of the city beach.

name: Truong Xuan Gallery
keywords: Browse rotating Vietnamese painting and mixed-media shows at Trường Xuân — a small Nha Trang gallery stop for travelers who want living artists, not Cham replicas in a hotel lobby.
about: Browse rotating Vietnamese painting and mixed-media shows at Trường Xuân — a small Nha Trang gallery stop for travelers who want living artists, not Cham replicas in a hotel lobby.
hook: A local contemporary gallery away from the souvenir strip.
cardSummary: Independent gallery; hours and hanging change with each show. Confirm the current address before you go — Nha Trang galleries move. Free to look, sales optional. Do not confuse it with the Trầm Hương Tower exhibition floors.
whyGo: Art without a ticketed “cultural village.”

name: Tri Nguyễn Aquarium (Hòn Miếu Pirate Ship)
keywords: Boat to Hòn Miếu for Trí Nguyên, the island aquarium built as a wrecked sailing ship: walk-through tanks and outdoor pools that have shown thousands of marine specimens since the m
about: Boat to Hòn Miếu for Trí Nguyên, the island aquarium built as a wrecked sailing ship: walk-through tanks and outdoor pools that have shown thousands of marine specimens since the mid-20th century site became a tourist fixture.
hook: A beached “pirate ship” full of tanks on Hòn Miếu.
cardSummary: On Hòn Miếu, usually bundled into bay boat tours from Cầu Đá. Island/beach tickets are separate from city museum prices. 45–75 minutes on site. The island card is Hòn Miếu; this card is the ship building. Do not pay twice for the same landing.
whyGo: The kitsch-and-fish island stop on the classic four-island loop.

name: Hòn Chồng Promontory
keywords: Walk the paved path through balanced granite boulders at Hòn Chồng–Hòn Vợ, 3–4 km north of the centre, for bay views toward Hòn Tre and a short beach.
about: Walk the paved path through balanced granite boulders at Hòn Chồng–Hòn Vợ, 3–4 km north of the centre, for bay views toward Hòn Tre and a short beach. The hill above holds Vietnam’s first astronomical observatory.
hook: Stacked granite fingers in the sea on the north shore.
cardSummary: Small ticketed cape on Phạm Văn Đồng. 45–75 minutes. Combine with Hòn Đỏ / Từ Tôn by boat, not with Ba Hồ the same morning unless you start very early. Sunrise and late afternoon beat midday glare.
whyGo: The easiest dramatic rock stop that is not a waterfall day.

name: Hòn Đỏ (Red Island Rocks)
keywords: Cross to the uninhabited red-rock islet that gives Hòn Đỏ its name.
about: Cross to the uninhabited red-rock islet that gives Hòn Đỏ its name. The geology is the sight; Từ Tôn pagoda occupies the same rock. Come for colour, swimming ledges, and a city-shore skyline, not a trek.
hook: A rust-red granite islet 300 metres off Hòn Chồng.
cardSummary: Same islet as Chùa Từ Tôn — one boat, two cards. Weather and tide decide access. Wear grip shoes; the rock is sharp. Do not book a separate “Red Island tour” if you already paid a Hòn Chồng canoe.
whyGo: The photogenic twin of Hòn Chồng, five minutes by boat.

name: Ba Hồ Waterfalls
keywords: Hike the boulder trail from Vạn Thuận (Ninh Hòa) up three swimming holes fed by Hòn Sơn.
about: Hike the boulder trail from Vạn Thuận (Ninh Hòa) up three swimming holes fed by Hòn Sơn. Pool one is an easy swim; pool two is a scramble; pool three is a further rocky push. “Ba Hồ” literally means three lakes.
hook: Three jungle pools on a granite stream 25 km north.
cardSummary: Ticketed eco site ~30–45 minutes north. Wear water shoes. Dry season can thin the falls; after rain the rocks are slick. Do not treat it as a boardwalk. Pair with Ninh Vân views on the coastal ride, not Yang Bay the same day.
whyGo: The real hike-and-swim day closest to the city beach.

name: Yang Bay Waterfall & Eco Park
keywords: Spend a developed eco-park day 45 km west in Khánh Vĩnh: Yang Bay (“heavenly waterfall” in Raglai) drops about 80 m into swim pools, with rafts, optional mineral soaks, and forest
about: Spend a developed eco-park day 45 km west in Khánh Vĩnh: Yang Bay (“heavenly waterfall” in Raglai) drops about 80 m into swim pools, with rafts, optional mineral soaks, and forest paths on a large ticketed campus.
hook: An 80-metre “heaven waterfall” in a 570-hectare Raglai valley.
cardSummary: Full half-day transfer. Adult tickets often ~150,000 VND plus extras. 08:00–17:00 typical. This is a park, not a secret cascade. Do not stack with Ba Hồ or Tà Gụ. Best in the wetter months if you want volume; paths get muddy.
whyGo: The waterfall-plus-facilities outing when Ba Hồ feels too raw.

name: Tà Gụ Waterfall
keywords: Commit to Khánh Sơn / Sơn Hiệp country for Tà Gụ, a ~40 m cascade sourced near 1,300 m on Hòn Bà.
about: Commit to Khánh Sơn / Sơn Hiệp country for Tà Gụ, a ~40 m cascade sourced near 1,300 m on Hòn Bà. White water on grey rock in primary forest — a long road day, not a Nha Trang afternoon.
hook: A 40-metre forest fall off Hòn Bà, far west of the city.
cardSummary: About 80–100 km west. Hire a driver; do not squeeze it after a beach morning. Facilities are thinner than Yang Bay. Wet season = more water and worse roads. One waterfall card per day.
whyGo: The remote fall if Yang Bay already felt too programmed.

name: Suối Thạch Lâm
keywords: Spend a lighter nature day ~20 km southwest at Waterland / Suối Thạch Lâm (open since 2011): Ngọc Lake, granite stream beds, and family play (paintball, grass sleds) under the Hòn
about: Spend a lighter nature day ~20 km southwest at Waterland / Suối Thạch Lâm (open since 2011): Ngọc Lake, granite stream beds, and family play (paintball, grass sleds) under the Hòn Bà massif.
hook: A 25-hectare stream park at the foot of Hòn Bà.
cardSummary: Ticketed eco park, not a wilderness reserve. Good with kids. Morning is cooler. Do not confuse it with Suối Mơ (a different eco zone) or Suối Tiên. Pair with a late beach, not another waterfall.
whyGo: Stream shade without Ba Hồ’s scramble.

name: Hòn Bà Nature Reserve
keywords: Drive the winding road into Khu bảo tồn thiên nhiên Hòn Bà for cool cloud forest, endemic plants, and a climate that feels closer to Đà Lạt than Trần Phú.
about: Drive the winding road into Khu bảo tồn thiên nhiên Hòn Bà for cool cloud forest, endemic plants, and a climate that feels closer to Đà Lạt than Trần Phú. This is a nature reserve, not a waterfall ticket booth.
hook: A 1,500-metre forest massif with highland air above the coast.
cardSummary: Protected forest southwest of Nha Trang. Access, gates, and research-station rules change — go with a licensed driver or tour. Fog and rain are common. Do not expect VinWonders facilities. Tà Gụ and Thạch Lâm sit on the same massif’s flanks.
whyGo: The altitude day when the city beach is 34 °C.

name: Nha Trang Beach (Trần Phú Beach)
keywords: Swim the municipal beach that made Nha Trang a resort city: pale sand, morning locals, loungers, and a steepish shore break in front of the hotel wall.
about: Swim the municipal beach that made Nha Trang a resort city: pale sand, morning locals, loungers, and a steepish shore break in front of the hotel wall. The promenade card is the walkway; this card is the water.
hook: The city’s 6 km crescent of sand in front of Trần Phú.
cardSummary: Free public beach along Trần Phú. Flags and currents matter; swim in front of lifeguards when posted. Sunrise and late afternoon beat midday tour buses. Distinct from the promenade card and from Bãi Dài in Cam Ranh.
whyGo: The default swim — no boat ticket required.

name: Bãi Dương Beach
keywords: Swim or walk Bãi Dương along Phạm Văn Đồng, the calmer urban beach north of the granite cape, with fewer hotel towers than Trần Phú and a view back to the bay islands.
about: Swim or walk Bãi Dương along Phạm Văn Đồng, the calmer urban beach north of the granite cape, with fewer hotel towers than Trần Phú and a view back to the bay islands.
hook: The quieter north-city sand past Hòn Chồng.
cardSummary: Free public/resort-adjacent beach on the north shore. Pair with Hòn Chồng. Not Dốc Lết (that is Ninh Hòa) and not Bãi Dài (Cam Ranh). Bring your own shade; facilities are thinner than the main strip.
whyGo: City sand without the Trần Phú speaker wall.

name: Dốc Lết Beach
keywords: Leave town for Dốc Lết in Ninh Hải — a long casuarina-backed strand about 50 km north, often sold with Điệp Sơn day tours, with shallow water and a “Hawaii of Vietnam” marketing li
about: Leave town for Dốc Lết in Ninh Hải — a long casuarina-backed strand about 50 km north, often sold with Điệp Sơn day tours, with shallow water and a “Hawaii of Vietnam” marketing line that oversells but the sand is real.
hook: Six kilometres of pale sand in Ninh Hòa, north of the city.
cardSummary: Half-day or full-day north. Some resort gates charge ~50,000 VND. Combine with Điệp Sơn if you already have a tour van; do not hire two cars. Not a Nha Trang city-beach substitute for a one-night stay.
whyGo: The wide, pale beach the city crescent cannot match.

name: Bãi Dài (Long Beach, Cam Ranh)
keywords: Ride south toward the airport peninsula for Bãi Dài — kilometres of open sand and resort gardens, quieter and windier than Trần Phú, used as a beach day when you have a Cam Ranh ar
about: Ride south toward the airport peninsula for Bãi Dài — kilometres of open sand and resort gardens, quieter and windier than Trần Phú, used as a beach day when you have a Cam Ranh arrival or an extra night.
hook: The long resort beach on the Cam Ranh peninsula.
cardSummary: 30–45 minutes south of central Nha Trang. Resort segments may charge for loungers. Free stretches exist. Do not confuse with Trần Phú Beach. Best as airport-day or resort-base swimming, not a third city-beach card.
whyGo: Space and a cleaner horizon than the city wall.

name: Hòn Tre Island (Bamboo Island)
keywords: Cross to Hòn Tre — Bamboo Island — on the ~3.
about: Cross to Hòn Tre — Bamboo Island — on the ~3.3 km Vinpearl gondola (a record-length sea cable when it opened in 2007). The island holds VinWonders, harbour town, beaches, and resorts; this card is the island crossing and shore, not the theme-park ticket.
hook: The big bay island at the end of the sea-crossing cable car.
cardSummary: Reached by cable car from the south mainland station (about 8 minutes) or boat in bad weather. Park tickets often include the gondola. If you only want the ride and a beach, look for cable-only or harbour products — do not buy VinWonders twice. Distinct from VinWonders and Vinpearl Harbour cards.
whyGo: The island itself: cable-car views and sand beyond the rides.

name: Hòn Tằm Island (Silkworm Island)
keywords: Boat to Hòn Tằm for a managed beach day: sand, lunch decks, and optional spa, sold as a quieter alternative to VinWonders.
about: Boat to Hòn Tằm for a managed beach day: sand, lunch decks, and optional spa, sold as a quieter alternative to VinWonders. The island name means silkworm; the product is a ticketed shore, not a village.
hook: A resort-and-beach islet 7 km off the city.
cardSummary: Boat from Cầu Đá or hotel pier. Adult island tickets often a few hundred thousand VND. Half day is enough. Combo tickets with VinWonders exist — read the date rules. Not Hòn Tre and not Hòn Mun.
whyGo: An island swim without a theme-park queue.

name: Hòn Mun Island (Ebony Island)
keywords: Snorkel or dive the reserve around Hòn Mun, named for dark volcanic rock.
about: Snorkel or dive the reserve around Hòn Mun, named for dark volcanic rock. Wikipedia notes it among the world’s early IUCN marine protected areas. The reef is pressured; some scuba was restricted after 2022 — ask operators what is currently allowed.
hook: Vietnam’s first marine protected area — black cliffs, clear water.
cardSummary: 15–20 minutes by speedboat from Cầu Đá, or 60–90 on a wooden day boat. A small marine-park fee is often bundled. The activity card “Hon Mun Island Snorkel” is the guided day; this card is the place. Book one, not both, for the same date.
whyGo: The marine-park island, not the generic “four islands” lunch stop.

name: Hòn Miếu Island
keywords: Land on Hòn Miếu, the inshore island south of Cầu Đá, for Bãi Tranh swimming and the Trí Nguyên ship aquarium.
about: Land on Hòn Miếu, the inshore island south of Cầu Đá, for Bãi Tranh swimming and the Trí Nguyên ship aquarium. Most four-island boats call here first because the crossing is short.
hook: The nearest inhabited island: aquarium ship and Bãi Tranh.
cardSummary: Boat from Cầu Đá. Beach and aquarium have separate or combo fees. The pirate-ship building is its own card. One landing is enough — do not buy a second “Hòn Miếu tour” after a four-island ticket.
whyGo: The easy island when you do not want Hòn Mun’s longer run.

name: Hòn Một Island
keywords: Stop at Hòn Một — “Island One” — a compact rock-and-reef landing used on classic bay loops, sometimes branded Coral Bay, with shorter swim time than Hòn Mun itself.
about: Stop at Hòn Một — “Island One” — a compact rock-and-reef landing used on classic bay loops, sometimes branded Coral Bay, with shorter swim time than Hòn Mun itself.
hook: A small snorkel islet on the way to Hòn Mun.
cardSummary: Almost always a stop on a multi-island boat, not a solo ferry. If your ticket already lists Hòn Mun + Hòn Một, do not add this as a second day. Reef quality varies; follow no-touch rules.
whyGo: The extra snorkel notch, not a destination you book alone.

name: Hòn Lao (Monkey Island)
keywords: Boat into Nha Phu Lagoon to Hòn Lao, marketed as Monkey Island: macaques, a beach, and a simple entertainment area.
about: Boat into Nha Phu Lagoon to Hòn Lao, marketed as Monkey Island: macaques, a beach, and a simple entertainment area. This is a ticketed wildlife-tourism island — keep food sealed and do not tease animals.
hook: A Nha Phu Bay islet sold for monkeys, beach, and a small show.
cardSummary: North of the city in Nha Phu Bay, often paired with Hoa Lan. Adult tickets often ~126,000 VND plus boat. Wildlife encounters can be stressful for animals and visitors. Skip if you dislike baited monkey tourism. Not Hòn Tre.
whyGo: Only if you want the classic “monkey island” boat, eyes open.

name: Đảo Hoa Lan (Orchid Island)
keywords: Visit Hoa Lan (Orchid Island / Suối Hoa Lan on some tickets) in the lagoon north of Nha Trang: a managed beach-and-garden island often combined with Hòn Lao, not the city-bay four-
about: Visit Hoa Lan (Orchid Island / Suối Hoa Lan on some tickets) in the lagoon north of Nha Trang: a managed beach-and-garden island often combined with Hòn Lao, not the city-bay four-island loop.
hook: A ticketed eco-islet in Nha Phu Bay.
cardSummary: Boat from the Nha Phu / Ninh Hòa side. Ticket often ~168,000 VND adult. Confirm whether “Hoa Lan” means this island or Suối Hoa Lan stream — operators reuse the name. Pair with Hòn Lao only if you want both north-bay stops in one van.
whyGo: A calmer north-bay island day if Hòn Tre is too much park.

name: Điệp Sơn Island (Sandbar Island)
keywords: Wade the famous shallow sandbar linking Điệp Sơn’s islets (Hòn Bịp, Hòn Giữa, Hòn Đuốc) in Vạn Ninh, about 60 km north.
about: Wade the famous shallow sandbar linking Điệp Sơn’s islets (Hòn Bịp, Hòn Giữa, Hòn Đuốc) in Vạn Ninh, about 60 km north. The path sits in ankle-to-knee water at typical tides — the photograph everyone comes for.
hook: A 700-metre sand path that walks you into Vân Phong Bay.
cardSummary: Full day from Nha Trang via Vạn Giã pier. Tide matters; ask before you book. Usually combined with Dốc Lết. Wear water shoes. This is Vân Phong, not Nha Trang Bay — do not expect a Hòn Mun coral garden.
whyGo: The sandbar, not another city-bay snorkel.

name: Ninh Vân Bay
keywords: Look down on Ninh Vân from the coastal road to Ba Hồ, or book a resort boat into the sheltered bay of white sand and boulder headlands.
about: Look down on Ninh Vân from the coastal road to Ba Hồ, or book a resort boat into the sheltered bay of white sand and boulder headlands. Six Senses and neighbours made the name; the seascape is older than the brands.
hook: A granite-backed luxury bay north of the city.
cardSummary: Resorts are boat-access and priced accordingly. Independent travelers can still stop at roadside viewpoints on the way to Ba Hồ. Do not expect a public city beach. Distinct from Vân Phong further north.
whyGo: The beautiful north bay — viewpoint cheap, beach stay expensive.

name: Vân Phong Bay
keywords: Travel north to Vân Phong — one of Vietnam’s large natural harbours — for empty-looking water, fishing towns, and the Điệp Sơn sandbar.
about: Travel north to Vân Phong — one of Vietnam’s large natural harbours — for empty-looking water, fishing towns, and the Điệp Sơn sandbar. Port and industrial plans keep changing the shoreline; the scale is the sight.
hook: A huge, still-developing bay that holds Điệp Sơn and Đầm Môn.
cardSummary: A region, not a single ticket booth. Most visitors see it via Điệp Sơn / Dốc Lết / Đầm Môn tours. Full day from the city. Do not book “Vân Phong” and “Điệp Sơn” as two separate products for the same water.
whyGo: The wide north seascape, not another Nha Trang Bay island loop.

name: VinWonders Nha Trang (Vinpearl Land)
keywords: Spend a full ticketed day on Hòn Tre at VinWonders (formerly Vinpearl Land, opened 2006): rides, Tropical Paradise water park, Sea World tunnel, King’s Garden, and night shows.
about: Spend a full ticketed day on Hòn Tre at VinWonders (formerly Vinpearl Land, opened 2006): rides, Tropical Paradise water park, Sea World tunnel, King’s Garden, and night shows. Round-trip cable car is usually included.
hook: Vietnam’s largest island theme park at the cable-car landing.
cardSummary: Standard adult tickets about 1,050,000 VND (2026 lists); after-16:00 is cheaper. Under ~100 cm often free. Hours have extended into the evening; cable often runs until 22:30. Do not also buy a separate Hòn Tre “island” product for the same date unless you only want the beach.
whyGo: The one all-day park if you have children or want the gondola bundled.

name: Vinpearl Harbor
keywords: Walk the purpose-built harbour district on Hòn Tre: dining streets, a night-market food row, go-karts and add-on shows.
about: Walk the purpose-built harbour district on Hòn Tre: dining streets, a night-market food row, go-karts and add-on shows. It sits beside VinWonders but is sold as its own cable + district ticket when you do not want the full park.
hook: Harbour town, night market, and shows on Hòn Tre.
cardSummary: Cheaper than VinWonders — cable + harbour products often ~190–300,000 VND. Tata Show and karts are extras. Same gondola as the park. If you already hold a VinWonders ticket, this is usually included or adjacent — do not double-pay.
whyGo: Island evening without a ride-park wristband.

name: Tháp Bà Hot Springs & Mud Bath
keywords: Soak in the Tháp Bà (Lady Tower) springs northwest of the Cham towers: sodium-silicate water from about 38–72 °C, communal or private mud tubs, then mineral pools.
about: Soak in the Tháp Bà (Lady Tower) springs northwest of the Cham towers: sodium-silicate water from about 38–72 °C, communal or private mud tubs, then mineral pools. One of Vietnam’s first commercial hot-spring parks.
hook: The original 1994 mineral-mud complex behind Po Nagar.
cardSummary: Open roughly 07:00–19:30. Packages from about 120,000–500,000 VND depending on private tubs. Bring a swimsuit you do not mind staining. Shower before pools. Pair with morning Po Nagar — same taxi, different ticket. Not I-Resort.
whyGo: The mud afternoon that sits next to the Cham towers.

name: I-Resort Mud Bath
keywords: Spend a half-day at I-Resort’s outdoor mud tubs under trees, mineral waterfalls, and swimming pools on the north-west edge of town — a more landscaped, family-scale alternative to
about: Spend a half-day at I-Resort’s outdoor mud tubs under trees, mineral waterfalls, and swimming pools on the north-west edge of town — a more landscaped, family-scale alternative to Tháp Bà’s older site.
hook: The larger mineral campus in Vĩnh Ngọc: mud, falls, and pools.
cardSummary: Vĩnh Ngọc, inland. Water-park tickets often ~170,000 VND; shared mud ~260,000; private tubs more. Hours commonly 07:00–20:00. Pick one mud complex per trip. Swimsuit, flip-flops, and a lock for valuables.
whyGo: Mud plus a proper swim park if Tháp Bà looks cramped.

name: 100 Egg Mud Bath (Khu Du Lịch Trăm Trứng)
keywords: Sit in the trademark oval “egg” tubs at Trăm Trứng in Phước Đồng — a cheaper, photogenic mud park on the south highway, with mineral soak and simple grounds rather than I-Resort’s
about: Sit in the trademark oval “egg” tubs at Trăm Trứng in Phước Đồng — a cheaper, photogenic mud park on the south highway, with mineral soak and simple grounds rather than I-Resort’s scale.
hook: Egg-shaped mud pods on Nguyễn Tất Thành.
cardSummary: Adult entry often ~120,000 VND. South of the centre toward the airport road. One mud card is enough for a short trip — do not do Tháp Bà, I-Resort, and Trăm Trứng. Eggs are shared or semi-private depending on package.
whyGo: The budget, Instagram mud stop.

name: Suối Mơ Eco Tourism Zone
keywords: Spend a low-key family day at Suối Mơ — Dream Stream — an eco-tourism zone of shallow water, picnic lawns, and simple play, used by Nha Trang residents more than island-boat touris
about: Spend a low-key family day at Suối Mơ — Dream Stream — an eco-tourism zone of shallow water, picnic lawns, and simple play, used by Nha Trang residents more than island-boat tourists.
hook: A local stream-and-garden park west of the city.
cardSummary: Inland eco park, not Suối Thạch Lâm and not Suối Tiên. Ticket and ride extras vary. Morning is cooler. Good with kids; skip if you already booked Yang Bay. Bring cash and mosquito repellent.
whyGo: Shade and freshwater when you are tired of salt and tickets.

name: Trần Phú Boulevard Promenade
keywords: Walk Trần Phú’s paved promenade along the crescent: sunrise exercisers, hotel terraces, Trầm Hương Tower at 2/4 Square, and evening lights.
about: Walk Trần Phú’s paved promenade along the crescent: sunrise exercisers, hotel terraces, Trầm Hương Tower at 2/4 Square, and evening lights. This is the boulevard, not the swimming-beach card.
hook: The long seaside walk from morning swimmers to neon.
cardSummary: Free, flat, and usable at any hour. Best at sunrise and after 17:00. The beach card is for swimming; this card is for walking, cafés, and night air. Links Yersin, the tower, and the night market without a Grab.
whyGo: The city’s free everyday coastal street — orientation for everything else.

name: Đầm Market (Chợ Đầm)
keywords: Move through Chợ Đầm, Nha Trang’s main multi-storey market: produce, dry goods, cheap clothes, and a food wing that still feeds locals.
about: Move through Chợ Đầm, Nha Trang’s main multi-storey market: produce, dry goods, cheap clothes, and a food wing that still feeds locals. It is a working hall, not a designed night bazaar.
hook: The city’s big covered market behind the station quarter.
cardSummary: Free to walk; you pay for goods. Morning is for produce; later floors skew souvenir. Watch bags and wet floors. Distinct from Xóm Mới (more local wet market) and the beach night market. Agree prices before juices.
whyGo: The real central market — fruit, coffee, and bargaining practice.

name: Xóm Mới Market
keywords: Eat at Chợ Xóm Mới, the local market west of the tourist beach where residents shop fish, herbs, and morning soup.
about: Eat at Chợ Xóm Mới, the local market west of the tourist beach where residents shop fish, herbs, and morning soup. Bún cá and bánh canh stalls here are the practical order, not lacquer boxes.
hook: The neighborhood wet market for bún cá and breakfast.
cardSummary: Free to enter. Go early; many stalls close by late morning. Cash, small bills. Not Chợ Đầm and not the night market. Keep a low profile with cameras around butchers. Pair with Long Sơn, which sits closer than the beach hotels imply.
whyGo: Breakfast with locals instead of another hotel buffet.

name: Nha Trang Night Market
keywords: Wander the night market that sets up along Trần Phú and the streets behind the hotel wall: grilled seafood, cheap clothes, and souvenirs aimed at walkers coming off the promenade.
about: Wander the night market that sets up along Trần Phú and the streets behind the hotel wall: grilled seafood, cheap clothes, and souvenirs aimed at walkers coming off the promenade. It is seasonal in density, not a historic covered hall.
hook: Evening stalls along the beach boulevard.
cardSummary: Free to walk; pay for food. Typically from dusk. Bargain, check seafood weight, and keep bags zipped. Distinct from Đầm Market (day hall) and Vinpearl Harbour’s island night row. Pair with the promenade and Trầm Hương lights.
whyGo: The easy evening graze after a swim — not Chợ Đầm.

name: Skylight Nha Trang (360° Skydeck, Havana Hotel)
keywords: Ride to the Havana Hotel skydeck — Skylight’s glass-walled bar and outdoor platforms — for a paid sunset circuit of the bay, Hòn Tre, and the Trần Phú grid.
about: Ride to the Havana Hotel skydeck — Skylight’s glass-walled bar and outdoor platforms — for a paid sunset circuit of the bay, Hòn Tre, and the Trần Phú grid. The product is the view and a drink minimum, not a museum.
hook: A rooftop 360° deck over the crescent beach.
cardSummary: Ticket or drink-minimum entry; prices change with happy hour. Dress code is smart-casual. Sunset books out — go 45 minutes early. Not a substitute for Long Sơn’s hill. Combine with the promenade below, not VinWonders the same exhausted evening.
whyGo: The city’s highest public-ish viewpoint without a hike.

name: Cái Răng Floating Market
keywords: Ride ~6 km south of Ninh Kiều to the delta’s largest working floating market: produce boats, a sample hung on a bamboo pole, and kitchen sampans selling hủ tiếu and coffee.
about: Ride ~6 km south of Ninh Kiều to the delta’s largest working floating market: produce boats, a sample hung on a bamboo pole, and kitchen sampans selling hủ tiếu and coffee. The Ministry of Culture recognised the market; it is a river, not a ticket booth.
hook: Dawn wholesale boats on the Hậu, poles hung with fruit.
cardSummary: Peak 05:30–07:30; empty after 09:00. No entry fee — pay the boat from Ninh Kiều (shared often 50–150k VND/person; private a few hundred thousand). Book the night before. The mekong-delta card is the late packaged tour; do not buy both for the same dawn.
whyGo: The reason to sleep in Cần Thơ instead of a Saigon day bus.

name: Phong Điền Floating Market
keywords: Go ~17 km southwest into Phong Điền for a smaller wholesale gathering on narrow canals.
about: Go ~17 km southwest into Phong Điền for a smaller wholesale gathering on narrow canals. More vendors live aboard; fewer tour boats. Peak is often 04:30–06:30 — earlier and shorter than Cái Răng.
hook: The quieter canal market, earlier and more local than Cái Răng.
cardSummary: Motorbike ~30–40 minutes or a longer private boat from Ninh Kiều. Combo boats covering both markets cost more and risk arriving late to one of them. Pick one dawn. Pair with Mỹ Khánh or Trúc Lâm in Phong Điền after breakfast.
whyGo: The second-morning market if Cái Răng already felt crowded.

name: Ninh Kiều Wharf (Bến Ninh Kiều)
keywords: Use Bến Ninh Kiều as Cần Thơ’s river hub: 05:00 longtails for Cái Răng, sunset over the Hậu, and the night-market edge.
about: Use Bến Ninh Kiều as Cần Thơ’s river hub: 05:00 longtails for Cái Răng, sunset over the Hậu, and the night-market edge. It is a working pier and park, not a single monument.
hook: The Hậu River square where dawn boats and evening lights meet.
cardSummary: Free, 24 hours. Book floating-market boats here the evening before. The Love Bridge, old market, and Chùa Ông are a short walk. Distinct from the bridge card and the night-market card — one evening stroll covers all three.
whyGo: Orientation for every other city card.

name: Mới Canal (Rạch Mới)
keywords: Drift or cycle Rạch Mới, one of the city’s named canals: stilt houses, orchards, and small boats.
about: Drift or cycle Rạch Mới, one of the city’s named canals: stilt houses, orchards, and small boats. Operators sometimes add it after Cái Răng when the wholesale is already over.
hook: A working side canal, not a second floating market.
cardSummary: No ticket booth — boat or xe ôm along the bank. Ask the Ninh Kiều driver to include it only if you have leftover morning. Not Phong Điền and not Cái Răng. Mosquitoes after rain.
whyGo: River texture without another 05:00 alarm.

name: Ông Temple (Chùa Ông – Quảng Đông Assembly Hall)
keywords: Step into the 1894–96 Quảng Đông (Quảng Triệu) assembly hall at about 32 Hai Bà Trưng: carved wood, red lanterns, and a sanctuary to Quan Công used by Cần Thơ’s Hoa community.
about: Step into the 1894–96 Quảng Đông (Quảng Triệu) assembly hall at about 32 Hai Bà Trưng: carved wood, red lanterns, and a sanctuary to Quan Công used by Cần Thơ’s Hoa community. It is a hội quán, not a Khmer wat.
hook: Cantonese incense and Quan Công on Hai Bà Trưng.
cardSummary: Free (donation). Cover shoulders. Combine with Chợ Cổ and Ninh Kiều on foot. Not Munir Ansay and not Nam Nhã. Festivals around Quan Công’s days fill the courtyard.
whyGo: The city’s Chinese hall, two minutes from the old market.

name: Nam Nhã Pagoda
keywords: Visit Nam Nhã Đường on the Bình Thủy River (612 Cách Mạng Tháng 8): founded in 1895 by Nguyễn Giác Nguyên as a Minh Sư hall and later a liaison point for Hậu Giang and Nam Kỳ organ
about: Visit Nam Nhã Đường on the Bình Thủy River (612 Cách Mạng Tháng 8): founded in 1895 by Nguyễn Giác Nguyên as a Minh Sư hall and later a liaison point for Hậu Giang and Nam Kỳ organisers. Rebuilt 1917; yellow Franco-Asian halls. Ranked a historic site.
hook: An 1895 river pagoda that hid patriot networks.
cardSummary: Free, typically 07:00–17:00. 30–45 minutes. ~6 km from Ninh Kiều. Pair with the ancient house — same district, different ticket. Boat tours can stop if you ask. Dress modestly; this is still a working temple.
whyGo: The political pagoda next to Bình Thủy Ancient House.

name: Phước Hậu Pagoda
keywords: Pay respects at Chùa Phước Hậu, a local Bắc tông monastery in greater Cần Thơ — incense halls and a courtyard used by neighbourhood Buddhists rather than dawn-market groups.
about: Pay respects at Chùa Phước Hậu, a local Bắc tông monastery in greater Cần Thơ — incense halls and a courtyard used by neighbourhood Buddhists rather than dawn-market groups.
hook: A working southern Mahayana pagoda away from the pier touts.
cardSummary: Free, donation. Confirm the current ward address — the name is reused in the delta (including Trà Vinh). Not the Khmer wats. Cover shoulders. 20–40 minutes.
whyGo: A quiet temple stop when Chùa Ông is packed.

name: Chùa Pôthi SômRôn (Khmer Pagoda)
keywords: Ride out to Pôthi SômRôn (Pothi Somron), a Theravāda Khmer monastery in Ô Môn: pointed roofs, coloured prang details, and a village wat rhythm rather than a city-boulevard façade.
about: Ride out to Pôthi SômRôn (Pothi Somron), a Theravāda Khmer monastery in Ô Môn: pointed roofs, coloured prang details, and a village wat rhythm rather than a city-boulevard façade.
hook: A rural Khmer wat in Ô Môn, older and quieter than Munir Ansay.
cardSummary: Free, modest dress. Do not visit both Khmer pagodas back-to-back unless you care about comparison. Ô Môn is a Grab, not a promenade stroll. Ask before photographing monks or schoolchildren.
whyGo: The countryside Khmer card; Munir Ansay is the in-town one.

name: Chùa Munir Ansay (Khmer Pagoda)
keywords: Walk to Munirensay / Munir Ansay at 36 Đại lộ Hoà Bình: one of Cần Thơ’s largest in-town Khmer pagodas, with bright Theravāda roofs and a community wat used for festivals as well a
about: Walk to Munirensay / Munir Ansay at 36 Đại lộ Hoà Bình: one of Cần Thơ’s largest in-town Khmer pagodas, with bright Theravāda roofs and a community wat used for festivals as well as daily chanting.
hook: The city’s main Khmer wat on Hoà Bình, founded 1948.
cardSummary: Free. Cover shoulders and knees. 30–45 minutes. Pair with Cần Thơ Museum on the same avenue. Pôthi SômRôn is the rural counterpart — pick one unless you have a Khmer-architecture morning. Not Chùa Ông.
whyGo: Khmer architecture without leaving Ninh Kiều.

name: Quang Đức Pagoda
keywords: Visit Chùa Quang Đức at 146 Mậu Thân, An Phú: founded by Thích Bửu Lai in 1958 and restored in 2006.
typical hours Daily; ceremony times vary
about: Visit Chùa Quang Đức at 146 Mậu Thân, An Phú: founded by Thích Bửu Lai in 1958 and restored in 2006. Southern Mahayana halls, a prominent gate, and neighbourhood sermons — not the Khmer street.
hook: A 1958 Bắc tông pagoda on Mậu Thân with a tall tam quan.
cardSummary: Free, ~2 km from Ninh Kiều. Do not confuse with the self-immolation monk Thích Quảng Đức’s memorials in Saigon — this is a different dedication. 30 minutes. One Mahayana + one Khmer + Ông is enough for a temple day.
whyGo: The in-city Vietnamese pagoda if you already did Ông and Munir.

name: Thiền Viện Trúc Lâm Phương Nam
keywords: Spend a quieter hour at Trúc Lâm Phương Nam on TL 923 in Mỹ Khánh, Phong Điền: a southern branch of the Trúc Lâm zen lineage — broad courtyards, a tall Buddha, and lotus ponds abou
about: Spend a quieter hour at Trúc Lâm Phương Nam on TL 923 in Mỹ Khánh, Phong Điền: a southern branch of the Trúc Lâm zen lineage — broad courtyards, a tall Buddha, and lotus ponds about 10–15 km from Ninh Kiều.
hook: A large Trúc Lâm zen campus in Mỹ Khánh countryside.
cardSummary: Free, modest dress. Pair with Mỹ Khánh eco-village next door, not with a second zen campus. Morning is cooler. This is not Trúc Lâm Đà Lạt. Do not expect a floating-market boat here.
whyGo: The monastery scale that city wats cannot match.

name: Cần Thơ Cathedral (Giáo xứ Chính Tòa)
keywords: Walk to the mother parish of the Diocese of Cần Thơ — Giáo xứ Chính Tòa — a colonial-era Catholic landmark among the museum avenue and government buildings, used for Mass more than
about: Walk to the mother parish of the Diocese of Cần Thơ — Giáo xứ Chính Tòa — a colonial-era Catholic landmark among the museum avenue and government buildings, used for Mass more than for tour groups.
hook: The diocesan church in the Hoà Bình civic grid.
cardSummary: Free courtyard. Quiet if Mass is on. Combine with Cần Thơ Museum and Military Zone 9 on Hoà Bình. Not a river sunset stop. Dress for a working church.
whyGo: The Christian counterpoint to Ông, Munir, and Quang Đức.

name: Bình Thủy Ancient House
keywords: Tour Nhà cổ Bình Thủy on Bùi Hữu Nghĩa: a ~150-year mix of French colonial and Nam Bộ woodwork, high ceilings, and a courtyard still associated with the Dương lineage and period fi
about: Tour Nhà cổ Bình Thủy on Bùi Hữu Nghĩa: a ~150-year mix of French colonial and Nam Bộ woodwork, high ceilings, and a courtyard still associated with the Dương lineage and period films including The Lover.
hook: An 1870s Dương-family timber house used as a film set.
cardSummary: About 15–20,000 VND. Hours commonly 08:00–12:00 and 14:00–18:00. ~8 km / 20 minutes. Pair with Nam Nhã Pagoda. Interiors are dim — no flash on lacquer. Not a floating-market substitute.
whyGo: The one historic house that earns a Grab from Ninh Kiều.

name: Cần Thơ Grand Prison (Khám Lớn / Nhà Tù Cần Thơ)
keywords: Walk 8 Ngô Gia Tự to Khám Lớn Cần Thơ — Prison Provinciale, built 1876–86 beside the old provincial compound (now the city People’s Committee).
about: Walk 8 Ngô Gia Tự to Khám Lớn Cần Thơ — Prison Provinciale, built 1876–86 beside the old provincial compound (now the city People’s Committee). Cells, watch posts, and later RVN “trại cải huấn” rooms document political imprisonment in the west delta.
hook: The 1886 French provincial prison, now a national relic.
cardSummary: National historic site; display access can vary — check the gate. Free or a small fee when open. Not a theme-park jail. Pair with Cần Thơ Museum. Quiet, no costume photos.
whyGo: The city’s hardest history, five minutes from the river.

name: Cần Thơ Museum
keywords: Visit Bảo tàng Cần Thơ at 1 Đại lộ Hoà Bình: founded 1976, rebuilt and reopened 31 August 2000 on about 3,000 m², with Kinh, Hoa, and Khmer rooms and the city’s civic story.
typical hours Typical museum weekday hours (confirm)
about: Visit Bảo tàng Cần Thơ at 1 Đại lộ Hoà Bình: founded 1976, rebuilt and reopened 31 August 2000 on about 3,000 m², with Kinh, Hoa, and Khmer rooms and the city’s civic story.
hook: The largest provincial museum campus in the delta, on Hoà Bình.
cardSummary: Central, often a small or free ticket. Weekday mornings are safest. One hour. Combine with Munir Ansay and Military Zone 9 on the same avenue. Not the HCM wing — that is next door on the military campus.
whyGo: Context for the river you just rode at dawn.

name: Military Zone 9 Museum
keywords: Walk 6 Đại lộ Hoà Bình for Bảo tàng Quân khu 9: tens of thousands of documents on the southwest front, outdoor armour, and chronological rooms.
about: Walk 6 Đại lộ Hoà Bình for Bảo tàng Quân khu 9: tens of thousands of documents on the southwest front, outdoor armour, and chronological rooms. Free on typical listings; often closed weekends, open ~07:30–11:00 and 13:30–16:30.
hook: The Mekong armed-forces museum on Hoà Bình, opened 1979.
cardSummary: Free when open. The Hồ Chí Minh Museum Cần Thơ branch is a wing of this campus — one visit covers both cards. Do not expect Hanoi’s military museum scale. Pair with Cần Thơ Museum 450 m away.
whyGo: Local war history without flying back to the War Remnants Museum.

name: Hồ Chí Minh Museum (Cần Thơ Branch)
keywords: See the Cần Thơ branch of the Hồ Chí Minh Museum — rooms on his life and the delta’s relationship with him, including the “Studying Uncle Hồ” civic display — inside 6 Hoà Bình, not
typical hours Same as Military Zone 9 Museum
about: See the Cần Thơ branch of the Hồ Chí Minh Museum — rooms on his life and the delta’s relationship with him, including the “Studying Uncle Hồ” civic display — inside 6 Hoà Bình, not a separate river site.
hook: The 1990 HCM galleries inside the Military Zone 9 campus.
cardSummary: Same gate as Military Zone 9 Museum. Established 1990 as a wing. One ticket/visit. Do not take a second Grab. Smaller than the Hà Nội HCM complex.
whyGo: Only if you are already in Quân khu 9.

name: Bằng Lăng Stork Sanctuary
keywords: Go ~60 km north to Vườn cò Bằng Lăng in Thuận An, Thốt Nốt: a sanctuary grown since 1983 on about 1.
about: Go ~60 km north to Vườn cò Bằng Lăng in Thuận An, Thốt Nốt: a sanctuary grown since 1983 on about 1.65 hectares of grove, now one of the delta’s best-known stork gardens, with 20+ waterbird species returning at dusk.
hook: Tens of thousands of storks over Thốt Nốt bamboo and rice.
cardSummary: Tickets often 10–20,000 VND. Be there 06:00–07:00 as birds leave, or ~17:00 as they return. Full half-day from Ninh Kiều. Do not use drones over nests. Not Lung Ngọc Hoàng (that is a wetland reserve).
whyGo: The bird evening that is not an orchard lunch.

name: Sơn Islet (Cồn Sơn)
keywords: Boat to Cồn Sơn, a Hậu River islet run as a community tourism village: orchards, folk cakes, and the well-known cá lóc bay feeding.
about: Boat to Cồn Sơn, a Hậu River islet run as a community tourism village: orchards, folk cakes, and the well-known cá lóc bay feeding. Closer and more programmed than Lung Ngọc Hoàng.
hook: Community tourism, fruit, and the “flying” snakehead show.
cardSummary: Boat from Ninh Kiều or a combined garden tour. Fees for gardens and the fish show are separate. Half day. Cồn Ấu and Cồn Khương are quieter siblings — do not book three islet tickets. Ask to skip souvenir workshops you do not want.
whyGo: The islet day most visitors actually take.

name: Ấu Islet (Cồn Ấu)
keywords: Cross to Cồn Ấu for a slower river-island walk: local gardens and views back to the city shore without Cồn Sơn’s fish-show circuit.
