about: Cross to Cồn Ấu for a slower river-island walk: local gardens and views back to the city shore without Cồn Sơn’s fish-show circuit.
hook: The quieter Hậu islet — gardens and houses, fewer shows.
cardSummary: Boat from the city front. Facilities thinner than Cồn Sơn. One islet per day. Not Cái Khế (the sandbar off the Love Bridge).
whyGo: An islet if you already did the community-tourism script.

name: Khương Islet (Cồn Khương)
keywords: Visit Cồn Khương for the third of the inner-city Hậu islets: fruit trees, river wind, and less signage than Cồn Sơn.
about: Visit Cồn Khương for the third of the inner-city Hậu islets: fruit trees, river wind, and less signage than Cồn Sơn. Good when a boatman offers a multi-cồn loop and you only want one extra stop.
hook: Another Hậu sand-islet of orchards and quiet houses.
cardSummary: Negotiate as an add-on, not a separate tour company. Same river as Cồn Sơn / Cồn Ấu. Do not stack all three after a 05:00 market.
whyGo: Only as a second islet, not a third full product.

name: Mỹ Khánh Eco-Tourism Village
keywords: Spend a ticketed afternoon at Làng du lịch Mỹ Khánh (335 Lộ Vòng Cung): orchards, folk games, animals, and snack stalls aimed at families — useful if you cannot string real gardens
about: Spend a ticketed afternoon at Làng du lịch Mỹ Khánh (335 Lộ Vòng Cung): orchards, folk games, animals, and snack stalls aimed at families — useful if you cannot string real gardens yourself.
hook: A 20-hectare “delta in miniature” in Phong Điền.
cardSummary: Adult tickets often ~70,000 VND. This is a tourist village, not a farmer’s backyard. Pair with the zen monastery. Do not also pay for Giọt Đắng and Ba Láng the same afternoon unless you love fruit.
whyGo: The easy orchard park next to Trúc Lâm Phương Nam.

name: Giọt Đắng / Chín Hồng Fruit Orchard
keywords: Sit down at Giọt Đắng or Chín Hồng — two well-known Phong Điền / canal-side orchards sold as garden restaurants.
typical hours Lunch service; season matters
about: Sit down at Giọt Đắng or Chín Hồng — two well-known Phong Điền / canal-side orchards sold as garden restaurants. Season runs hardest May–August (rambutan, mangosteen, durian, longan); other months are thinner.
hook: Named miệt-vườn tables: pick, taste, and lunch under fruit.
cardSummary: One orchard booking. Confirm which garden the driver means — both names appear on menus. You pay for food and fruit, not a monument ticket. Pair with Phong Điền, not with three other garden cards.
whyGo: A real orchard lunch, not only Mỹ Khánh’s ticketed path.

name: Ba Láng Fruit Gardens
keywords: Stop in Ba Láng (Cái Răng) for smallholder fruit gardens that boatmen add after the floating market: longan, mango, and seasonal tasting tables on the same water as the wholesale.
about: Stop in Ba Láng (Cái Răng) for smallholder fruit gardens that boatmen add after the floating market: longan, mango, and seasonal tasting tables on the same water as the wholesale.
hook: Canal orchards on the Cái Răng side of town.
cardSummary: Usually bundled on the Cái Răng boat. Agree the extra before you leave Ninh Kiều. Not Mỹ Khánh and not Giọt Đắng. Tip the garden, eat what is in season, skip the coconut-candy hard sell if you already saw one.
whyGo: The orchard that does not need a Phong Điền transfer.

name: Lung Ngọc Hoàng Nature Reserve
keywords: Commit to Khu bảo tồn thiên nhiên Lung Ngọc Hoàng in Phương Bình (formerly Hậu Giang, now in the Cần Thơ city map after merger): core swamp forest, bird lungs, and a developing eco
about: Commit to Khu bảo tồn thiên nhiên Lung Ngọc Hoàng in Phương Bình (formerly Hậu Giang, now in the Cần Thơ city map after merger): core swamp forest, bird lungs, and a developing eco-tourism scheme. This is a reserve, not a stork garden.
hook: A 2,800-hectare tràm wetland — the west Hậu “green lung.”
cardSummary: Full day, licensed access; core zone is restricted. Not Bằng Lăng (Thốt Nốt storks) and not Mỹ Khánh. Bring repellent and expect mud. Confirm the current visitor gate — rules shift with the eco-tourism plan.
whyGo: The wild wetland if Bằng Lăng already felt like a grove park.

name: Ninh Kiều Pedestrian Bridge (Love Bridge)
keywords: Walk Cầu đi bộ Ninh Kiều — Cầu Tình Yêu — about 200 m of LED-lit S-curve over Rạch Khai Luông, opened February 2016, linking the wharf park to Cái Khế’s play shore.
about: Walk Cầu đi bộ Ninh Kiều — Cầu Tình Yêu — about 200 m of LED-lit S-curve over Rạch Khai Luông, opened February 2016, linking the wharf park to Cái Khế’s play shore. Free, 24 hours.
hook: The 2016 S-curve footbridge to Cồn Cái Khế.
cardSummary: Free. Best after 18:00 when the lights are on. Same stroll as the wharf and night market — do not give it a separate taxi. Not Cầu Cần Thơ (the big cable-stayed highway bridge).
whyGo: The city’s evening photograph, not a second river tour.

name: Cần Thơ Bridge (Cầu Cần Thơ)
keywords: Look at Cầu Cần Thơ, the cable-stayed highway bridge opened in 2010 after a long construction (and a fatal 2007 collapse during building).
about: Look at Cầu Cần Thơ, the cable-stayed highway bridge opened in 2010 after a long construction (and a fatal 2007 collapse during building). It is the city’s modern skyline mark, not a pedestrian deck like the Love Bridge.
hook: The 2010 cable-stayed span that replaced the Hậu ferry.
cardSummary: View from Ninh Kiều, a river boat, or the approach roads. You cannot treat it as a walking tour. Distinct from Cầu Tình Yêu. Night lighting photographs well from the wharf.
whyGo: The civic landmark you see from the river, not a stroll.

name: Cần Thơ Market (Chợ Cổ / Old Market)
keywords: Walk the old Cần Thơ market building — also called Chợ Hàng Dương — produce, dry goods, and a tiled hall that still feeds the city by day.
about: Walk the old Cần Thơ market building — also called Chợ Hàng Dương — produce, dry goods, and a tiled hall that still feeds the city by day. The same waterfront becomes night stalls; this card is the morning hall.
hook: The historic riverside market hall on Hai Bà Trưng.
cardSummary: Free to walk. Morning for fruit and hủ tiếu. The night-market and Tây Đô cards are the evening version of this shore — do not plan three separate market expeditions. Watch bags and wet floors.
whyGo: Daytime market life, two minutes from Chùa Ông.

name: Cần Thơ Night Market
keywords: Eat through the night stalls that fill Hai Bà Trưng and the wharf edge after dusk: grilled skewers, fruit, and cheap clothes.
about: Eat through the night stalls that fill Hai Bà Trưng and the wharf edge after dusk: grilled skewers, fruit, and cheap clothes. Locals also call this stretch Chợ đêm Ninh Kiều.
hook: Evening food and souvenirs along the Ninh Kiều shore.
cardSummary: Free to walk, roughly 17:00–23:00. Tây Đô Market is the branded name for the same waterfront night bazaar — one evening. Bargain, check seafood weight. Pair with the promenade, not a second taxi to “another night market.”
whyGo: The easy dinner walk after the Love Bridge lights.

name: Tây Đô Market
keywords: Use “Chợ đêm Tây Đô” as the evening identity of the renovated riverside market (also Hàng Dương / Chợ Cần Thơ after 2005): tiled roofs, lights, fruit, and clothes facing Hai Bà Trư
about: Use “Chợ đêm Tây Đô” as the evening identity of the renovated riverside market (also Hàng Dương / Chợ Cần Thơ after 2005): tiled roofs, lights, fruit, and clothes facing Hai Bà Trưng and the river.
hook: The branded night bazaar name for the Hậu waterfront hall.
cardSummary: Same shore as the night-market card. One visit. Daytime use the Old Market card. Official tourism pages treat the names as aliases. Do not pay a guide for “three markets” on one street.
whyGo: Only as a name check — it is the same night as Cần Thơ Night Market.

name: Lưu Hữu Phước Park
keywords: Walk Công viên Lưu Hữu Phước, Cần Thơ’s central green named after the musician Lưu Hữu Phước: shade, morning exercise, and a pause between Hoà Bình museums and the stadium quarter.
about: Walk Công viên Lưu Hữu Phước, Cần Thơ’s central green named after the musician Lưu Hữu Phước: shade, morning exercise, and a pause between Hoà Bình museums and the stadium quarter.
hook: The civic park named for the composer, inland from the river.
cardSummary: Free, anytime. Morning tai chi, late-afternoon shade. Distinct from Sông Hậu Park on the river. Pair with the museum avenue. Not a ticketed garden.
whyGo: A free sit-down that is not the tourist wharf.

name: Sông Hậu Park
keywords: Sit in Công viên Sông Hậu along the city bank: breeze, bridge views, and the same evening crowd that uses Ninh Kiều.
about: Sit in Công viên Sông Hậu along the city bank: breeze, bridge views, and the same evening crowd that uses Ninh Kiều. It is the park layer of the waterfront, not a separate destination across town.
hook: The river-edge lawn in front of the Hậu.
cardSummary: Free. Same evening as the Love Bridge and wharf. Do not Uber here as a third “park” after Lưu Hữu Phước unless you want contrast (river vs inland). Best at sunset.
whyGo: The grass and view if the night-market aisle is too loud.

name: Ma Pi Leng Pass
keywords: Ride Đèo Mã Pì Lèng between Đồng Văn and Mèo Vạc — the dramatic shelf of Hạnh Phúc Road, built by volunteer labour through the karst.
about: Ride Đèo Mã Pì Lèng between Đồng Văn and Mèo Vạc — the dramatic shelf of Hạnh Phúc Road, built by volunteer labour through the karst. Designated pull-offs look into Tu Sản canyon; the optional Sky Walk is a separate exposed path.
hook: The Happiness Road cut above the Nho Que gorge.
cardSummary: No gate ticket for the road. Stop only in bays — never in the carriageway. Fog and gravel kill. The Nho Que boat and Tu Sản viewpoint are the same gorge family; do not stack a rushed boat if you will still be on the pass at dusk. The ha-giang-loop card is the day product, not a second pass.
whyGo: The loop’s defining pass — one slow crossing, not a race.

name: Dong Van Karst Plateau Geopark
keywords: Understand Cao nguyên đá Đồng Văn as a 2,356 km² UNESCO Global Geopark (2010) covering Quản Bạ, Yên Minh, Đồng Văn, and Mèo Vạc — limestone peaks, fossil beds, and inhabited corn t
about: Understand Cao nguyên đá Đồng Văn as a 2,356 km² UNESCO Global Geopark (2010) covering Quản Bạ, Yên Minh, Đồng Văn, and Mèo Vạc — limestone peaks, fossil beds, and inhabited corn terraces, not a single ticket booth.
hook: UNESCO Global Geopark across four highland districts.
cardSummary: Overnight stays in the four districts may be charged a geopark visitor fee (listings ~30,000 VND/adult/night). The dong-van city card is the same plateau overnight. Individual sites (Lũng Cú, Nhà Vương, cave) still sell their own tickets. This is not Hoàng Su Phì, which sits west of the geopark.
whyGo: The landscape that makes every other Hà Giang card make sense.

name: Quan Ba Heaven Gate
keywords: Stop at Cổng Trời Quản Bạ on QL4C, about 40–50 km from the provincial capital: the classic first-day viewpoint over the Twin Mountains valley and the climb onto the plateau.
about: Stop at Cổng Trời Quản Bạ on QL4C, about 40–50 km from the provincial capital: the classic first-day viewpoint over the Twin Mountains valley and the climb onto the plateau.
hook: The first high saddle after Hà Giang city — cloud sea if you are lucky.
cardSummary: Roadside / small viewpoint fee sometimes. Same stop cluster as Núi Đôi — one pull-over. Fog erases the view; do not wait hours. Bắc Sum is an earlier pass on the same climb.
whyGo: The loop’s opening act; skip it and the Twin Mountains read as a rumour.

name: Tu San Canyon
keywords: Look into Hẻm Tu Sản from Ma Pi Leng pull-offs or from a river boat: vertical limestone walls on the Nho Que.
about: Look into Hẻm Tu Sản from Ma Pi Leng pull-offs or from a river boat: vertical limestone walls on the Nho Que. Depth claims vary; the spectacle does not.
hook: The Nho Que slot marketed as the deepest canyon in Southeast Asia.
cardSummary: Viewpoint is a pass stop; the boat is a separate ticket down a steep access. Do not pay twice for “canyon + river” as two full days. One gorge morning.
whyGo: The gorge you came to photograph — same water as the boat card.

name: Nho Que River
keywords: Boat the Nho Que (usually from the Mậu Duệ / Tu Sản access): a dam-raised stretch of jade water through the canyon.
typical hours Day boats; weather cancels
about: Boat the Nho Que (usually from the Mậu Duệ / Tu Sản access): a dam-raised stretch of jade water through the canyon. Life jackets matter; the climb back to the road is steep.
hook: Turquoise reservoir water under Ma Pi Leng’s walls.
cardSummary: Shared boats often 100–150,000 VND; private more. 45–90 minutes on the water plus transfer. Confirm the driver waits. Not a second Ma Pi Leng. Midday glare; morning is kinder. Reservoir, not a wild alpine torrent.
whyGo: The only way to sit inside the gorge instead of above it.

name: Tham Ma Pass
keywords: Ride the tight bends of Thẩm Mã between Yên Minh and Đồng Văn.
about: Ride the tight bends of Thẩm Mã between Yên Minh and Đồng Văn. Local legend names the pass for horses that lost their footing; today it is a short, photogenic shelf with a small shrine stop.
hook: Đèo Thẩm Mã — the “horse-trampling” saddle toward Đồng Văn.
cardSummary: Free road. One photo bay. Do not linger in fog. Chin Khoanh is the nine-bend pass nearer Quản Bạ — different saddle.
whyGo: The pass before the old town, not a second Ma Pi Leng.

name: Chin Khoanh Pass
keywords: Count the bends of Đèo Chín Khoanh — the “nine-section” pass on the Quản Bạ side of the plateau road, a technical stretch more than a viewpoint plaza.
about: Count the bends of Đèo Chín Khoanh — the “nine-section” pass on the Quản Bạ side of the plateau road, a technical stretch more than a viewpoint plaza.
hook: Nine hairpins on the climb through Quản Bạ.
cardSummary: Free road. Eyes on gravel, not the camera. Heaven Gate is the lookout; this is the staircase. One climb.
whyGo: The riding highlight before Heaven Gate if you care about corners.

name: Bac Sum Pass
keywords: Cross Đèo Bắc Sum on the first hours of the loop: pine, cloud, and the sense that the plateau has started before Heaven Gate’s official postcard.
about: Cross Đèo Bắc Sum on the first hours of the loop: pine, cloud, and the sense that the plateau has started before Heaven Gate’s official postcard.
hook: The early QL4C climb out of Hà Giang city.
cardSummary: Free road, city-to-Quản Bạ. Photo if the cloud opens; keep moving. Km 0 is where you started, not a second climb.
whyGo: The warmup pass — do not treat it as Ma Pi Leng.

name: Quan Ba Twin Mountains (Fairy Bosom)
keywords: Photograph the Twin Mountains from Heaven Gate or the valley floor: a pair of limestone hills that local storytelling reads as a fairy’s bosom.
about: Photograph the Twin Mountains from Heaven Gate or the valley floor: a pair of limestone hills that local storytelling reads as a fairy’s bosom. Best after rain or in rice green; winter can be grey.
hook: Núi Đôi Cô Tiên — two karst breasts in the Quản Bạ valley.
cardSummary: Same stop as Cổng Trời. No separate ticket required for the view. Do not climb unofficial paths. One photo, then Lung Khuy or Nam Dam — not an hour of the same hill.
whyGo: The postcard that tells you you have entered the geopark.

name: Yen Minh Pine Forest
keywords: Walk or ride through the thông Yên Minh grove used as a loop tea-and-photo stop: cooler air, needle floor, and a pause between Quản Bạ and Thẩm Mã.
about: Walk or ride through the thông Yên Minh grove used as a loop tea-and-photo stop: cooler air, needle floor, and a pause between Quản Bạ and Thẩm Mã.
hook: A roadside pine stand on the way through Yên Minh.
cardSummary: Free or a small local fee. 20 minutes. Yên Minh town is the lunch card; this is the trees. Do not expect Hoàng Su Phì terraces.
whyGo: Shade on a hot climb — not a national park.

name: Du Gia Waterfall
keywords: Hike a short path to Thác Du Già: a cold pool used on the return from Mèo Vạc or as an extra loop night.
about: Hike a short path to Thác Du Già: a cold pool used on the return from Mèo Vạc or as an extra loop night. Slippery rock; after rain the fall is louder and the path worse.
hook: A swim cascade in the Tày valley south of the plateau.
cardSummary: Small local ticket sometimes. Pair with Du Già village — one valley, two cards. Off the classic 3-day timing; do not force it after a late Ma Pi Leng. Not Hoàng Su Phì.
whyGo: The swim that is not a river boat.

name: Hoang Su Phi Rice Terraces
keywords: Leave QL4C for Hoàng Su Phì: layered rice on Nùng, Tày, and Dao slopes, best in water-fill (roughly May–June) or harvest gold (September–October).
about: Leave QL4C for Hoàng Su Phì: layered rice on Nùng, Tày, and Dao slopes, best in water-fill (roughly May–June) or harvest gold (September–October). This is a 2–3 night add-on, not a viewpoint on the way to Đồng Văn.
hook: National-heritage terraces west of Hà Giang — not on the 3-day loop.
cardSummary: Different road from the karst loop. Pair with Chiêu Lầu Thi or Tây Côn Lĩnh, not with Ma Pi Leng the same day. Homestay nights, not a day trip from the city unless you like 10 hours in a car.
whyGo: The terrace district the geopark loop does not include.

name: Chieu Lau Thi Mountain
keywords: Trek Chiêu Lầu Thi (Kiêu Liêu Ti) from Hồ Thầu: a northeast cloud-sea summit often listed around 2,402 m.
about: Trek Chiêu Lầu Thi (Kiêu Liêu Ti) from Hồ Thầu: a northeast cloud-sea summit often listed around 2,402 m. Sunrise camps are the product; this is not a roadside pass.
hook: A 2,402 m cloud-hunt peak in Hồ Thầu, Hoàng Su Phì.
cardSummary: Guide and fitness required. Tây Côn Lĩnh (~2,418 m) is the higher Ha Giang massif — do not hike both in 24 hours. Not on the Đồng Văn geopark road. 2 days with a homestay is honest.
whyGo: The peak day west of the loop.

name: Tay Con Linh Mountain
keywords: Commit to Tây Côn Lĩnh on the Hoàng Su Phì / Vị Xuyên divide: moss forest, waterfalls on the approach, and a long ridge.
about: Commit to Tây Côn Lĩnh on the Hoàng Su Phì / Vị Xuyên divide: moss forest, waterfalls on the approach, and a long ridge. Higher and wilder than Chiêu Lầu Thi’s cloud meadow reputation.
hook: Ha Giang’s highest massif, about 2,418 m on the Chảy headwaters.
cardSummary: Multi-day trek with a licensed guide. One peak per trip. Not Ma Pi Leng. Weather closes the ridge. This is the west, hours from Đồng Văn.
whyGo: The province high point — not a loop viewpoint.

name: Lung Khuy Cave
keywords: Walk the boarded galleries of Hang Lùng Khúy: a developed karst cave near the Twin Mountains road, with lighting and a modest climb from the ticket booth.
about: Walk the boarded galleries of Hang Lùng Khúy: a developed karst cave near the Twin Mountains road, with lighting and a modest climb from the ticket booth.
hook: A lit limestone cave under Quản Bạ’s hills.
cardSummary: Adult tickets often ~50,000 VND. 45–75 minutes. Pair with Heaven Gate, not with a second cave. Helmets/lighting included in the developed route. Slippery after rain.
whyGo: The one cave on the classic first-day loop.

name: Lung Cu Flag Tower
keywords: Climb Cột cờ Lũng Cú at about 1,470 m: an octagonal tower modelled on Hà Nội’s flag tower, a 54 m² flag for 54 ethnic groups, bronze-drum reliefs, and two ponds locals call a drago
about: Climb Cột cờ Lũng Cú at about 1,470 m: an octagonal tower modelled on Hà Nội’s flag tower, a 54 m² flag for 54 ethnic groups, bronze-drum reliefs, and two ponds locals call a dragon’s eyes. Clear days look into Yunnan.
hook: Vietnam’s northern flag, 34.85 m above Lũng Cú commune.
cardSummary: Adult ~25,000 VND; hours often 08:00–17:00. Stairs or a small electric cart. Pair with Lô Lô Chải, not with a second flag. Border rules: stay on marked paths. Lũng Pù is a different village.
whyGo: The sovereignty stop — 24 km north of Đồng Văn town.

name: Dong Van Ancient Town
keywords: Walk Phố cổ Đồng Văn: late-Nguyễn and French-period façades, a compact square, cafés, and lantern evenings.
about: Walk Phố cổ Đồng Văn: late-Nguyễn and French-period façades, a compact square, cafés, and lantern evenings. Restoration is real — it is pleasant, not an untouched trading town.
hook: Stone-and-timber shop houses around the highland square.
cardSummary: Heritage-street ticket sometimes ~20,000 VND. The dong-van city card is the same town as a plateau stay. The Đồng Văn-page dong-van-old-quarter card is these streets — do not book both. Sunday market is a separate morning. Do not race Ma Pi Leng and a night walk if you will ride after dark.
whyGo: The overnight streets after the passes.

name: Palace of the Hmong King (Vuong Family Palace)
keywords: Tour Dinh Vua Mèo at Sà Phìn: an early-20th-century stone-and-timber compound of the Vương family, blending Chinese courtyard planning with highland Hmong power.
about: Tour Dinh Vua Mèo at Sà Phìn: an early-20th-century stone-and-timber compound of the Vương family, blending Chinese courtyard planning with highland Hmong power. National architectural relic.
hook: The Sà Phìn mansion of Vương Chính Đức / Vương Chí Sình.
cardSummary: Ticket often ~20,000 VND; typical 07:00–17:00. On the road between Yên Minh and Đồng Văn. 45–70 minutes. Audio guides extra. Not Pao’s House (that is a film house in Sủng Là).
whyGo: The one historic interior on the plateau that is not a cave.

name: Meo Vac Town
keywords: Sleep or lunch in Mèo Vạc: a working highland district centre, Wednesday/Sunday market energy depending on the week, and the practical base after the pass.
about: Sleep or lunch in Mèo Vạc: a working highland district centre, Wednesday/Sunday market energy depending on the week, and the practical base after the pass. Less polished than Đồng Văn’s old quarter.
hook: The south-end loop town under Ma Pi Leng’s shadow.
cardSummary: No ticket. The market card is the weekly stall morning. Khau Vai is a further commune, not the town square. One night here or Đồng Văn is enough unless you add Du Già.
whyGo: The other overnight — so you do not recross the pass in the dark.

name: Yen Minh Town
keywords: Use Yên Minh as the midpoint: phở, petrol, a stretch, and the pine grove.
about: Use Yên Minh as the midpoint: phở, petrol, a stretch, and the pine grove. It is a district town, not an ancient quarter.
hook: The plateau’s lunch and fuel town, pines on the edge.
cardSummary: Free. Pair with the pine forest and Thẩm Mã, then keep moving. Market days are local; do not expect Đồng Văn Sunday density every morning.
whyGo: Logistics with a view — not a second Đồng Văn.

name: Km 0 Milestone (Ha Giang City Center)
keywords: Photograph Cột mốc Km 0 in Hà Giang city — the ceremonial start of QL4C stories, a riverside provincial capital, hotels, and the last easy ATM before the plateau.
about: Photograph Cột mốc Km 0 in Hà Giang city — the ceremonial start of QL4C stories, a riverside provincial capital, hotels, and the last easy ATM before the plateau.
hook: The painted zero-kilometre stone where loops begin.
cardSummary: Free, always. Sleep here the night before a 3–4 day loop. The ha-giang-loop card is the road day that starts from this town. Hoàng Su Phì is a different departure west.
whyGo: Orientation night before Bắc Sum, not a mountain day.

name: Sung La Valley
keywords: Drop into Sủng Là between Yên Minh and Đồng Văn: a wide cultivated bowl famous in autumn buckwheat and spring rape, with Lao Sa hamlet and Pao’s House on the floor.
about: Drop into Sủng Là between Yên Minh and Đồng Văn: a wide cultivated bowl famous in autumn buckwheat and spring rape, with Lao Sa hamlet and Pao’s House on the floor.
hook: A Hmong valley of buckwheat, canola, and stone houses.
cardSummary: Small village/house tickets possible. Season makes the colour. Pao’s House and Lao Xa are the same hamlet cluster — one stop. Not a second Sapa terrace.
whyGo: The valley card; Pao’s House is the doorway on the same floor.

name: Pao's House (Lao Sa)
keywords: Visit Nhà Pao in Lao Sa, Sủng Là: a traditional Hmong house used as the set for the 2006 film The Story of Pao.
about: Visit Nhà Pao in Lao Sa, Sủng Là: a traditional Hmong house used as the set for the 2006 film The Story of Pao. It is a lived-in courtyard, not the Vương palace.
hook: The film house from The Story of Pao, still in Lao Sa.
cardSummary: Small ticket. 20–40 minutes. Same stop as Sủng Là / Lao Xa — do not book three village products. Ask before portraits. Buy hemp only if you want it.
whyGo: The interior that matches the valley photographs.

name: Lao Xa Village
keywords: Walk Lao Sa / Lao Xa as a living hamlet: stone fences, hemp, corn cribs.
about: Walk Lao Sa / Lao Xa as a living hamlet: stone fences, hemp, corn cribs. Tourism is concentrated at the film house; the rest is still a village.
hook: The Hmong hamlet that holds Pao’s House.
cardSummary: Same valley as Sủng Là and Pao’s House. One visit. Do not pay children to pose. Lũng Pù and Mã Lé are different communes.
whyGo: Only if you want the lanes beyond the ticketed door.

name: Lung Tam Linen Weaving Village
keywords: Stop at Lùng Tám, a Hmong weaving cooperative village: beating hemp, looms, and indigo.
about: Stop at Lùng Tám, a Hmong weaving cooperative village: beating hemp, looms, and indigo. The activity card “Hmong weaving” is a workshop; this card is the place.
hook: Hmong hemp and indigo on the Quản Bạ road.
cardSummary: Free to walk; pay for cloth or a short try-on. Buy from the makers. Nam Dam is a different (Dao) village nearby — one craft stop is enough unless you care. Not Sapa Cat Cat.
whyGo: The craft village that is actually on the first-day road.

name: Du Gia Village
keywords: Stay in Du Già: stilt houses, river, and a slower night used on 4-day loops returning to Hà Giang.
about: Stay in Du Già: stilt houses, river, and a slower night used on 4-day loops returning to Hà Giang. The waterfall is a walk away; the village is the meal and sleep.
hook: A Tày homestay valley and the waterfall’s village.
cardSummary: Homestay, not a ticket booth. Pair with the waterfall card. Off the Đồng Văn–Mèo Vạc ridge. Do not add Hoàng Su Phì the same evening.
whyGo: The extra night that makes the return humane.

name: Nam Dam Village
keywords: Visit Nam Dam: Dao houses, community homestays, and a quieter alternative to the Heaven Gate parking lot.
about: Visit Nam Dam: Dao houses, community homestays, and a quieter alternative to the Heaven Gate parking lot. Distinct from Lùng Tám’s Hmong looms.
hook: A Dao community-tourism village under Quản Bạ.
cardSummary: Small community fee sometimes. Ask before photos. One Quản Bạ village plus Lùng Tám is plenty. Not Nam Hồng in Hoàng Su Phì.
whyGo: A first-day village that is not a weaving shop.

name: Lo Lo Chai Village
keywords: Walk Lô Lô Chải beside the flag tower: distinctive Lô Lô dress and houses.
about: Walk Lô Lô Chải beside the flag tower: distinctive Lô Lô dress and houses. It is a living border hamlet, easy to turn into a costume stop — don’t.
hook: The Lô Lô hamlet under the Lũng Cú flag.
cardSummary: Same excursion as the flag. Ask before portraits; never pay children. Mã Lé is another old village, further — one cultural stop with the tower is enough for most loops.
whyGo: The village that belongs on the Lũng Cú morning.

name: Seo Lung Village
keywords: Pass Sẻo Lủng when a driver offers a village that is not on every blog list: stone, corn, and ordinary highland life near the Đồng Văn–Mèo Vạc hills.
about: Pass Sẻo Lủng when a driver offers a village that is not on every blog list: stone, corn, and ordinary highland life near the Đồng Văn–Mèo Vạc hills.
hook: A quieter Hmong hamlet used as a loop side-stop.
cardSummary: Confirm the pin — names repeat. Not Lũng Pù, not Lao Xa. No costume market. Fifteen to thirty minutes.
whyGo: Only if you still have time after the pass, not instead of Ma Pi Leng.

name: Ma Le Ancient Village
keywords: Detour to Mã Lé for packed stone houses and a less-staged fabric than Lô Lô Chải’s parking.
about: Detour to Mã Lé for packed stone houses and a less-staged fabric than Lô Lô Chải’s parking. Still a living village; tourism is thinner.
hook: An older stone Hmong village on the Lũng Cú peninsula.
cardSummary: Same northern spur as the flag. Do not do Lô Lô Chải, Mã Lé, and Lũng Pù in one morning. Ask before entering yards.
whyGo: The “ancient village” if Lũng Cú’s hamlet felt like a turnout.

name: Lung Pu Village
keywords: Stop at Lũng Pù when the road offers a hamlet above the Nho Que country: ordinary Hmong life, not the flag tower (that is Lũng Cú).
about: Stop at Lũng Pù when the road offers a hamlet above the Nho Que country: ordinary Hmong life, not the flag tower (that is Lũng Cú).
hook: A Hmong village on the Mèo Vạc / gorge side of the plateau.
cardSummary: Easy to confuse with Lũng Cú by ear. Confirm the map. Short stop. Sẻo Lủng is another optional hamlet — pick one.
whyGo: A gorge-side village, not another Lũng Cú photo.

name: Khau Vai Love Market site
keywords: Reach Khau Vai commune (Mèo Vạc): historically a gathering where people who could not marry freely met once a year.
typical hours Festival: lunar 27/3; site daylight otherwise
about: Reach Khau Vai commune (Mèo Vạc): historically a gathering where people who could not marry freely met once a year. The lunar festival still happens; the site is marketed year-round and is quieter on ordinary days.
hook: The highland meeting ground of the 27th of the 3rd lunar month.
cardSummary: Festival crowds need a reserved night. Off-season it is a hillside commune, not Đồng Văn Sunday. Ask before photographs of ritual. Not the Mèo Vạc town market.
whyGo: Go for the festival date, or treat the site as a story — not a weekly market.

name: Dong Van Sunday Market
keywords: Arrive early Sunday in Đồng Văn when highland communes come in to trade.
about: Arrive early Sunday in Đồng Văn when highland communes come in to trade. It is an economic morning, not a costume park. The old-town card is the streets the other six days.
hook: The plateau’s main weekly trade — livestock, cloth, and breakfast.
cardSummary: Free. Busiest 06:00–10:00 Sunday. Ask before portraits; do not block sales. Mèo Vạc and Quản Bạ have their own weekly days — you cannot honestly do three Sunday markets. The dong-van city guide already describes this morning.
whyGo: The one market worth bending a loop calendar for.

name: Meo Vac Market
keywords: Shop Mèo Vạc’s highland market for produce, meat, and cloth.
typical hours Morning on market day (confirm)
about: Shop Mèo Vạc’s highland market for produce, meat, and cloth. Guides disagree on the “main” day (often Sunday or midweek); ask your host the night you arrive.
hook: The district market in Mèo Vạc town — confirm the weekday.
cardSummary: Free. Not Khau Vai’s love-market festival. If Sunday is Đồng Văn’s big day, do not expect the same density here the same morning. One weekly market per loop.
whyGo: Town-market energy if you sleep on this side of the pass.

name: Quan Ba Market
keywords: Time a Quản Bạ morning market if your calendar hits the local weekly day: Dao, Hmong, and Tày trade closer to Heaven Gate than to Đồng Văn.
about: Time a Quản Bạ morning market if your calendar hits the local weekly day: Dao, Hmong, and Tày trade closer to Heaven Gate than to Đồng Văn.
hook: The first-district market on the climb from the city.
cardSummary: Confirm the day. Free. Lùng Tám weaving is a village, not this market. One highland market morning is enough.
whyGo: A market without riding to the end of the plateau.

name: Hoang Su Phi Market
keywords: Use Hoàng Su Phì’s market morning when you are already on the terrace side: a different ethnic mix from the Đồng Văn karst Sundays.
about: Use Hoàng Su Phì’s market morning when you are already on the terrace side: a different ethnic mix from the Đồng Văn karst Sundays.
hook: The west-district highland market — Nùng, Dao, Tày trade.
cardSummary: Confirm the weekday. Free. Do not ride here from Mèo Vạc for a market and back. Pair with the terrace card.
whyGo: Only with the terraces — not a loop detour.

name: Cát Bà National Park
keywords: Enter Vườn quốc gia Cát Bà (~109 km² of island and marine buffer): tropical karst forest, the critically endangered Cát Bà langur, and the trailheads for Ngự Lâm, Kim Giao, and lon
about: Enter Vườn quốc gia Cát Bà (~109 km² of island and marine buffer): tropical karst forest, the critically endangered Cát Bà langur, and the trailheads for Ngự Lâm, Kim Giao, and longer Việt Hải walks. UNESCO’s 2023 Ha Long–Cát Bà property includes this park; you still buy a park ticket.
hook: Limestone jungle on Vietnam’s largest Ha Long island — langur country.
cardSummary: Park ticket often ~40–80,000 VND (listings). HQ is inland from town (~15–20 min). Do not expect to see a langur. Ngự Lâm, Kim Giao, Nho Khôi, and Trung Trang sit inside or beside this ticket — do not buy a second “park day.” The cat-ba card is the island product, not a second gate.
whyGo: The land half of Cát Bà — without it the island is only a pier.

name: Lan Hạ Bay
keywords: Day-boat or overnight into Vịnh Lan Hạ from Bến Bèo or the town pier: hundreds of islets, pocket beaches, and aquaculture lanes inside the same UNESCO seascape as Ha Long, with few
about: Day-boat or overnight into Vịnh Lan Hạ from Bến Bèo or the town pier: hundreds of islets, pocket beaches, and aquaculture lanes inside the same UNESCO seascape as Ha Long, with fewer mega-ships.
hook: The quieter karst water south of Ha Long — boarded from Cát Bà.
cardSummary: Pay the boat, not a bay “gate.” Ask passenger count, kayak minutes, and weather plan. The lan-ha city card is the kayak product — do not book both for the same morning. Cái Bèo and Monkey Island are often on the same water, not extra bays. Cửa Vạn is usually a Ha Long cruise cove.
whyGo: The water day that makes sleeping on Cát Bà worth the ferry.

name: Trung Trang Cave
keywords: Walk Hang Trung Trang: a developed limestone cave on the national-park approach, boardwalks and lights, about 300 m of passage.
about: Walk Hang Trung Trang: a developed limestone cave on the national-park approach, boardwalks and lights, about 300 m of passage. A first karst hour, not Sơn Đoòng.
hook: The park’s walkable show cave — humid halls beside the HQ road.
cardSummary: Often bundled with the park ticket or a small add-on. 30–50 minutes. Slippery after rain. Pair with Ngự Lâm the same morning. Hoa Cương, Thiên Long, and Nguồn Giống are other caves — pick one extra, not four.
whyGo: The one cave most visitors can do without a specialist guide.

name: Hospital Cave (Hang Quân Y)
keywords: Tour Hang Quân Y (Hospital Cave): 17 rooms on three levels, used as a secret hospital and command post during the American War.
about: Tour Hang Quân Y (Hospital Cave): 17 rooms on three levels, used as a secret hospital and command post during the American War. Concrete floors, hospital fittings, and a short film or guide at busy times.
hook: A bombproof wartime hospital cut into the karst above the town road.
cardSummary: Separate ticket, listings often ~20–40,000 VND. 30–45 minutes. On the road toward the park, not inside the jungle gate. Not Trung Trang. Stairs and low light.
whyGo: The island’s clearest war site — not another pretty dripstone hall.

name: Hoa Cương Cave (Diamond Cave)
keywords: Visit Hang Hoa Cương when a park or boat combo offers it: calcite sparkle, uneven floor, usually a guide.
typical hours With guide / park hours
about: Visit Hang Hoa Cương when a park or boat combo offers it: calcite sparkle, uneven floor, usually a guide. Less staged than Trung Trang.
hook: A glitter-named park cave — crystals in the limestone, not a jewellery shop.
cardSummary: Confirm it is open and whether the park ticket covers it. 30–60 minutes. Same cave family as Thiên Long and Nguồn Giống — one extra cave. Not Hospital Cave.
whyGo: Only if you want a second cave after Trung Trang, not instead of the bay.

name: Thiên Long Cave
keywords: Hang Thiên Long is a local karst cave used on some park or private-guide loops.
about: Hang Thiên Long is a local karst cave used on some park or private-guide loops. Lighting and access change; it is not Thiên Cung on the Ha Long day boats.
hook: A less-sold Cát Bà cave — confirm the pin before you hire a xe ôm.
cardSummary: Do not confuse with Thiên Cung (Ha Long). Same “extra cave” slot as Hoa Cương and Nguồn Giống. Skip if the park morning is already full.
whyGo: Only with a named guide and time — not a must beside Trung Trang.

name: Nguồn Giống Cave
keywords: Hang Nguồn Giống sits in the national-park karst and appears on specialist or ranger walks.
about: Hang Nguồn Giống sits in the national-park karst and appears on specialist or ranger walks. Facilities are thin; treat it as a guided add-on.
hook: A park-side cave tied to local origin stories — quiet, not a show cave.
cardSummary: Guide recommended. One of the Hoa Cương / Thiên Long extras — not a third cave the same afternoon. Park ticket still applies.
whyGo: For cave collectors after Trung Trang — not a first-day stop.

name: Cannon Fort (Cao Điểm 177)
keywords: Climb Cao Điểm 177 above Cát Bà town: French and later Vietnamese gun positions, tunnels, and a sweep over the harbour and Lan Hạ.
typical hours Verify locally — may be closed
about: Climb Cao Điểm 177 above Cát Bà town: French and later Vietnamese gun positions, tunnels, and a sweep over the harbour and Lan Hạ. Access has been closed or restricted at times for military use — ask in town the morning you go.
hook: The 177 m hill of Pháo Đài Thần Công — harbour views when the gate is open.
cardSummary: May be closed. When open, a small ticket and a steep walk. 45–90 minutes. Not Hospital Cave. Sunset is beautiful and the path is dark on the way down — torch or go earlier.
whyGo: The classic town viewpoint, if it is actually open.

name: Cát Cò 1 Beach
keywords: Walk or taxi to Bãi Cát Cò 1: the first of the three cliff-backed coves south of town.
typical hours Daylight; flags rule swimming
about: Walk or taxi to Bãi Cát Cò 1: the first of the three cliff-backed coves south of town. Development and access paths change; follow signs and swim only where flags allow.
hook: The closest cove beach under the town cliffs — sand, deck, weekend noise.
cardSummary: Cát Cò 1–3 are one shoreline family. Pick one cove, not three tickets. Water is seasonal; winter is grey. Tùng Thu is the in-town alternative. Monkey Island is a boat, not this sand.
whyGo: The easy swim after a park or boat day — not a tropical postcard every week.

name: Cát Cò 2 Beach
keywords: Use Bãi Cát Cò 2 when 1 is packed or a hotel path dumps you here.
about: Use Bãi Cát Cò 2 when 1 is packed or a hotel path dumps you here. Same water, same seasonality, same “one beach afternoon” rule.
hook: The middle Cát Cò cove — same cliffs, a slightly different deck.
cardSummary: Same cove cluster as Cát Cò 1 and 3. Do not itinerary all three. Confirm current access; some stretches have been gated by resorts.
whyGo: Only if you are already on this stair — not a second beach product.

name: Cát Cò 3 Beach
keywords: Reach Bãi Cát Cò 3 along the cliff walk or a longer drop from town.
about: Reach Bãi Cát Cò 3 along the cliff walk or a longer drop from town. Often the least built-up of the three when access is allowed.
hook: The farthest Cát Cò cove — quieter sand if the path is open.
cardSummary: Same family as Cát Cò 1–2. One cove. Check closures. Tùng Thu is easier if you do not want the stairs.
whyGo: The prettier Cát Cò if you will walk for it — still not Lan Hạ.

name: Tùng Thu Beach
keywords: Use Bãi Tùng Thu on the harbour edge of Cát Bà town: cafés, evening light, a practical dip when you will not taxi to Cát Cò.
about: Use Bãi Tùng Thu on the harbour edge of Cát Bà town: cafés, evening light, a practical dip when you will not taxi to Cát Cò.
hook: The in-town strip — sunset walk more than a swim brochure.
cardSummary: Free town beach. Water quality varies with boats. Not Cát Cò and not Monkey Island. Pair with the square and night market, not a second swim card.
whyGo: Zero-transfer sand after dinner planning — lower expectations.

name: Monkey Island (Đảo Cát Dứa)
keywords: Boat to Đảo Cát Dứa (Monkey Island) in Lan Hạ: a short island call sold for swimming and macaques.
about: Boat to Đảo Cát Dứa (Monkey Island) in Lan Hạ: a short island call sold for swimming and macaques. These are not the park’s Cát Bà langurs. Feeding and close photos stress the animals.
hook: Hòn Cát Dứa — macaques, a beach stop, and a boat from town.
cardSummary: Usually on a Lan Hạ day boat, not a separate ticket you must buy. Do not feed monkeys. Same water as lan-ha-bay — do not stack a second boat. Skip if you dislike baited primate stops.
whyGo: Only if your bay boat already stops — not a wildlife conservation visit.

name: Việt Hải Ancient Village
keywords: Reach Việt Hải via Lan Hạ: a settled farming and fishing commune in a green bowl, old paths, homestays, and bicycles.
about: Reach Việt Hải via Lan Hạ: a settled farming and fishing commune in a green bowl, old paths, homestays, and bicycles. “Ancient village” is the brochure name for this same place as the fishing-village card.
hook: The inland valley village — boat, then a walk or xe through the karst.
cardSummary: Boat + transfer; often a half or full day. The viet-hai-fishing-village card is the same commune — do not book twice. Cái Bèo is the harbour float, not this valley. Ask before yard photos.
whyGo: The slow land hour after the karst channels — a village, not a set.

name: Việt Hải Fishing Village
keywords: Walk the inhabited side of Việt Hải: small boats, gardens, and meals.
about: Walk the inhabited side of Việt Hải: small boats, gardens, and meals. It is not a second village from the ancient-village card.
hook: The working edge of the same Việt Hải valley — nets, gardens, homestay kitchens.
cardSummary: Same place as viet-hai-village. One pin. Cái Bèo is the Cát Bà harbour float. Cửa Vạn is Ha Long’s cove.
whyGo: Only as the fishing angle of Việt Hải — same boat, same bowl.

name: Cửa Vạn Fishing Village
keywords: Cửa Vạn sits in a Ha Long Bay pocket, not on Cát Bà town water.
typical hours If the boat calls
about: Cửa Vạn sits in a Ha Long Bay pocket, not on Cát Bà town water. Some through-bay itineraries from the island still call; most Lan Hạ day boats do not.
hook: Ha Long’s headline floating cove — only if your Cát Bà boat actually goes there.
cardSummary: Same village as the Ha Long cua-van-village card. Do not book both. Cái Bèo is the Cát Bà harbour float. Việt Hải is an inland valley.
whyGo: Pin only when the captain names Cửa Vạn — otherwise use Cái Bèo.

name: Cái Bèo Floating Village (Vạn Chài Cái Bèo)
keywords: Pass or kayak Vạn chài Cái Bèo: Cát Bà’s own floating community at the mouth of the town harbour, still a workplace beside the tourist pier.
about: Pass or kayak Vạn chài Cái Bèo: Cát Bà’s own floating community at the mouth of the town harbour, still a workplace beside the tourist pier.
hook: The harbour float next to Bến Bèo — pens, houses, and the Lan Hạ start.
cardSummary: Often free from the pier or included on a kayak. 30–60 minutes. Not Cửa Vạn and not Việt Hải. Ask before photographing people. Same morning as lan-ha-bay, not a second boat.
whyGo: The village you can see without a Ha Long cruise ticket.

name: Hới Lake (Hải Hải)
keywords: Stop at Hồ Hới (often written Hải Hải on English lists): a small freshwater bowl in the national-park / Trân Châu hills, farmstays on the bank, not a town reservoir.
about: Stop at Hồ Hới (often written Hải Hải on English lists): a small freshwater bowl in the national-park / Trân Châu hills, farmstays on the bank, not a town reservoir.
hook: A quiet park-side lake in Trân Châu — also listed as Hải Hải.
cardSummary: Free to look; lodging is separate. Pair with the park, not with Cát Cò. Confirm the map pin — names wander. Not Ao Ếch on every trail map; ask at HQ if you want the Frog Pond hike instead.
whyGo: A green pause on the park road — not a swimming resort lake.

name: Kim Giao Forest
keywords: Walk the Kim Giao forest trail from park HQ: a protected grove of the slow kim giao tree among karst, often paired with Ngự Lâm rather than done as its own day.
about: Walk the Kim Giao forest trail from park HQ: a protected grove of the slow kim giao tree among karst, often paired with Ngự Lâm rather than done as its own day.
hook: The rare kim giao stand inside the national park — shade, not a viewpoint plaza.
cardSummary: Included in the park ticket. 45–90 minutes. Same gate as Ngự Lâm and Nho Khôi — pick one serious hike. Stay on the path; this is langur habitat.
whyGo: The botanical hour of the park ticket.

name: Nho Khôi Mountain
keywords: Hike Núi Nho Khôi inside Cát Bà National Park: a fuller ridge than the 30-minute Ngự Lâm climb, karst, heat, and little shade at noon.
about: Hike Núi Nho Khôi inside Cát Bà National Park: a fuller ridge than the 30-minute Ngự Lâm climb, karst, heat, and little shade at noon.
hook: A longer park summit than Ngự Lâm — guide and water, not a viewpoint staircase.
cardSummary: Park ticket plus fitness. Half day. Not Ngự Lâm — choose one peak. Guide wise in wet months. Same park as Kim Giao; do not stack both plus Việt Hải.
whyGo: When Ngự Lâm felt like a warm-up and you still have a land day.

name: Đỉnh Ngự Lâm (Ngự Lâm Peak)
keywords: Climb Đỉnh Ngự Lâm from the national-park entrance: 20–40 minutes up on roots and limestone, a viewpoint deck, then the same path down.
about: Climb Đỉnh Ngự Lâm from the national-park entrance: 20–40 minutes up on roots and limestone, a viewpoint deck, then the same path down. The standard first hike.
hook: The short, steep HQ climb — island-and-bay view if the cloud lifts.
cardSummary: Park ticket. Shoes with grip; slick after rain. Not Nho Khôi. Pair with Trung Trang. Midday heat is miserable. Langurs are unlikely.
whyGo: The park view most people actually finish.

name: Cát Bà Market
keywords: Walk Chợ Cát Bà in town: wet counters in the morning, quieter by lunch.
about: Walk Chợ Cát Bà in town: wet counters in the morning, quieter by lunch. The working market, not the evening tourist row.
hook: The covered day market — fish, fruit, and breakfast before the pier.
cardSummary: Free. Morning is the point. The night market is the same town, different hours — do not list both as must-dos. Square is next door.
whyGo: Cash fruit and a plate before the 8 a.m. boat.

name: Cát Bà Night Market
keywords: Graze the Cát Bà night market along the harbour streets: grilled shellfish, beer, T-shirts.
about: Graze the Cát Bà night market along the harbour streets: grilled shellfish, beer, T-shirts. Agree prices; ice and origin vary.
hook: Seafood grills and souvenir aisles when the boats are in.
cardSummary: Free to walk; food is the cost. Same shore as the square and Tùng Thu. Day market is the morning version — one market ritual is enough.
whyGo: The easy town evening after Lan Hạ.

name: Cát Bà Central Square
keywords: Use Cát Bà’s central square as orientation: the statue/plaza, the walk to Tùng Thu, and the last easy grab of cash and SIM before a rural stay.
about: Use Cát Bà’s central square as orientation: the statue/plaza, the walk to Tùng Thu, and the last easy grab of cash and SIM before a rural stay.
hook: The harbour plaza — buses, ice cream, and the town’s meeting ground.
cardSummary: Free. Pair with market or night market, not a third town pin. Cannon Fort rises above if the gate is open. Km of ferry stress ends here.
whyGo: Zero-ticket town geography — not a sight you travel for.

name: Cát Bà Cable Car (Sun World Cát Bà)
keywords: Ride the Sun World Cát Bà cable car between the Cát Hải mainland station and Phù Long on the island: a long marine karst crossing used as transport and a ticketed viewpoint.
about: Ride the Sun World Cát Bà cable car between the Cát Hải mainland station and Phù Long on the island: a long marine karst crossing used as transport and a ticketed viewpoint. It is not the Hạ Long Queen Cable / Sun Wheel.
hook: Sun World’s Cát Hải–Phù Long span — a crossing and a view, not a town toy.
cardSummary: Sun World ticket; prices are resort-level. Last cars matter. Phù Long mangrove is the same north end. Do not buy this and a Ha Long Sun World ticket thinking they are one park. Weather stops the line.
whyGo: When it fits your Hai Phong / Cát Hải arrival — not a must if you already ferried.

name: Phù Long Mangrove Forest
keywords: Paddle or walk Phù Long’s mangrove: the Cát Bà wetland on the Cát Hải approach, birds at slack tide, the cable-car island station nearby.
about: Paddle or walk Phù Long’s mangrove: the Cát Bà wetland on the Cát Hải approach, birds at slack tide, the cable-car island station nearby.
hook: The north-island mangroves — kayak roots, not the town harbour.
cardSummary: Kayak hire or a short tour; free to look from the road. Same north end as the Sun World cable — one visit. Not Cái Bèo. Tide matters; noon glare is dull.
whyGo: A different Cát Bà than Lan Hạ’s open karst — mud and shade.

name: Dong Van Ancient Town
keywords: Walk Phố cổ Đồng Văn from the stay: late-Nguyễn and French-period shop houses, a compact square, cafés.
about: Walk Phố cổ Đồng Văn from the stay: late-Nguyễn and French-period shop houses, a compact square, cafés. Restoration is real; it is pleasant, not an untouched trading town.
hook: The stone square you sleep beside — lanterns after the pass.
cardSummary: Heritage-street ticket sometimes ~20,000 VND. Same streets as the Hà Giang dong-van-ancient-town card — do not book both. The dong-van card is the stay. Sunday is the market morning. Old market is the everyday hall. Do not recross Ma Pi Leng after dark for lanterns.
whyGo: The town half of a plateau night — streets, not another pass.

name: Dong Van Old Market
keywords: Use Chợ cũ Đồng Văn on ordinary mornings: produce, noodles, household stalls in or beside the old quarter.
about: Use Chợ cũ Đồng Văn on ordinary mornings: produce, noodles, household stalls in or beside the old quarter. Sunday’s big market is a different rhythm on the same town.
hook: The everyday covered hall — breakfast, not the Sunday livestock crush.
cardSummary: Free. Morning. Sunday market is the weekly event — do not list both as must-dos on a Sunday. Phó Bảng and Mã Lé markets are other communes.
whyGo: A working breakfast if you are not here on Sunday.

name: Palace of the Hmong King (Vuong Family Palace)
keywords: Tour the Vương family residence (Vương Chính Đức / Vương Chí Sình): early-20th-century stone and timber courtyards, a national architectural relic, about 15–20 km west of Đồng Văn
about: Tour the Vương family residence (Vương Chính Đức / Vương Chí Sình): early-20th-century stone and timber courtyards, a national architectural relic, about 15–20 km west of Đồng Văn town.
hook: Dinh Vua Mèo at Sà Phìn — the courtyard mansion on the Yên Minh–Đồng Văn road.
cardSummary: Ticket often ~20,000 VND; ~07:00–17:00. 45–70 minutes. Same house as the Hà Giang vuong-palace card — do not book both. Not Pao’s House in Sủng Là. Pair with the town, not with a late Ma Pi Leng start.
whyGo: The one historic interior on the plateau that is not a cave.

name: Ma Pi Leng Pass
keywords: Ride Đèo Mã Pì Lèng toward Mèo Vạc: Hạnh Phúc Road above the Nho Que / Tu Sản gorge.
about: Ride Đèo Mã Pì Lèng toward Mèo Vạc: Hạnh Phúc Road above the Nho Que / Tu Sản gorge. Pull-offs only; the Sky Walk is a separate exposed path.
hook: The Happiness Road shelf from the Đồng Văn overnight — one daylight crossing.
cardSummary: No road toll. Same pass as ma-pi-leng-pass on the Hà Giang page — do not book both. Tu Sản and Nho Que are the same gorge morning. Night riding is unsafe. Sleep Mèo Vạc or return with daylight.
whyGo: The pass you came north for — start from town with hours of light.

name: Tu San Canyon
keywords: Look into Hẻm Tu Sản from a pass pull-off or from the river: vertical walls.
about: Look into Hẻm Tu Sản from a pass pull-off or from the river: vertical walls. Depth claims vary; the spectacle does not.
hook: The Nho Que slot under Ma Pi Leng — viewpoint or boat, not both rushed.
cardSummary: Same canyon as tu-san-canyon on Hà Giang. One gorge morning with Ma Pi Leng and Nho Que. Do not stand in the carriageway.
whyGo: The gorge photograph — same water as the boat card.

name: Nho Que River
keywords: Boat the Nho Que from the Mậu Duệ / Tu Sản side: shared boats often 100–150,000 VND.
typical hours Daylight; last boats early afternoon
about: Boat the Nho Que from the Mậu Duệ / Tu Sản side: shared boats often 100–150,000 VND. Life jackets and enough light to climb out.
hook: The turquoise reservoir under the pass — a ticketed descent, then the climb back.
cardSummary: Same river as nho-que-river on Hà Giang. 45–90 minutes on the water. Not a second Ma Pi Leng. Waiting driver required.
whyGo: The gorge from below — only if the pass crossing still has daylight after.

name: Lung Cu Flag Tower
keywords: Visit Cột cờ Lũng Cú: octagonal tower modelled on Hà Nội’s, ~54 m² flag for 54 groups, two “dragon-eye” ponds.
about: Visit Cột cờ Lũng Cú: octagonal tower modelled on Hà Nội’s, ~54 m² flag for 54 groups, two “dragon-eye” ponds. Adult listings ~25,000 VND; 08:00–17:00 typical.
hook: The 34.85 m tower ~24 km north of town — flag, stairs, Yunnan on a clear day.
cardSummary: Same tower as lung-cu-flag-tower on Hà Giang. Cực Bắc milestone is a nearby marker — one spur, not two destinations. Lũng Pù is a different village. Stay on marked border paths.
whyGo: The northern-spur monument — pair with Lô Lô Chải, not a second peak.

name: North Pole Milestone (Cực Bắc)
keywords: Photograph the Cực Bắc milestone on the Lũng Cú spur: a border-area marker sold as the country’s north pole.
typical hours With the Lũng Cú visit
about: Photograph the Cực Bắc milestone on the Lũng Cú spur: a border-area marker sold as the country’s north pole. The true northernmost metre is fussed over; the visit is this stone plus the flag, not a geography exam.
hook: The Cột mốc Cực Bắc stone — Vietnam’s billed northern point, not the flag tower.
cardSummary: Same morning as the flag tower — not a second outing. Confirm the pin; do not wander off marked paths at the border. Not Lũng Pù.
whyGo: Five extra minutes if you already climbed to Lũng Cú.

name: Lo Lo Chai Village
keywords: Walk Lô Lô Chải on the Lũng Cú road: distinctive dress, stone houses, a turnout that can feel like a costume stop.
about: Walk Lô Lô Chải on the Lũng Cú road: distinctive dress, stone houses, a turnout that can feel like a costume stop.
hook: The Lô Lô hamlet under the flag — dress, courtyards, easy to stage.
cardSummary: Same hamlet as lo-lo-chai-village on Hà Giang. One stop with the tower. Mã Lé is the thinner-tourism stone village if you have time — not both plus Phó Cáo.
whyGo: The village that sits on the flag morning — ask before portraits.

name: Lao Sa Village
keywords: Pass Lao Sa / Lao Xa on the Sủng Là floor: lived-in Hmong yards, tourism concentrated at the film-house door.
about: Pass Lao Sa / Lao Xa on the Sủng Là floor: lived-in Hmong yards, tourism concentrated at the film-house door.
hook: The hamlet around Pao’s House — stone fences, hemp, corn.
cardSummary: Same hamlet as lao-xa-village on Hà Giang. One valley with sung-la-dong-van and pao-house-dong-van. Do not pay children to pose.
whyGo: Only as the village of the Sủng Là / Pao stop — not a third product.

name: Sung La Valley
keywords: Drop into Sủng Là between Yên Minh and Đồng Văn: a green floor of corn and flowers, Lao Sa and Pao’s House on the same ground.
about: Drop into Sủng Là between Yên Minh and Đồng Văn: a green floor of corn and flowers, Lao Sa and Pao’s House on the same ground.
hook: The cultivated Hmong bowl — buckwheat in autumn, rape in spring.
cardSummary: Same valley as sung-la-valley on Hà Giang. Small house tickets at Pao’s. One stop with Lao Sa. Not the Vương palace.
whyGo: Colour season on the plateau road — one valley pull-over.

name: Pao's House (Lao Sa)
keywords: Visit Nhà Pao in Lao Sa: the lived-in house from the 2006 film.
about: Visit Nhà Pao in Lao Sa: the lived-in house from the 2006 film. Small ticket, twenty to forty minutes.
hook: The Hmong house used for The Story of Pao — a courtyard, not a palace.
cardSummary: Same house as pao-house on Hà Giang. One hamlet with Lao Sa and the valley card. Not the Vương palace at Sà Phìn.
whyGo: The interior of Sủng Là — not Dinh Vua Mèo.

name: Tham Ma Pass
keywords: Stop Đèo Thẩm Mã: a shrine and a view, not the equal of Mã Pì Lèng.
about: Stop Đèo Thẩm Mã: a shrine and a view, not the equal of Mã Pì Lèng. Free road.
hook: The horse-legend shelf between Yên Minh and Đồng Văn — short, photogenic.
cardSummary: Same pass as tham-ma-pass on Hà Giang. Chín Khoanh is the nine-bend climb further south. Do not treat this as a second Ma Pi Leng.
whyGo: A stretch on the way into town — one bay.

name: Chin Khoanh Pass
keywords: Count Đèo Chín Khoanh if you ride QL4C up from Hà Giang / Quản Bạ.
about: Count Đèo Chín Khoanh if you ride QL4C up from Hà Giang / Quản Bạ. Heaven Gate is the lookout; this is the staircase.
hook: The nine-section hairpins on the Quản Bạ climb — on the way to Đồng Văn, not in town.
cardSummary: Same pass as chin-khoanh-pass on Hà Giang. Eyes on gravel. Not Thẩm Mã. Do not ride back south just to “collect” it after you already arrived.
whyGo: Only if that is your inbound road — not a day trip from the old quarter.

name: Ma Le Ancient Village
keywords: Walk Mã Lé: stone walls, quieter yards, the same northern road as the flag.
about: Walk Mã Lé: stone walls, quieter yards, the same northern road as the flag. Ask before entering courtyards.
hook: Older stone Hmong houses on the Lũng Cú spur — thinner turnout than Lô Lô Chải.
cardSummary: Same village as ma-le-village on Hà Giang. One extra stop with Lũng Cú — not Lô Lô Chải and Mã Lé and Phó Cáo. Market day is the ma-le-market card.
whyGo: The less-staged village if the flag morning still has time.

name: Dong Van Sunday Market
keywords: Be in Đồng Văn Sunday 06:00–10:00: a working highland market, not a costume display.
about: Be in Đồng Văn Sunday 06:00–10:00: a working highland market, not a costume display. Ask before close portraits; do not block stalls.
hook: The plateau’s main weekly trade — livestock, cloth, breakfast before 10:00.
cardSummary: Same market as dong-van-sunday-market on Hà Giang. Old market is the other six mornings. You cannot honestly do Mã Lé, Phó Bảng, and this Sunday. The old-quarter card is the evening streets.
whyGo: The reason to time a Saturday night in town.

name: Ma Le Market
keywords: Hit Mã Lé’s weekly market when your host names the morning: a smaller highland trade than Đồng Văn Sunday.
about: Hit Mã Lé’s weekly market when your host names the morning: a smaller highland trade than Đồng Văn Sunday.
hook: The commune market on the Lũng Cú road — confirm the day.
cardSummary: Confirm weekday. Do not chase it on the same Sunday as Đồng Văn. The village card is the stone lanes the other six days.
whyGo: Only if you are already on that spur and it is market day.

name: Don Cao Fortress (French Bunker Viewpoint)
keywords: Climb Đồn Cao: a crumbling bunker and gun post over Đồng Văn’s rooftops.
typical hours Daylight; dusk only with a torch
about: Climb Đồn Cao: a crumbling bunker and gun post over Đồng Văn’s rooftops. The dong-van stay guide already flags this hill; access and footing change after rain.
hook: Ruined French-era post above town — the karst bowl at dusk if the path is open.
cardSummary: Free or informal. 30–60 minutes. Isolated paths after dark are a bad idea. Not the Vương palace. Confirm the trail with your hotel.
hours: Daylight; dusk only with a torch
whyGo: The town viewpoint that is not a pass.

name: Thien Huong Ancient Village
keywords: Thiên Hương was a rare Tày earthen-house village on the stone plateau (~37–40 households).
typical hours Verify — historic site may be closed
about: Thiên Hương was a rare Tày earthen-house village on the stone plateau (~37–40 households). Storms and ground cracks in 2024 forced evacuation; authorities sealed the historic lanes. Families moved to a resettlement about 400–500 m away and have been encouraged to rebuild in a similar style.
hook: A ~200-year Tày hamlet ~7 km from town — the old lanes were closed after 2024 slides.
cardSummary: Original village is unsafe and off-limits unless officially reopened. Ask in Đồng Văn that morning. Not Phó Bảng (Hmong stone town) and not Sủng Là. Respect a community that lost its street.
hours: Verify — historic site may be closed
whyGo: Only if locals say a visit is open — do not treat ruins as a photo set.

name: Lung Ngoc Ho Cave
keywords: Hang Lũng Ngọc Hố appears on visitor lists for the plateau.
about: Hang Lũng Ngọc Hố appears on visitor lists for the plateau. Names wander: do not assume it is Lùng Khúy (Quản Bạ, on the Hà Giang page) or Hang Rồng at Sảng Tủng. Go only with a named local pin and a light.
hook: A Đồng Văn-district cave listing — confirm the pin before you hire a xe.
cardSummary: Not lung-khuy-cave. Guide or clear map. One cave. Slippery. Skip if the pass and flag already fill the day.
whyGo: A cave hour if you are cave-curious after the town — not a must.

name: Pho Cao Village
keywords: Ride into Phó Cáo, Đồng Văn district: corn terraces and hamlets used on quieter loops.
about: Ride into Phó Cáo, Đồng Văn district: corn terraces and hamlets used on quieter loops. Confirm which pin your driver means; “Phó” names cluster.
hook: Phó Cáo commune — Hmong slopes, thinner tourism than Sủng Là.
cardSummary: Not Phó Bảng (the stone ancient town in Yên Minh). Not Lũng Cẩm. One optional hamlet. Ask before yard photos.
whyGo: An extra village only if Sủng Là already felt staged.

name: Pho Bang Ancient Town
keywords: Walk Phó Bảng: a compact Hmong / highland trading street of stone houses on the plateau road, often 20–30 minutes south of Đồng Văn.
about: Walk Phó Bảng: a compact Hmong / highland trading street of stone houses on the plateau road, often 20–30 minutes south of Đồng Văn. Less café polish, more lived-in walls.
hook: Phó Bảng’s stone street in Yên Minh — older fabric than Đồng Văn’s restored square.
cardSummary: Not Đồng Văn old quarter and not Phó Cáo village. Lũng Cẩm is the nearby cultural village — pair those two, not three towns. Confirm opening of any ticketed houses.
whyGo: The other “ancient town” — one, not both plus a pass in the same hour.

name: Lung Cam Cultural Village
keywords: Visit Lũng Cẩm as the inhabited cultural village beside Phó Bảng: hemp, courtyards, a quieter walk than Đồng Văn Sunday.
about: Visit Lũng Cẩm as the inhabited cultural village beside Phó Bảng: hemp, courtyards, a quieter walk than Đồng Văn Sunday.
hook: Lũng Cẩm — community-tourism Hmong lanes next to Phó Bảng.
cardSummary: Pair with Phó Bảng, not with Sủng Là / Pao the same morning. Not Phó Cáo. Not Lô Lô Chải. Small community fee possible.
whyGo: The village half of the Phó Bảng stop — one cluster.

name: Xuan Huong Lake Loop
keywords: Walk or cycle the lakeside path through gardens and café stretches.
about: Walk or cycle the lakeside path through gardens and café stretches.
hook: Cool highland air and a swan-boat lake in Da Lat’s center.
cardSummary: Loop Xuan Huong Lake on foot or by bike through Da Lat’s cool highland center — gardens, cafés, and swan boats. A gentle first afternoon that sets the pace for Crazy House or Valley of Love.
whyGo: Orientation stroll for Da Lat’s pine-town charm.

name: Hang Nga Crazy House
keywords: Explore Hang Nga’s whimsical concrete sculptures, tunnels, and viewpoint rooms.
about: Explore Hang Nga’s whimsical concrete sculptures, tunnels, and viewpoint rooms.
hook: Surreal treehouse architecture you climb through like a dream.
cardSummary: Explore Hang Nga Crazy House — surreal concrete branches, tunnels, and lookout rooms that feel like a walk-in sculpture. Odd, memorable, and very Da Lat; allow time to climb slowly.
whyGo: Da Lat’s most unique attraction — pure playful design.

name: Valley of Love
keywords: Wander landscaped hills, rent a swan boat, and photograph flower displays.
about: Wander landscaped hills, rent a swan boat, and photograph flower displays.
hook: Flower gardens, lake boats, and hillside paths in Da Lat’s parkland.
cardSummary: Spend a mellow half-day in Valley of Love: flower gardens, hillside paths, and swan boats on the lake. Touristy but pleasant highland parkland that fits Da Lat’s romantic reputation.
whyGo: Classic Da Lat park day — gentle scenery and couple-friendly vibes.

name: Datanla Waterfall
keywords: Ride or walk down to Datanla’s falls in the pines south of town.
about: Ride or walk down to Datanla’s falls in the pines south of town.
hook: Pine forest, a roller coaster down the hill, and a cool highland cascade.
cardSummary: A short hop from central Da Lat to Datanla: alpine coaster or forest steps, then a waterfall in cool air. Easy to pair with a lake loop or Crazy House the same day.
whyGo: Active Da Lat without needing a full canyoning day.

name: Da Lat Night Market
keywords: Wander Hoa Binh night market for snacks, souvenirs, and cool-air crowds.
about: Wander Hoa Binh night market for snacks, souvenirs, and cool-air crowds.
hook: Strawberries, grilled skewers, and jumper weather under market lights.
cardSummary: Da Lat’s night market is snacks, steam, and a fleece on your shoulders — grilled corn, bánh tráng nướng, and fruit. Walk it after a lake loop; buy nothing you have to carry south.
whyGo: The highland evening that is actually the plan.

name: Tuyền Lâm Lake
keywords: Walk or boat Tuyền Lâm, the large highland lake south of town, usually paired with the cable car and Trúc Lâm monastery.
about: Walk or boat Tuyền Lâm, the large highland lake south of town, usually paired with the cable car and Trúc Lâm monastery.
hook: The big pine reservoir below Trúc Lâm and Robin Hill.
cardSummary: Large reservoir south of the centre. Shore paths and boats are free-to-cheap; the Robin Hill cable car (~100,000đ return) drops you at Trúc Lâm above the water. Daylight visit. Pair with Clay Tunnel on the same southern road, not with another city-lake stroll.
whyGo: Da Lat’s widest water view — not another Xuân Hương loop.

name: Lake of Sighs (Hồ Than Thở)
keywords: Visit Hồ Than Thở, a quieter lake east of the centre named for a tragic folk story, with pine paths and a small island shrine.
about: Visit Hồ Than Thở, a quieter lake east of the centre named for a tragic folk story, with pine paths and a small island shrine.
hook: A pine-ringed lake with a sad legend and fewer swan boats.
cardSummary: Pine lake with a local love-and-loss legend, northeast of town. Typical park hours 07:00–17:00 and a small ticket. Boats and photo props cost extra. Do not confuse it with Tuyền Lâm (the big southern reservoir) or Valley of Love.
whyGo: Atmosphere without Xuân Hương’s traffic.

name: Da Lat Railway Station
keywords: Tour the 1938 ga Đà Lạt, then optionally ride the slow train 7 km to Trại Mát for Linh Phước Pagoda.
about: Tour the 1938 ga Đà Lạt, then optionally ride the slow train 7 km to Trại Mát for Linh Phước Pagoda.
hook: Art Deco station with three peaked roofs — and a heritage train.
cardSummary: Heritage station (1932–38) with three triangular roofs. Grounds and hall from about 07:00; a viewing fee may apply. The Trại Mát tourist train is roughly 150,000đ return, 25–30 minutes each way, when a carriage fills. Pair the ride with Linh Phước and hydrangea farms.
whyGo: The best colonial interior in town if you like machines and light.

name: Da Lat Cathedral (Chicken Church)
keywords: Nicholas Cathedral on Trần Phú (1931–42): Romanesque brick, Grenoble stained glass, and the rooster weathervane that named it.
about: See St. Nicholas Cathedral on Trần Phú (1931–42): Romanesque brick, Grenoble stained glass, and the rooster weathervane that named it.
hook: The rooster on the 47-metre spire — Nhà thờ Con Gà.
cardSummary: Da Lat’s cathedral at 15–17 Trần Phú. Exterior anytime; interior mainly at mass (weekdays ~05:15 and 17:15). Free. Do not treat it as a museum. The Pink Church (Domaine de Marie) is a different hill compound 2 km away.
whyGo: The centre’s landmark church — free, and locked outside mass.

name: Domaine de Marie (Pink Church)
keywords: Walk the Domaine de Marie compound: 1940s pink church, gardens, and the convent that still sells handmade knitwear.
about: Walk the Domaine de Marie compound: 1940s pink church, gardens, and the convent that still sells handmade knitwear.
hook: Pink convent church on Mai Anh hill, with a wool shop run by sisters.
cardSummary: Pink church at 1 Ngô Quyền. Typically 07:30–11:30 and 13:30–17:30; free. Dress modestly. The sisters’ wool stall is the honest souvenir. Not the same building as Nhà thờ Con Gà downtown.
whyGo: Quieter and prettier than the Chicken Church for most photographs.

name: Linh Phước Pagoda
keywords: Visit Linh Phước in Trại Mát: a flamboyant pagoda famous for its bottle-mosaic dragon, floral ceramics, and tall tower.
about: Visit Linh Phước in Trại Mát: a flamboyant pagoda famous for its bottle-mosaic dragon, floral ceramics, and tall tower.
hook: The mosaic dragon built from a million glass bottles.
cardSummary: Glass-and-ceramic pagoda 8 km east in Trại Mát. Free, typically 07:00–17:00. Reach it by heritage train or road. Combine with hydrangea farms on the same lane. Cover shoulders; the dragon is for looking, not climbing.
whyGo: The most photogenic temple in the province — and the train’s reason to exist.

name: Trúc Lâm Zen Monastery
keywords: Visit Trúc Lâm on Phụng Hoàng / Robin Hill: meditation halls, gardens, and a view over Tuyền Lâm Lake.
about: Visit Trúc Lâm on Phụng Hoàng / Robin Hill: meditation halls, gardens, and a view over Tuyền Lâm Lake.
hook: A working Zen monastery above Tuyền Lâm’s pines.
cardSummary: Large Zen monastery, free, about 07:00–17:00. Most visitors arrive by Robin Hill cable car then walk down, or the reverse. Keep voices low; photography of monks needs consent. Pair with Tuyền Lâm, not with a second city pagoda crawl.
whyGo: The sacred half of the southern lake outing.

name: Linh Ẩn Pagoda
keywords: Stop at Linh Ẩn for the large outdoor Buddha, halls, and a quieter courtyard than Linh Phước’s mosaics.
about: Stop at Linh Ẩn for the large outdoor Buddha, halls, and a quieter courtyard than Linh Phước’s mosaics.
hook: A tall pale Buddha above the Prenn road.
cardSummary: Pagoda south of town near the Prenn pass road. Free, daylight hours. The standing Buddha is the landmark. Dress modestly. Easy to pair with Prenn Waterfall; do not confuse it with Linh Phước in Trại Mát.
whyGo: A calm pagoda on the way to Prenn or Tuyền Lâm.

name: Thiên Vương Cổ Sát (Chùa Tàu)
keywords: Visit Thiên Vương Cổ Sát, a Taiwanese-built monastery known locally as Chùa Tàu, for its three huge Buddha statues and pine setting.
about: Visit Thiên Vương Cổ Sát, a Taiwanese-built monastery known locally as Chùa Tàu, for its three huge Buddha statues and pine setting.
hook: The “Chinese pagoda” with three giant seated Buddhas.
cardSummary: Chinese-style monastery on a pine hill. Free, typically 07:00–17:00. The three seated Buddhas are the reason to go. Cover shoulders. A short ride from the station — not the same as Linh Phước or Trúc Lâm.
whyGo: Scale without Linh Phước’s bottle kitsch.

name: Bảo Đại Summer Palace I
keywords: Visit Dinh I, the earliest Bảo Đại palace on a high pine ridge, now a ticketed heritage house with the widest palace view.
about: Visit Dinh I, the earliest Bảo Đại palace on a high pine ridge, now a ticketed heritage house with the widest palace view.
hook: The hilltop first palace — views first, furniture second.
cardSummary: Palace I on a pine hill. Typically 07:00–17:30; adult ticket about 50,000đ. More about setting than royal clutter. Dinh II and Dinh III are different buildings — do not assume one ticket covers all three.
whyGo: If you only do one extra palace after Dinh III, make it this hill.

name: Bảo Đại Summer Palace II
keywords: See Dinh II at 12 Trần Hưng Đạo, built as the Indochina governor’s residence, later used by Bảo Đại, now often a provincial guesthouse.
about: See Dinh II at 12 Trần Hưng Đạo, built as the Indochina governor’s residence, later used by Bảo Đại, now often a provincial guesthouse.
hook: The governor’s house on Trần Hưng Đạo — when it is actually open.
cardSummary: Palace II on Trần Hưng Đạo (1933–37). Hours listed 07:00–17:30 and about 50,000đ when public; it is frequently closed as an official guesthouse. Check the door. Walk the French villa street even if the house is shut.
whyGo: Architecture on the villa street — only if the gate is open that day.

name: Bảo Đại Summer Palace III
keywords: Tour Dinh III on Triệu Việt Vương, Bảo Đại’s main Da Lat home (1933–38), preserved as a house museum.
about: Tour Dinh III on Triệu Việt Vương, Bảo Đại’s main Da Lat home (1933–38), preserved as a house museum.
hook: The palace everyone means — Art Deco interiors in Ái Ân pine forest.
cardSummary: The main summer palace, ~1,540 m elevation. Typically 07:00–17:30; adults about 40,000–50,000đ. Some listings close for lunch. Interiors, pine garden, and a small shop. This is not Dinh I or II — start here if you visit only one.
whyGo: The only palace that reliably shows how the last emperor actually lived here.

name: Lâm Viên Square
keywords: Lam Vien Square (Vietnamese: Quảng trường Lâm Viên) is the central square of the former city of Da Lat, Lâm Đồng Province. It has become one of Da Lat's most popular public spaces and a major venue for cultural and tourism events, including Dalat Flower Festival.
about: Use Lâm Viên Square as the city’s outdoor room: the lotus/artichoke sculptures, lake edge, and night-market approach.
hook: Artichoke towers and evening lights on Xuân Hương’s edge.
cardSummary: Lakeside square with the iconic artichoke towers. Free, anytime; liveliest after 17:00. Walk it with Xuân Hương and the night market. No ticket. The sculptures are civic art, not a theme park.
wikiAnchor: Lam Vien Square (Vietnamese: Quảng trường Lâm Viên) is the central square of the former city of Da Lat, Lâm Đồng Province. It has become one of Da Lat's most popular public spaces and a major venue for cultural and tourism events, including Dalat Flower Festival. Name In its early days, the square was named Đà Lạt Central Square (Quảng trường Trung tâm Đà Lạt) and it still used as an colloquial name. On November 10, 2011, the People's Council of Đà Lạt City approved its official name as Lâm Viên Square. The name recalls Đà Lạt's location on the Lâm Viên Plateau as well as the former Lâm Viên province before merged with Đồng Nai Thượng province to become Lâm Đồng province. Location Lam Vien Square is located on the southern side of Xuân Hương Lake, surrounded by Trần Quốc Toản Street. Architecture This landmark was constructed with an impressive budget of 681 billion VND (nearly 30 million USD) and has the capacity to hold around 60,000 people. Covering more than 70,000 m², the square includes open plazas, gardens, fountains, underground parking, and recreational areas.
whyGo: Free orientation — the photo people take before they know the city’s name.

name: Clay Tunnel (Dalat Sculpture Tunnel)
keywords: Walk the open-air sculpture trench near Tuyền Lâm: red-clay figures of Da Lat history, the Faces of Love, and a lakeside café at the end.
about: Walk the open-air sculpture trench near Tuyền Lâm: red-clay figures of Da Lat history, the Faces of Love, and a lakeside café at the end.
hook: A kilometre of unbaked-clay giants beside Tuyền Lâm.
cardSummary: 1.2 km sunken sculpture path (~13 km south), record-listed as Vietnam’s largest unbaked-clay work. Typical hours 07:00–17:00; expect a modest ticket. Open to the sky. Combine with Tuyền Lâm, not with another city sculpture house.
whyGo: Weird in a different way from Crazy House — and it is not an underground tunnel.

name: Elephant Falls (Thác Voi)
keywords: Descend to Thác Voi in Nam Ban: a powerful cascade often combined with Pongour on a southern loop.
about: Descend to Thác Voi in Nam Ban: a powerful cascade often combined with Pongour on a southern loop.
hook: The loudest waterfall near Da Lat — raw, not landscaped.
cardSummary: Powerful waterfall west/south of town. Listed tickets around 20,000đ; some access now via café/view platforms (~60,000đ) if the old stair gate is shut. Hours ~07:00–17:00. Steps are wet. Pair with Pongour, not with Datanla the same morning.
whyGo: If Datanla felt like a theme park, this is the corrective.

name: Pongour Waterfall
keywords: Walk down to Pongour, a broad multi-tier waterfall south of Da Lat, best as half of a countryside day with Elephant Falls.
about: Walk down to Pongour, a broad multi-tier waterfall south of Da Lat, best as half of a countryside day with Elephant Falls.
hook: A wide, layered fall on the road toward HCMC — the “seven-layer” one.
cardSummary: About 50 km south, open 07:00–17:00, ticket commonly 20,000đ plus parking. Not a city hop. Combine with Elephant Falls via Tà Nung rather than as a lone taxi trophy. Dry season thins the water; after rain it earns the trip.
whyGo: Width instead of height — the photogenic curtain after rain.

name: Prenn Waterfall
keywords: Visit Prenn just south of town: a landscaped cascade you can walk behind, five kilometres from the centre.
about: Visit Prenn just south of town: a landscaped cascade you can walk behind, five kilometres from the centre.
hook: The close-in fall on the pass road, with a walk behind the curtain.
cardSummary: Near Prenn Pass, ticket about 50,000đ, hours ~07:00–17:00. More park than wilderness. Pair with Linh Ẩn Pagoda. Skip if you already did Datanla the same morning — two small falls in one day dulls both.
whyGo: A waterfall when you do not want a 50 km ride.

name: Tiger Cave Waterfall
keywords: Walk Tiger Cave Waterfall for a compact cave-and-cascade stop, cheaper and quieter than Datanla’s coaster park.
about: Walk Tiger Cave Waterfall for a compact cave-and-cascade stop, cheaper and quieter than Datanla’s coaster park.
hook: Thác Hang Cọp — a cave and a fall on the same short trail.
cardSummary: Thác Hang Cọp, ticket often ~20,000đ, 07:00–17:00. Cave plus waterfall; shoes with grip. Not Dambri and not Datanla. Good on a motorbike loop toward Nam Ban.
whyGo: A small wild fall if the big names are booked with tour buses.

name: Cam Ly Waterfall
keywords: See Cam Ly Waterfall on the city edge: closest cascade to the centre, with a park setting and a modest ticket.
about: See Cam Ly Waterfall on the city edge: closest cascade to the centre, with a park setting and a modest ticket.
hook: The in-town fall — convenient, and often the weakest water.
cardSummary: Urban-edge waterfall, ticket around 40,000đ, ~07:00–17:00. Flow is often thin in the dry season. Fine as a 45-minute add-on, not a half-day. Cam Ly Church next door is a bonus façade, not this card.
whyGo: Only if you cannot leave town; otherwise pick Prenn or Elephant.

name: Dambri Waterfall
keywords: Day-trip to Dambri in Bảo Lộc: a high cascade with an elevator option, 50-plus kilometres from Da Lat.
about: Day-trip to Dambri in Bảo Lộc: a high cascade with an elevator option, 50-plus kilometres from Da Lat.
hook: Bảo Lộc’s big fall — elevator, rain-forest spray, a real day trip.
cardSummary: Lam Dong’s largest developed fall, ticket commonly ~200,000đ (includes elevator). Hours ~07:00–17:00. This is Bảo Lộc, not a Da Lat suburb — plan a half or full day. Do not stack with Pongour unless you enjoy six hours of road.
whyGo: The only waterfall on this list that needs its own morning.

name: Langbiang Mountain & Peak
keywords: Climb or jeep Langbiang for plateau views, pine ridgelines, and the mountain that names the highlands in local memory.
