about: Climb or jeep Langbiang for plateau views, pine ridgelines, and the mountain that names the highlands in local memory.
hook: The sacred K’Ho peak above Lát village — jeep or hike.
cardSummary: Peak north of town. Gate about 50,000đ; jeep to the summit is extra and the usual choice. Hours ~07:00–17:00. Cold and sudden fog. Combine with Chicken Village (Đồng K’Ho) at the foot, not with a second peak.
whyGo: Altitude and wind after too many flower parks.

name: Da Lat Flower Gardens
keywords: Walk Vườn Hoa Đà Lạt for seasonal beds, greenhouses, and a short lakeside garden that is not a working village.
about: Walk Vườn Hoa Đà Lạt for seasonal beds, greenhouses, and a short lakeside garden that is not a working village.
hook: The municipal flower park on Xuân Hương’s north shore.
cardSummary: City flower garden by the lake. Ticket often 50,000–100,000đ; hours ~07:00–17:00. Displays change with the season. This is not Vạn Thành or Fresh Garden — those are village/photo farms west of town.
whyGo: Flowers without driving to Thái Phiên.

name: Vạn Thành Flower Village
keywords: Wander Vạn Thành’s flower lanes and plastic-house rows, the production village behind Da Lat’s market bunches.
about: Wander Vạn Thành’s flower lanes and plastic-house rows, the production village behind Da Lat’s market bunches.
hook: Working greenhouses on the west side — roses you can smell.
cardSummary: Flower-growing village west of the centre. Many yards are free to peek; some charge for posed photos. Daylight. Pair with Fresh Garden or Fairytale Land on the same road. Ask before stepping into a bed.
whyGo: Real horticulture, not a ticketed ornamental park.

name: Thái Phiên Flower Village
keywords: Ride out to Thái Phiên for broader flower fields and family farms, a counterpart to Vạn Thành’s tighter lanes.
about: Ride out to Thái Phiên for broader flower fields and family farms, a counterpart to Vạn Thành’s tighter lanes.
hook: The other growing village — wider fields toward Trại Mát.
cardSummary: Flower village on the Trại Mát / east side. Informal, daylight, some paid photo gardens. Combine with the railway or Linh Phước. Do not book both Vạn Thành and Thái Phiên unless you really like greenhouses.
whyGo: Space and fewer photo-stall operators.

name: Cầu Đất Tea Hill
keywords: Visit Cầu Đất’s historic tea plantation for contour rows, a hill café, and the coolest air on a clear day.
about: Visit Cầu Đất’s historic tea plantation for contour rows, a hill café, and the coolest air on a clear day.
hook: Old French tea slopes and a café in the wind.
cardSummary: Tea estate southeast of town. Plantation walking is typically free; drinks and viewpoint decks are the spend. Daylight; fog is common. About 20–25 km — a dedicated outing, not a 30-minute add-on.
whyGo: The highland landscape that is not flowers or a waterfall.

name: Da Lat Market
keywords: Shop Chợ Đà Lạt in daylight for produce, jam, and cheap layers; this is the working hall, not the night-snack street.
about: Shop Chợ Đà Lạt in daylight for produce, jam, and cheap layers; this is the working hall, not the night-snack street.
hook: Daytime chợ — artichokes, strawberries, and wet floors.
cardSummary: Central covered market, roughly 05:00–18:00. Free to enter. Morning is produce; afternoon is souvenirs. The night market is a separate evening card already on this list — do not add both for the same hour.
whyGo: The market that feeds the city, before the fairy lights.

name: Da Lat Fairytale Land
keywords: Walk Fairytale Land’s miniature village, seasonal flowers, and optional wine cellar on the west-side photo-farm strip.
about: Walk Fairytale Land’s miniature village, seasonal flowers, and optional wine cellar on the west-side photo-farm strip.
hook: Tiny storybook houses on the Vạn Thành road.
cardSummary: Theme-garden in Vạn Thành. Listings often 07:30–17:00 and about 90,000đ adult — confirm at the gate. 60–90 minutes. Next to Fresh Garden and flower lanes. Not Valley of Love and not Crazy House.
whyGo: A short, staged park — fine with kids, skippable if you dislike props.

name: Lumiere Light Garden
keywords: Walk Lumiere’s illuminated garden paths and installations after sunset, a ticketed evening attraction.
about: Walk Lumiere’s illuminated garden paths and installations after sunset, a ticketed evening attraction.
hook: After-dark flower lights — a night garden, not a farm.
cardSummary: Light garden open in the evening (typically ~17:00–21:00; confirm). Ticketed photo park. Bring a jacket. This is not Fresh Garden or the municipal flower park — those close in daylight.
whyGo: When the night market is enough food and you still want a walk.

name: Hydrangea Flower Farm (Trại Mát)
keywords: Photograph hydrangea (cẩm tú cầu) farms around Trại Mát, a cluster of paid photo gardens rather than one official park.
about: Photograph hydrangea (cẩm tú cầu) farms around Trại Mát, a cluster of paid photo gardens rather than one official park.
hook: Cẩm tú cầu fields at the end of the heritage train.
cardSummary: Seasonal hydrangea farms at Trại Mát. Each yard sets its own fee and hours (daylight). Peak colour is roughly late year into spring. Combine with Linh Phước and the train. Stay on paths; these are working beds.
whyGo: The flower people actually come to Da Lat to stand in.

name: Fresh Garden Dalat
keywords: Tour Fresh Garden’s landscaped beds and photo corners, a ticketed garden next to Vạn Thành village and Fairytale Land.
about: Tour Fresh Garden’s landscaped beds and photo corners, a ticketed garden next to Vạn Thành village and Fairytale Land.
hook: A designed flower park on the Vạn Thành strip.
cardSummary: West-side flower park. Daylight hours and a modest ticket (confirm). 60–90 minutes. Same neighbourhood as Vạn Thành and Fairytale Land — pick one or two, not all three. Not the municipal Vườn Hoa by the lake.
whyGo: Neater than the working greenhouses, less theme-park than Fairytale Land.

name: Cu Lần Village
keywords: Visit Cu Lần’s wooden-house resort village: stream, gardens, and staged highland atmosphere north of town.
typical hours 08:00 – 18:00 typical for day visits
about: Visit Cu Lần’s wooden-house resort village: stream, gardens, and staged highland atmosphere north of town.
hook: A rustic lodge-village in the pines toward Lát.
cardSummary: Eco-village / lodge cluster in the northern pine belt. Day visitors usually pay a gate or F&B minimum; overnight is the fuller use. Not an ethnic museum. Pair with Langbiang or Chicken Village, not with Vạn Thành flower streets.
whyGo: A countryside hour if you are already heading to Langbiang.

name: Chicken Village (Đồng K’Ho)
keywords: Stop in Đồng K’Ho / Chicken Village for a K’Ho settlement, weaving stalls, and the oversized chicken sculpture that named it for tourists.
about: Stop in Đồng K’Ho / Chicken Village for a K’Ho settlement, weaving stalls, and the oversized chicken sculpture that named it for tourists.
hook: K’Ho community at the foot of Langbiang — and a giant rooster statue.
cardSummary: K’Ho village near Langbiang. Informal; some homes sell textiles. The rooster statue is a photo stop, not the culture. Ask before photographing people. Combine with the mountain. This is not Cu Lần (a lodge village).
whyGo: The cultural footnote on a Langbiang morning — go respectfully or skip.

name: Mongo Land Dalat
keywords: Stop at Mongo Land for the long colourful slide, viewpoints, and a brief family park on the road toward Elephant Falls.
about: Stop at Mongo Land for the long colourful slide, viewpoints, and a brief family park on the road toward Elephant Falls.
hook: Rainbow hillside slide on the Tà Nung pass.
cardSummary: Hillside activity park on Tà Nung. Daylight; slide and zone tickets extra. Good as a pause on an Elephant / Pongour loop. Skip if you dislike staged rainbow sets.
whyGo: A 45-minute laugh between waterfalls — not a destination by itself.

name: French Quarter Villa Complex
keywords: Walk the hill-station villa quarter: French houses, steep lanes, and the fabric that still makes Da Lat feel like a resort town.
about: Walk the hill-station villa quarter: French houses, steep lanes, and the fabric that still makes Da Lat feel like a resort town.
hook: Pine streets of colonial villas around Trần Hưng Đạo.
cardSummary: Villa district around Trần Hưng Đạo, Dinh II, and the older hotels. Free, anytime; best in late afternoon light. Many houses are private or official — photograph from the street. Pair with Palace II if the gate is open.
whyGo: Free architecture — the city’s actual historic core.

name: 100 Roofs Bar (Maze Bar)
keywords: Navigate 100 Roofs (Ngàn Mái): a multi-level maze bar of tiny tiled roofs, corners, and a cocktail at the end.
about: Navigate 100 Roofs (Ngàn Mái): a multi-level maze bar of tiny tiled roofs, corners, and a cocktail at the end.
hook: A drink inside a tiled maze — Da Lat’s oddest bar.
cardSummary: Maze bar near the centre. Evening hours; expect a drink minimum or cover. Tight stairs, low roofs, not for claustrophobia or wheelchairs. Go after the night market. This is a bar, not a temple or a park.
whyGo: Nightlife that is actually a sight, not a beer street.
